                      Re-Calibration and Simulation of Process Signal
                      The loop test readjustment and re-calibration of field instruments shall be
                      done in the same operation, and after the instrument has been checked
                      for complete process, pneumatic and electrical hook-up.

                      Performance of re-calibration:
                      In general the manufacturer's installation and maintenance manual for
                      calibration and testing shall always be adhered to. The following is only a
                      general advice for calibration.

                      Simulation of process condition

                      • Pressure:
                        Be sure that there are no leaks between the calibration equipment and
                        the calibration object. Check 0% -50% and 100% of range by applying
                        pressure. If range is below 10 bar, air should be used as test medium.
                        For higher pressures, liquid should be used (however take care that
                        the used liquid is compatible with instrument design, original process
                        fluid and process conditions).
                      • Temperature (filled system):
                        Check immersion depth. If no immersion depth is specified, the mini-
                        mum requirement is that the complete sensing element is submerged
                        in the bath. The temperature should be raised against the set point with
                        suitable steps / velocity. Be careful not to exceed the set point tempe-
                        rature with more than 5 centigrade.
                      • Level (float or displacer):
                        The level switch shall be calibrated before installation. Activate the le-
                        vel switch manually during loop test, and a full check shall be done du-
                        ring commissioning.

                      Note:       Only a short circuit of the loop is not sufficient.


                      Equipment for Re-Calibration and Loop Test
                      All equipment for calibration and loop test should be portable and have
                      sufficient accuracy to maintain a satisfactory total accuracy of loops.

1.9.4.5    Function Testing of Rotating Equipment
                      New rotating equipment are subject to a function test in order to check the
                      mechanical performance and to find out possible damages before start-
                      up of the plant. Comment and information from manufacturer are neces-
                      sary. For details please refer to the vendor documentation of pumps.

                      The following general instructions should be followed:

                      • Check of lubrication oil sealing liquid
                      • If necessary cooling water or seal flushing water supply has to be as-
                        sured
                      • The pump must be turned manually and checked for easy operation of
                        rotating parts.
                      • Thereafter it must be filled with operating liquid and vented.



1.9.4.5.1 Centrifugal Pumps
                      Shaft Pumps

                      • During start-up of centrifugal pumps, the valve in the suction line must
                        be completely opened.
                      • The valve on the discharge side must be kept slightly open (not fully
                        closed).
                      • Then it is slowly opened, after the pump has reached its nominal
                        speed.
                      • In case of gate valves with a bypass, the bypass must be opened at
                        first.
                      • During test-run, the suction lines are to be provided with fine gauze
                        screens (start-up strainer).

                                                         Doc. ID-Code                          Rev.
Copyright 2005 Uhde GmbH
                                                   8408205-CB-PR-MNL-0102                       02

                      • After the pump has been running for some hours or when there is a
                        loss of suction, the pump is shut down, so that the screen (start-up
                        strainer) can be removed, checked and cleaned.
                      • Thereafter the screen is re-installed, the pump started up again and
                        the same procedure repeated until the screen remains clean.
                      • Then the start-up screen is removed.
                      • The test-run of centrifugal pumps should last at least 24 hours.
                      • The test-run of stand-by pumps is done alternately with the pertaining
                        pump.
                      • Before the motor is switched off, the valve in the discharge line must
                        be closed.

1.9.5      COMMISSIONING, SPECIAL INSTRUCTIONS (C/A PLANT)
                      It is highly recommended to commission and start-up one train after the
                      other. Please refer to commissioning schedule, chapter 1.9.4.1.

                      For „Initial Start-up“ please refer to the corresponding chapter of each
                      unit.

1.9.5.1    General Prerequisites
                      a.) Utilities

                      Check and confirm the availability and quality of the following utilities:

                      • Cooling water (WS)
                      • Demineralised water (WDS)
                      • Chilled water (WCOS)
                      • Nitrogen (NL)
                      • Instrument air (AII)
                      • Steam (STL)
                      • Steam (STH)
                      • Raw / service water (WP)
                      For commissioning a large amount of water will be needed to fill tanks,
                      operate pumps and check interlocks. The water source to be used must
                      be determined, e. g. raw water (WP) and its suitability to be confirmed.

                      b.) Chemicals

                      For commissioning and start-up the following chemicals will be required:

                      • Laboratory chemicals (see analytical manual)
                      • Chemicals for initial filling:
                             • Caustic soda NaOH 32% or NaOH 50% (dilute to 18%-32% at site)
                             • Sulphuric acid (H2SO4 98%) (Note: commissioning of the chlorine
                               drying section will be performed with sulphuric acid only).
                             • Hydrochloric acid (HCl 32%, min. HCl 15%)
                             • Washed Salt (NaCl)
                             • Sodium carbonate (Na2CO3 solid in "50 kg bags“)
                             • Flocculent
                             • Alpha cellulose
                             • Sodium bisulphite (Na2S2O5 solid in "big bags")
                             • Anti-foaming agent

                      c.) Miscellaneous

                      For commissioning and start the following miscellaneous items will be re-
                      quired:

                             • Lubricants for machinery, pumps etc.
                             • Transformer oil
                             • Lube oil for the chlorine compressors
                             • Spare parts (mechanical seals, rupture disks....)
                             • Laboratory equipment for testing and sample taking
                             • Make sure that special tools are available
                             • Temporary blinds with and without chemical resistant layer (by

                      Arvand to make sure that drainage pit (outside Battery Limits OSBL) has

                      ceiver area is closed.

                      Filling of lean brine transfer line
                      • The line is vented at saturation area by opening manual 12" brine drain
                        valve at scraper receiver area.
                      • Line will be filled by means of scraper to remove air from line while fill-
                        ing. For operation of scraper please refer to document “Scraper oper-
                        ation procedure“ Doc. ID: 8408205-CB-PI-VDP-0300-107.
                      • Scraper in lean brine transfer line is started from scraper launching
                        area at buffer tanks, accelerated by means of lean brine transfer pump:

                          – Two of three lean brine transfer pumps 41P-02002A-C are started
                            in manual mode, PIC 0100101 is set on manual with set point 0 bar.

                          – Adjust flow rate of lean brine at 41FI0200301 to approx. 510 m3/h
                            by adjusting frequency of lean brine transfer pumps in manual
                            mode. This flow rate corresponds to 0,5 m/s flow speed which is op-
                            timal for scraper operation.

                      • After receiving the scraper at saturation area, lean brine transfer line is
                        filled. Open 2" manual bypass valve around 20" manual valve in lean
                        brine line from scraper to saturation pits. Open control valves
                        41FV0100110/20 to saturation pits 41R-01001A/B in manual mode to
                        approx. 30%.
                      • When water reaches the saturation pits, PIC 0100101 is set on auto
                        mode with set point 1 bar g.
                      • When saturation pits including pump suction chamber are filled
                        41FV0100110/20 will be set on auto mode and lean brine transfer
                        pump will be stopped.
                      • Lean and raw brine buffer tanks have to be refilled during and after this
                        operation.

                      Filling of raw brine transfer line

                      Raw brine transfer line is filled by means of scraper in the same direction
                      like lean brine transfer line from complex area to saturation area. Ensure
                      filled raw and lean brine buffer tanks.

                      • Close manual 20" isolating valve from lean brine line to lean brine
                        transfer line at scraper launcher, close 41XV0200101 and appropriate
                        2" bypass valve, open manual 12" isolating valve between lean and
                        raw brine line.
                      • Close manual 20" isolating valve between raw brine transfer pump and
                        raw brine transfer line at scraper receiving area.
                      • Vent raw brine transfer line at scraper receiver area by opening man-
                        ual 12" isolating valve to brine drain line; open brine drain valve.
                      • Fill raw brine transfer line like lean brine transfer line as described
                        above.
                      • After receiving scraper, stop lean brine transfer pumps 41P-02002A-C.
                      • At scraper launching area operate the following valves:

                          – close manual 12" isolating valve between lean and raw brine line,

                          – open 2" bypass valve at 41XV0200101 to vent raw brine transfer
                            line to raw brine buffer tank,

                          – open manual 20" isolating valve from lean brine line to lean brine
                            transfer line.

                      • At scraper receiving station operate the following valves:

                          – Open manual 20" isolating valve between raw brine transfer pump
                            and raw brine transfer line

                          – Close manual 12" isolating valve from raw brine line to brine drain
                            line

                          – Close brine drain valve.

                        quency will slowly be increased to 1200 rpm (80%).

                        cates flow, isolating valve 41XV0200101 will be opened.
                      • If level in hydraulic connected lean- and raw brine buffer tank decreas-
                        es under 30% refill with raw/demin water.

                      • Nitrogen system in operation.

                      Commission Vacuum Pump Unit / Lean Brine System

                      The vacuum pump unit is the heart of the anolyte dechlorination system.
                      It creates the vacuum, which is pulling the lean brine from the anolyte tank
                      up into the dechlorination tank, where chlorine gas is desorbed, and the
                      lean brine is pumped away to the lean brine buffer tank. The desorbed
                      chlorine gas is fed to the first chlorine gas cooler.

                      The Vacuum Pump Unit is a Package Unit supplied by FRIATEC, Rhein-
                      hütte. For additional information please refer also to vendor documenta-
                      tion of Requisition 8408205-CB-RE-REQ-0007.

1.9.5.2.5 Catholyte System
                      PFD 08101 (08201)

                      The catholyte system consists of two trains each with the following major
                      process equipment:

                      Note:       Equipment numbers for train 2 are in brackets.

                      • Catholyte Cooler 41E-31102 (31202)

                      The following major equipment is common to both trains:

                      • NaOH intermediate storage tanks 41TK-32001A/B
                      • NaOH transfer pump 41P-32007

                      Prerequisites:

                      For commissioning of the catholyte system the following utilities should
                      be available:

                      • Cooling water
                      • Instrument air
                      • Nitrogen
                      • Demineralised water
                      • Low pressure steam.

                      Procedure:

                      1. Start demineralised water flow to pump seals of pumps

                         battery limits and to electrolysers

                      4. Start cooling water flow to catholyte cooler 41E-31102 (31202)
                      5. Put 41TIC3110102 (41TIC3120102) in AUTO. Change set points.
                      6. Start the catholyte pump and fill the catholyte head tank, till the
                         catholyte head tank overflows back to the catholyte tanks.
                      7. Check that circulation is established and observe local instrumenta-
                         tion and monitor instrumentation.
                      8. When circulation stable put LC of catholyte tanks in AUTO, close all
                         valves to the electrolysers and open bypass to electrolysers so that
                         circulation is established: catholyte tanks - catholyte pumps -
                         catholyte heat exchangers (cooler) - electrolyser feed header - elec-
                         trolyser discharge header - hydrogen separator - catholyte tank.
                      9. Switch over flow from catholyte cooler to catholyte heater and
                         change set points of 41TIC3110102 (41TIC3120102).
                      10. When flow is stable through heater, open steam valve slowly and
                          start heating the water. Check steam trap and condenser discharge.
                      11. Put 41TIC3110201 (41TIC3120201) in AUTO (use lower set point
                          than for start-up). Change set-points after several hours.
                      12. Open nitrogen valves to hydrogen separator, purge for a few min-
                          utes, check 41FIS3110101 and shut-off nitrogen.
                      13. Stop steam flow.
                      14. After several hours of circulation open valve to the intermediate
                          caustic soda storage tanks. Add demin water the catholyte cycle by
                          using 41FV3110104 (3120104).
                      15. Feed water until interlock low level of catholyte tanks switches off
                          catholyte pumps.
                      16. Drain catholyte system completely.
                      17. Check catholyte tanks, catholyte head tank and hydrogen separator
                          for silica (sand). Remove sediments from vessels.

                      Leak Test

                      After commissioning of Chlorine Cooling and Drying continue as follows:

                      • Close all air vents to Chlorine System.
                      • Check for closed isolation valves of electrolysers.
                      • Close chlorine A valve to compressor and B valve to waste gas unit.
                      • Pressurise the chlorine system with plant air or nitrogen (temporary
                        connection) to 200 mbar g.
                      • Monitor pressure for 12 hours.
                      • Check for leakages if pressure decreases more than 10 mbar in
                        12 hours. (Consider volume changes due to temperature variation.)

1.9.5.2.7 Chlorine Compression
                      PFD 22101 (22201)

                      The chlorine compression system consists of 2 trains, each with the fol-
                      lowing major process equipment:

                      • Three stage chlorine compressor with dry gas seal system (DGS).
                      • Two intercoolers.
                      • One after cooler.
                      • Tube oil system with tank, pump, coolers and filters.
                      • Cooling water circuit.
                      The chlorine compression unit is a integrated Package Unit supplied by
                      MAN Turbo AG. For commissioning instructions please refer to vendor
                      documentation of Requisition 8408205-CB-RE-REQ-0006 in details.

                      It is recommended to carry out final commissioning steps as well as initial
                      start-up under supervision of vendor specialist.



                      Prerequisites:

                             • That compressor and connecting pipework are clean free from wa-

1.9.5.2.8 Hydrogen System
                      PFD 34101 (34201)

                      The hydrogen treatment system consists of two trains, each with the fol-
                      lowing major process equipment:

                      Note:       Equipment numbers for train 2 are in brackets.

                      • 41E-34101 (34201)           Hydrogen Cooler
                      • 41FT34102 (34202)           Hydrogen Filter with Internals
                      • 41X-34101 (34201)           Hydrogen Stack
                      The following equipment is common to both trains:

                      • 41V-34001                   Condensate Tank
                      • 41P-34001 A, B, C           Condensate Pumps


                      Prior to commissioning of the hydrogen section, the following perquisites
                      must be fulfilled, and following systems should be ready for operation:

                      • Cooling water circulation
                      • Low pressure steam system
                      • Nitrogen system
                      • Demineralised water system.

                      Following must be considered:

                      • Hydrogen is a very light gas, and in case of leakage from equipment or
                        piping it will rest upwards.
                        As the gas is highly flammable no electric equipment and/or spark
                        causing tools such as cranes, shall be used above and directly around
                        equipment, which may leak.
                        No smoking, welding, grinding in hydrogen areas!
                      • In air the explosive limits for normal hydrogen are 4.2 and 74.2% v/v.
                      • Hydrogen has a high diffusion coefficient and dissipates quickly in air.
                      • Hydrogen is an asphyxiant.


                                                          Doc. ID-Code                          Rev.
Copyright 2005 Uhde GmbH
                                                    8408205-CB-PR-MNL-0102                       02
                                         PVC Arvand
                                       Operating Manual
                                                                       National Petrochemical comany
                 SAZE H
                 C O NSU LTANTS              C/A Plant                 Arvand Petrochemical
                                                                            Company
Uhde Project No: 03-3039           Sazeh Project No: 8047           Owner Project No: 8408205
Job Code:        PVC Arvand        Job Code:                        Owner Job Code: PVC Arvand
                                                                                      Page 182 of 967


                      • It is more dangerous if air is leaking into the hydrogen containing piping
                        and equipment, than the other way round, therefore avoid pulling vac-
                        uum in the hydrogen system.
                      • All hydrogen piping containing water vapour must be sloped, so that
                        condensate can freely be separated.


                      Procedure:

                      1. Start cooling water flow through hydrogen cooler.
                      2. Fill the condensate header completely with water, till overflow to the
                         condensate tank is visible in the sight glass.
                         Fill condensate tank and put 41LIC3410101 in AUTO.
                      3. Check if H2 valve A to EDC / VCM is closed and valve B to stack is
                         open.
                         Also isolation valves at electrolysers to be closed.
                      4. Start nitrogen or air flow to the hydrogen stack, to the condensate
                         tank and to the hydrogen header. Use temporary hose connection if
                         required.
                      5. Continue water flow to tank.
                      6. Start pump 41P-34001 A, B or C and pump water to lean brine
                         header.
                      7. During testing of hydrogen system all gases are vented through the
                         stack.
                      8. Check local instrumentation and monitor system from the FCS.
                      9. Check steam flow by opening 41HV3410101 (3410201) slowly, for a
                         short period, to stack (for warning system and expound piping).
                      10. After several hours stop pumps and flow of nitrogen.

                      Leak Test

                      After Commissioning of Hydrogen System continue as follows:

                      • Close all air vents to Hydrogen System.
                      • Check for closed isolation valves of electrolysers.
                      • Close A valve to EDC / VCM and B valve to stack.

1.9.5.2.9 Caustic Evaporation Unit
          PFD 32001
                      The Caustic Evaporation Unit is a single train package unit, consisting of:


                      • 3 falling film evaporators
                      • Steam condensate tank
                      • Vapour condensate tank
                      • Steam ejector group
                      • Heat exchangers / coolers
                      • Surface condenser
                      • Pumps.


                      The NaOH 32% produced in the electrolysers will be evaporated up to
                      50% by use of steam.

                      The NaOH 50% as a final product of the C/A Plant will be stored in the
                      NaOH 50% storage tanks. Intermediate storage tanks for NaOH 32% are
                      provided as a buffer between catholyte system of the two trains and the
                      evaporation unit. Being in normal operation the caustic of the catholyte
                      system is directly pumped into the evaporation unit until the intermediate
                      storage tanks are in bypass.

                      Caustic Evaporation

                      The unit is a integrated Package Unit supplied by Bertrams Chemical
                      Plants LTD. For commissioning instructions please refer to vendor docu-
                      mentation of Requisition 8408205-CB-PU-REQ-0006 in details.

                      It is recommended to carry out final commissioning steps as well as initial
                      start-up under supervision of vendor specialist.

1.9.5.2.11 Bleaching Lye Production
                      PFD 27001

                      The bleaching lye production system is common to both trains of the chlo-
                      rine plant, and it consists of the following major process equipment:

                      • 41V-27001                   Bleach Lye Product Tank
                      • 41P-27002 A/B               Bleaching Lye Circulation Pump
                      • 41E-27001                   Bleaching Lye Cooler
                      • 41J-27001                   Bleaching Lye Ejector
                      • 41TK27002                   Bleaching Lye Storage Tank
                      • 41P-27003 A/B               Bleaching Lye Filling Pump
                      • 41U-27050                   Filling Station for Bleaching Lye

                      Procedure:

                      Flush system around bleach lye production tank 41V-27001

                      1. Disconnect piping to bleach lye cooler 41E-27001.
                      2. Fill bleach lye production tank 41V-27001 with demineralised water
                         via temporary hose.
                      3. Start pump 41P-27002 A or B when level in the tank is at 50% and
                         circulate water back to tank via min. flow line.
                      4. Continue filling tank until overflow. Check alarms.
                      5. After 4 hours stop pump 41P-27002 A or B.

                      Flush system around bleaching lye storage tank 41TK27002

                      1. Fill bleaching lye storage tank 41TK27002 with water with temporary
                         hose.
                      2. Start bleach lye loading pump 41P-27003 A or B and circulate water.
                      3. Continue filling the tank, and check high level alarms.
                      4. Open valve to production tank and flush line from bleach lye storage
                         tank to bleach lye production tank.
                      5. Open valve to bleaching lye filling station and flush filling line.

1.9.5.2.14 HCl Synthesis
                      PFD 37001

                      The hydrochloric acid synthesis is a single train package unit, consisting
                      of:

                      • hydrochloric acid synthesis with burner, absorber and scrubber col-
                        umn, 41U-37050
                      • 2 storage tanks, 41TK38001 A/B
                      • 2 transfer pumps, 41P-38001 A/B.
                      The hydrochloric acid is produced as a 32 +/- 1% solution for internal use
                      within the chlorine plant, by burning hydrogen and chlorine gases, and
                      absorbing the resultant hydrochloric acid gas with demineralised water.

                      vendor documentation of Requisition 8408205-CB-ME-REQ-0007 in de-
                      tails.

                      It is recommended to carry out final commissioning steps as well as initial

                      Steam Reducing

                      High pressure steam form B.L. will be reduced to a pressure of 1,5 - 2 bar

                      • Interlocks are checked and active.

                      2. Slowly open 41PV9410502 in manual.
                      3. Slowly heat up downstream steam piping to avoid steam hammer-
                         ing.
                      4. Put 41PV9410502 in auto with set point 1,5 bar absolute.
                      5. Check draining of steam lines via steam traps. Open by-pass of
                         steam traps if required.

1.9.5.3    SPECIAL COMMISSIONING SUMMARY - FINAL START-UP PREPARATIONS
                      Before start up, after water batching, the C/A plant has to be prepared for
                      operation and be filled with chemicals.

                      The heart of the chlorine plant are the membrane electrolysers. As the
                      membranes and electrodes require high purity chemicals, the initial filling
                      and preparation should be carefully planned and executed. Sufficient
                      time should be available to complete analysis and observe parameters.

                      With regard to safety it is of utmost importance that the waste gas dechlo-
                      rination system is in good working order and reliable.

                      Some commissioning with chemicals can be carried out concurrently, but
                      generally the following instructions should be followed:

                      1. Make sure that seal water is fed to all pumps requiring seal water,
                         including vacuum pumps.
                      2. Make sure that cooling water is available to heat-exchangers requir-
                         ing cooling water.
                      3. Make sure that chilled water is available to heat-exchangers requir-
                         ing chilled water.

1.10       MAINTENANCE PHILOSOPHY (C/A PLANT)

1.10.1     INTRODUCTION
                      All technical equipment requires maintenance, some more some less.
                      Since the profit and the safety of modern industrial plants is to a large ex-
                      tent ruled by their reliable and trouble free operation, maintenance is a
                      very important factor and must be considered.

                      There are various maintenance strategies available and the choice of one
                      or other strategy is the result of the study in order to minimise costs (main-
                      tenance and operation) and to maintain the inherent safety and opera-
                      tional design properties.

                      The purpose of this manual is to give to the Owner of the Plant the main
                      guideline to follow, in order to reduce plant shutdown and optimise the
                      productivity.

                      Note:       This document shall only be used together with the manufac-
                                  turers instruction manuals.

                      It is also advisable to have a database of all maintenance activities per-
                      formed in the plant with relevant results and consideration; these informa-
                      tion shall be the base for future revision and updating of this manual to fit
                      the real performance of the plant according to the experience.

1.10.2     DEFINITION OF MAINTENANCE
                      Maintenance is defined as a combination of all technical and administra-
                      tive actions, including supervisory actions, intended to retain an item in,
                      or restore it to, a state in which it can perform a required function.

1.10.2.1   Definition of Preventive Maintenance
                      Preventive Maintenance may be either Schedule Based (fixed time) or
                      Condition Based / Predictive Maintenance.

                      Preventive maintenance has the scope to avoid any operational problems
                      of equipment by substitute all parts sub-checked to wear or damage prior
                      of this event.

1.10.2.1.1 Schedule Based (or Fixed Time) Maintenance and Routine Maintenance
                      Schedule based maintenance is the most expensive maintenance strate-
                      gy, if performed for all plant equipment involves the replacement of all
                      equipment parts subject to normal wear and tear, within regular, prede-
                      termined intervals.

                      This gives excellent results with respect to the availability of the plant and
                      eliminates all risks mentioned with the 'breakdown strategy'.

                      It is however too expensive since many parts, normally the majority, are
                      exchanged long before they have reached the end of their potential serv-
                      ice life.

1.10.2.1.2 Condition Based (or Predictive) Maintenance
                      This is a more recent maintenance philosophy which tries to schedule the
                      maintenance tasks as result of the real necessity.

                      This might require extensive installation of measuring devices and/or
                      control of equipment to be able to predict the necessity of maintenance
                      before the failure point is reached.

1.10.2.2   Definition of Maintenance on Failure
                      The simplest maintenance strategy, if it can be called a strategy, is to just
                      repair the equipment after it has failed i.e. 'is broken down'.

                      This required:

                      • a large and costly maintenance force
                      • a well equipped warehouse with spare parts.

                      Results in:

                      • shorter plant life due to unplanned and abrupt plant shut downs.
                      • loss of production
                      • late delivery which may influence the long-term relationship with the
                        customer
                      • loss of profit in all cases.

                                                                                     Page 204 of 967


                      Some plant operators incorrectly call their maintenance 'break down
                      maintenance', but actually carry out routine maintenance, consisting of
                      regular visual checks and general servicing as needed depending upon
                      the type of equipment, e.g. topping up or changing oil and grease.

1.10.2.3   Definition of Corrective and Modification Maintenance
                      This strategy is used when a component of an equipment, or the way how
                      it operates, fail.

                      Plant Engineering Department decide to modify the equipment by rede-
                      sign it completely or by operate it in a different way. It is recommended
                      the equipment vendor is involved in this job by giving its advise and ac-
                      ceptance.

1.10.3     MAINTENANCE STRATEGY
                      The explanations given above demonstrate that in these days of small
                      profit margins and high safety requirements the application of only one of
                      the methods will no longer satisfy previously mentioned requirements.

                      A modern maintenance strategy, however, has as one of its main fea-
                      tures the aim to have a considerable portion of the total maintenance
                      work performed on a planned and scheduled basis and to consequently
                      decrease the unforeseen and unexpected plant shut downs and to re-
                      duce the maintenance cost to a minimum.

                      Therefore a mixture of the methods given above will have to be applied
                      to achieve the best result with lowest maintenance costs.

                      Planned routine and condition based servicing and inspection will have,
                      without any question, to be applied to detect developing damages as ear-
                      ly as possible. The extent and ratio of these methods will however have
                      to be defined.

                      Such analyses to determine the correct mix of the different maintenance
                      measures are performed by an interdisciplinary team using the individual
                      technical know how and the practical experience from former start-up or
                      operation activities. During the analysis the necessity of equipment avail-
                      ability in regard to plant performance, safety and environmental require-
                      ments are analyzed, this means, less critical and less important or even
                      redundant equipment may not require the same amount of control than
                      one which is essential for the operation of the plant.

                      This will result in the definition of the type of maintenance to be applied to
                      the single equipment being either :

                      Schedule based maintenance

                      • routine maintenance will be applied for equipment classified as impor-
                        tant or non-critical
                      • preventive maintenance will in exceptional cases be applied only to
                        such equipment who's failure is highly critical for production or safety.
                      Condition based maintenance

                      • predictive servicing and inspection (predictive maintenance) based on
                        results of frequent monitoring.

                      This might be done by permanently installed equipment, like vibration
                      measurement at heavy machinery or with portable equipment on se-
                      quences defined by the behavior of the equipment.

                      The predicted resulting service life cycle as well as the date of the next
                      inspection will be analyzed and recommended by the specialized soft-
                      ware used with the monitoring equipment called maintenance by condi-
                      tion monitoring.



                      During the equipment guarantee period service intervals should not be
                      longer than requested by the Vendor/Manufacturer.

                      Later on periods might be defined as specified above e.g. for oil changes
                      for heavy machinery be determined in accordance with oil analyses.

                      Any maintenance strategy which disregards the human being who will
                      have to perform the services will not be successful.

                      Therefore service personnel must be trained from the very beginning for
                      their fields of service. Training should not only be limited to the technical
                      skill, but should also strengthen the sense of responsibility.

                      A further requirement for successful maintenance is to follow up mainte-
                      nance activities to ensure they are executed when due and that the re-
                      sults are fed back and are processed to get comparable figures. These
                      can then be used for improvement and adjustment of the maintenance
                      measures originally defined.

                      The follow up and evaluation of such an immense amount of data re-
                      ceived during maintenance performance manually is nearly impossible.
                      Therefore in our days modern maintenance software programs are indis-
                      pensable.

                      In the following UHDE will give some information regarding the mainte-
                      nance activities based on experience.

1.10.4     ROUTINE / PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE
                      An important requirement for visible success through routine/preventive
                      maintenance and inspection is a well thought out and practicable concept
                      according to which the individual measures are taken at regular intervals.

                      The aim of these measures, as far as maintenance is concerned, is to
                      keep the plant in a constant state of operability and, as far as inspection
                      is concerned, to detect imminent damage at an early stage so that serious
                      damage can be prevented by eliminating the former in good time.

                      The economic aims of routine/preventive maintenance and inspection
                      are:

                      • to restrict operational disturbances and, therefore, reduce production
                        losses,
                      • to attain a longer service life of machinery and equipment, and
                      • to reduce repair costs.
                      The following routine/preventive maintenance work and intervals are rec-
                      ommended to assure optimum plant operation and safety.



                       Description of work recommended                          Time interval

1.10.5     PREPARATION OF EQUIPMENT FOR MAINTENANCE WORK (GENERAL IN-
           STRUCTIONS)
                      Before commencing repair or maintenance work on an item of equipment,
                      all flammable and aggressive materials have to be removed from the
                      equipment.

                      After shut-down, the following operations have to be carried out:

                      • Drainage of liquids, gas or material
                      • Depressurization
                      • Flushing with nitrogen
                      • Flushing with demin water
                      • Purging with air
                      • Isolation
                      • Electrical Isolation.


1.10.5.1   Drainage
                      All vessels and items of equipment to be cleaned or inspected are dis-
                      charged as far as possible by means of installed pumps into other proc-
                      ess equipment (vessels, columns), into intermediate storage tanks or
                      waste water treatment unit.

1.10.5.2   Depressurisation
                      The gas pressure remaining in the equipment after drainage is released
                      either into atmosphere or - if chlorine and hydrogen chloride are present
                      - into the waste gas dechlorination unit.

1.10.5.3   Flushing with Nitrogen
                      Equipment containing flammable or aggressive gas have to be purged
                      with nitrogen.

                      After complete drainage and pressure release, the equipment concerned
                      is flushed with nitrogen supplied via permanently installed connections or
                      hose couplings, until all flammable or aggressive materials have been re-
                      moved.

1.10.5.4   Flushing with Demin Water
                      Equipment containing aggressive liquids or filling material have to be
                      purged with nitrogen.

                      After complete drainage and pressure release, the equipment concerned
                      is flushed with demin water supplied via permanently installed connec-
                      tions or hose couplings, until all aggressive materials have been re-
                      moved.

1.10.5.5   Purging with Air
                      After flushing with nitrogen, the equipment is purged with air until all nitro-
                      gen has been displaced by breathing air.

1.10.5.6   Isolation
                      Note:       Before any item of equipment is entered, spade plates/blinds
                                  in all incoming and outgoing lines have to be installed in order
                                  to prevent dangerous materials from getting in.

2.2        DESCRIPTION OF PROCESS

2.2.1      TECHNICAL PRINCIPALS
                      The brine saturation system is designed to produce saturated brine of
                      concentration 300 - 310 g/l NaCl from dechlorinated lean or depleted
                      brine having concentration of 220 - 230 g/l NaCl. The depleted brine is
                      pumped by means of the lean brine transfer pumps 41P-02002A-C from
                      the lean brine buffer tank to the saturation pits.

                      The three pits each have 50% capacity, and operate on a semi batch prin-
                      ciple - around the clock salt loading is not required.

                      From saturation pit area the saturated brine is pumped by means of raw
                      brine transfer pumps 41P-01001A-C to raw brine buffer tank.

                      From this tank raw brine is pumped with raw brine pumps 41P-02001A-C
                      through raw brine recuperators 41E-02102 (41E02202) where heat is re-
                      covered from lean brine to raw brine.

                      From brine recuperators raw brine is routed through raw brine heaters

                      precipitation unit 031 (032).
                      Each of the raw brine recuperators and heaters is related to one of the
                      downstream production trains.


2.2.2      UNIT DESCRIPTION

2.2.2.1    Brine Saturation (Unit 010)
                      The saturation area is located approx. 22 km away from the complex ar-
                      ea. The areas are connected with two parallel layed underground pipes
                      of diameter 24“. Lean (depleted) brine and raw (saturated) brine is trans-
                      ported by means of lean brine transfer pumps 41P02001A-C located in
                      the complex area and raw brine transfer pumps 41P01001A-C located in
                      the saturation area.

                      The brine saturation system consists of three brine saturation pits 41R-
                      01001A-C. Two of the saturation pits are in operation. Each pit is de-
                      signed for 50% capacity.
                      The dechlorinated lean brine from the lean brine transfer pumps 41P-
                      02002A-C is split in two streams which are routed via control valves
                      41FV0100110/20 in two saturation pits while the third is in stand-by (pit C
                      is common stand-by for pit A and B).

                      For good distribution of brine in the pit the lean brine is feed through 10
                      distribution pipes located at the bottom of the pit and which are sub-
                      merged with salt. The saturation pit is filled with washed salt by means of
                      a belt conveyor or shovel loader (outside Battery Limits).

                      Approx. 85% of salt crystals have to be of grain size < 4 mm to ensure
                      proper dissolution rates.

                      Lean brine passes from bottom to the top of the salt bed while getting sat-
                      urated. Saturated brine over flows through an overflow wear into the
                      pump suction chamber.

                      In order to adjust the concentration in raw brine at 300 - 310 g/l, the con-
                      centration in the saturated raw brine is monitored and controlled by den-
                      sity controllers 41DIC0100110/20 in two brine control loops (in each on-

                      line pit the concentration is ensured and controlled separately; isolating
                      valves to be set accordingly.

                      In this loops brine is sucked out of pump suction chambers through den-
                      sity meter by means of sample jet 41J-01002A/B which is driven by raw
                      brine transfer pump 41P-01001A-C and flows back to saturation pit. If
                      density is to high the brine is diluted by lean brine bypassing the pits via
                      control valve 41DV0100110/20.
                      The adjustment depends on the level of salt in the brine saturation pit and
                      on the NaCl concentration in the lean brine stream, which is measured
                      with 41D0100101 in the main line to the saturation area.

                      Impurities such as silica present in the salt, remains un-dissolved in the
                      pit. These insoluble are to be removed periodically as dictated by the
                      quality of salt by draining the brine saturation pit into drainage pits
                      (OSBL).

                      The level in pump suction chamber of the on-line pits is controlled by
                      41LIC0100111/21/31 (to be selected acc. to on-line pits) which acts on
                      control valves 41FV0100110/20.

                      The stand by pit has to be filled with lean brine by opening the hand
                      valves behind control valve 41DV0100110 or 41DV0100120 or loose
                      connection. This protects the rubber lining and prevents the distribution
                      pipes from blocking with salt crystals.
                      If stand by pit is taken in operation, lean brine flow, bypass flow and den-
                      sity control loop to sample jet has to be set accordingly by means of hand
                      valves behind control valves 41FV0100110/20 and 41DV0100110/20 to
                      the stand by pit. Also 41LIC0100131 has to be switched by selector
                      switch 41HS0100131 to either valve 41FV0100110 or 41FV0100120 de-
                      pending on which pit is taken out of operation (pit C in operation for pit A
                      or pit C in operation for pit B).

2.2.2.2    Raw and Lean Brine Treatment (Unit 021 / 022)
                      Lean brine is feed from lean brine pump 41P-07101 (41P-07201) through
                      parallel piped raw brine recuperators 41E-02102 (41E-02202) to lean
                      brine buffer tank 41TK02002.
                      To compensate the water balance, vapour condensate from condensate
                      tank 41V-34001 and raw/demin water is added to lean brine.

                      Tie-in point for condensate (78 °C) is upstream whereas tie-in point of
                      raw/demin water (ambient temperature) is down stream of raw brine re-
                      cuperators. This allows the best heat recovery from lean brine to raw
                      brine in the raw brine recuperator 41E-02102 (41E-02202).

                      Raw water can only be used if it is within specification, especially it has to
                      be free of TOC. If Ca2+ and HCO -3 is present, CaCO3 will precipitate due
                      to alkaline conditions in lean brine and will be settled in lean brine buffer
                      tank 41TK02002. Upsets in the brine system can be avoided by adding
                      demin water instead of raw water.

                      During the period of commissioning brine purge of approx. 120 m3/h brine
                      is located upstream of raw brine recuperator.

                      For future operation a shift of brine purge to the salt saturation area is
                      foreseen. The water addition to brine system will not be shifted to satura-
                      tion area. So the brine purge has to be increased to purge the same total
                      amount of impurities at lower concentration of impurities caused by water
                      addition to lean brine up-stream of purge. This leads to an additional wa-
                      ter consumption of approx. 50 m3/h raw/demin water.

                      The additional flow of 170 m3/h, when brine purge is shifted towards the
                      saturation pits is considered in design of equipment downstream to satu-
                      ration area.

                      Lean brine is feed from lean brine buffer tank 41TK02002 (complex area)
                      with lean brine transfer pumps 41P-02002A-C through an approx. 22 km
                      long underground brine transfer line with diameter 24" to the saturation
                      pits 41R-01001A-C (saturation area). The lean brine transfer pumps (2 in
                      operation, 1 in stand by) are frequency controlled by 41PIC0100101
                      which is located near the saturation pits. The set-point for PIC at satura-
                      tion is 2 barg to provide enough pressure for further brine purge routing.

                      Raw Brine is pumped from saturation pits 41R-01001A-C with frequency
                      controlled raw brine transfer pumps 41P-01001A-C (2 in operation, 1 in
                      stand by) through underground raw brine transfer pipeline of approx. 22
                      km length to raw brine buffer tank 41TK02001. This tank has an overflow
                      to lean brine buffer tank 41TK02002 and is equipped with level control
                      41LIC0200101 which acts on the frequency of raw brine transfer pumps.

                      Both raw and lean brine buffer tanks are equipped with additional 16“iso-
                      lating valves at the bottom of the tanks. This enables to install a line con-
                      nection in case of commissioning.
                      The line allows to run either a brine circle in the complex area (brine treat-
                      ment - cell room bypass - anolyte system) or a brine circle from complex
                      to saturation area (lean brine buffer tank - saturation pits - raw brine buffer
                      tank) independent from each other, but not in parallel.

                      From raw brine buffer tank 41TK02001 the brine is pumped by means of
                      frequency controlled raw brine pumps 41P-02001A-C to precipitation
                      tanks 41R-03101A/B and 41R-03201A/B: Pump A to tanks of train 1 and
                      pump B to tanks of train 2 while pump C is common stand-by.

                      The pumps are controlled by 41LIC0410101 (41LIC0420101) (level of
                      clarified brine tank 41V-04101(41V-04201)). For temperature adjustment
                      raw brine passes the raw brine recuperator 41E-02102 (41E-02202)
                      where heat is recovered from hot lean brine to raw brine. Downstream of
                      recuperator an additional raw brine heater 41E-02101 (41E-02201) is in-
                      stalled for heating up raw brine to 60°C.

                      Raw brine is heated up with low pressure steam, which will be generated
                      in the steam reducing station 41X-94102 from high pressure steam.
                      Steam condensates are collected in steam condensate tank 41V-02001
                      and pumped via steam condensate pump 41P-02003A/B to condensate
                      return header of C/A Plant.

2.2.2.3    Lean- and Raw Brine Transfer Lines
                      The transfer lines of diameter 24“are equipped with scraper launchers at
                      complex area and scraper receiver at saturation area for cleaning, air free
                      filling and draining the pipelines.
                      To protect transfer pipelines from liquid hammer, closing time of all auto-
                      matic valves in brine loop (41FV0100110/20, 41DV0100110/20 and
                      41FV0100101 in lean brine line and 41XV0200101 in raw brine line) is re-
                      stricted to more than 60s.
                      If the last running transfer pump fails the pipelines will be blocked at the
                      other end by means of the above mentioned automatic valves by inter-
                      lock. The aim is to avoid underpressure conditions and running dry of
                      pipeline.

                      Also all manual isolating valves in raw and lean brine line have to be
                      closed within time ranges greater than 60s.

                      For leakage monitoring both ends of pipelines are equipped with temper-
                      ature, flow and pressure indicator.

                      Total flow of lean brine entering saturation area has to be calculated by
                      addition of flows to the two saturation pits in operation 41FIC0100110/20
                      and the flow of brine purge 41FIC0100101.

                      Lean brine transfer line entering and raw brine transfer line leaving the
                      saturation area are equipped with additional density meter (41DI0100101
                      and 41DI0100102) to enable the calculation of salt balance around salt
                      saturation.

2.2.3      PROCESS CHEMISTRY
                      The dechlorinated lean brine stream entering the saturation area has a
                      concentration of 150 - 160 g/l of NaCl. Hence in order to re-saturate the
                      brine stream and build up the concentration of saturated brine up to 300
                      - 310 g/l of NaCl, the lean brine temperature should be kept as high as
                      possible.

                      Brine saturated at higher temperatures which cools down may approach
                      the crystallisation point, resulting in solid salt formation see attached
                      chart/diagram:

                      “Solubility of NaCl in Water as Function of Temperature“

                      The pH value of lean brine to the saturator is to be kept in the range of
                      8.0 - 9.5. At higher pH (approx. 12) silica present the salt tends to dissolve
                      in brine. Lower pH (approx. 6) may result in increased pick-up of polyva-
                      lent ions such as aluminium.

2.5        PART 5: PREPARATION FOR INITIAL START-UP

2.5.1      PRE-COMMISSIONING AND COMMISSIONING
                      Please refer to chapter 1.9 of Operating Manual C/A Plant, Pre-commis-
                      sioning and commissioning instructions.

                      Following prerequisites are to be ensured before start up of brine system.

                      • Lean and raw brine tank are connected with commissioning pipeline
                        and filled up to 30% with demin/ raw water.

                      • Raw and lean brine transfer pipelines are filled with demin/ raw water.

                      Establish brine loop: raw brine buffer tank- precipitation - clarification - fil-
                      tration - ion exchange - cell header bypass - anolyte system - lean brine
                      buffer tank.

                      • Take brine loop in operation and heat up to 60°C by means of raw brine
                        heater 41E-02101 (41E-02201) and brine heater 41E-06101 (41E-
                        06201).

                      • If only one train is taken is operation, both raw brine heaters can be
                        used to heat up one train. In this case manual isolating valve behind
                        heater of train, which is not in operation, has to be closed. Additionally,
                        manual isolation valve in connecting line has to be opened.

                      • Close commissioning pipeline between buffer tank and check that
                        complete brine loop including transfer pipelines and saturation pits is
                        ready to take in operation.

                      Following prerequisites are to be ensured before saturation of lean brine:

                      • Bypass line between raw brine and lean brine buffer tank is removed.

2.6.3      INITIAL START UP
                      • Start charging salt into the saturation pit on 41R-01001A-C, whichever
                        pit is in operation with shovel loaders/belt conveyor (OSBL).

                      • Don’t charge to much salt near overflow weir to pump suction chamber
                        to avoid carry over of salt crystals.

                      • Once a salt bed is established, start addition of lean brine to the satu-
                        ration pit through the distribution pipes submerged under the salt bed.
                        The lean brine rises from bottom to top of the salt bed by starting the
                        lean brine transfer pumps. In this process the lean brine gets saturated
                        from 150 - 160 g/l up to 300 - 310 g/l NaCl concentration.

                      • During first start-up, raw/demin water is taken into the in-line saturation
                        pit through the distribution tubes, and it passes through the salt bed.

                      • In this process, the water becomes saturated. It is to be ensured that
                        NaCl concentration at outlet of the saturator should not exceed
                        280 g/l NaCl during start-up.

                      • The saturated brine overflows through overflow weir to the pump suc-
                        tion chamber.

                      • Level in pump suction chamber is controlled by 41LIC0100111/21/31
                        which acts on flow control valves 41FV0100110/20.

                      • Saturated raw brine is pumped under level control by raw brine transfer
                        pump 41P01001A-C to the raw brine buffer tank 41TK02001.

                      • Adjust level in raw brine buffer tank to 80%

                      • Increase and maintain concentration of NaCl in raw brine to raw brine
                        buffer tank 41TK02001 at 300 - 310 g/l. This is done by
                        41DIC0100110/20, acting on 41DV0100110/20, which bypasses lean
                        brine to the pump suction chamber of the saturation pit.

                      • From raw brine buffer tank raw brine is pumped by raw brine pump un-
                        der level control of clarified brine tank 41V-04101 (41V-04201) through
                        raw brine recuperator 41E-02102 (41E-02202) and raw brine heater
                        41E-02101 (41E-02201) to UNIT 031 (032).




                                                          Doc. ID-Code                          Rev.

                                         PVC Arvand
                                       Operating Manual

                 SAZE H
                 C O NSU LTANTS              C/A Plant                 Arvand Petrochemical

                                                                                      Page 224 of 967


                      • Adjust raw brine temperature by means of raw brine heater 41E-02101
                        (41E-02201) with 41TIC0200202 (41TIC0200203 for train 2) to 60°C.

                      • Regular analysis is to be carried out at various sampling points as per
                        Analytical Manual.

                      When cell room is in operation, i.e. salt and water is consumed, the fol-

                        41FIC 3410108. Put controller on auto mode.

                        - 40%.

                      • Ensure that saturation pits in operation are filled properly with salt.

                        lytical Manual.

2.7        PART 7: NORMAL OPERATION

2.7.1      NORMAL ROUTINE OF OPERATION
                      • Observe and monitor the FCS carefully

                      • Record unusual circumstances or changes in process parameters

                      • Check field instrumentation and fill in log sheets as required

                      • Observe tank levels and levels in pump suction chamber of saturation
                        pits

                      • Check field equipment for leakage and unusual noises.

                      • Check leakage of raw brine transfer line by comparison of flow at
                        41FI0100201 and 41FI0200110

                      • Check leakage of lean brine transfer line by comparison of flow at
                        FI0200301 and sum of flows from 41FIC0100110, 41FIC0100120 and
                        41FIC0100101.

                      • Check regular filling of salt to saturation pits.

                      • Clean overflow sieve of saturation pits to pump suction chamber if re-
                        quired.

                      • Check level of raw brine buffer tank (normally 80%).

                      • Keep level of lean brine buffer tank at normally 30-40% by manual ad-
                        justment of demin / raw water flow to brine system.

2.7.3      PERFORMANCE CHECK
                      Samples are to be taken from the sample points provided, as per Analyt-
                      ical Manual.

                      From time to time a representative sample of the salt as delivered to the
                      saturation pits must be analysed. Results give conclusion about estimat-
                      ed consumption figures of chemicals for precipitation, cycle time of filters
                      and ion exchangers and amount of brine purge.

                      The following should be monitored in the field:

                      • Flow of demin water for pump seals of:

                          – Raw brine pump 41P-02001A-C

                          – Lean brine transfer pump 41P-02002A-C

                          – Raw brine transfer pump 41P-01001A-C

                      • Temperatures of:

                          – lean brine at starting and end point of lean brine transfer from com-
                            plex to saturation area (41TI0200301 and 41TI0100101).

                          – raw brine at starting and end point of raw brine transfer from satura-
                            tion to complex area (41TI0100201 and 41TI0200101).

                          – inlet (41TI0200206) and outlet (41TI0200209 and 41TI0200210) of
                            lean brine at raw brine recuperator 41E-02102 (41E-02202).

                          – inlet (41TI0200206) and outlet (41TI0200201) of raw brine at raw
                            brine recuperator 41E-02102.

                          – inlet (41TI0200207) and outlet (41TI0200204) of raw brine at raw
                            brine recuperator 41E-02202.

                      • Pressure of condensate pump 41P-02003A/B at pressure side
                        (41PI0200201/2)

2.7.4      REDUCED CAPACITY OPERATION
                      The brine saturation system is designed to operate from 100% plant ca-
                      pacity to 40% plant capacity.

                      When the saturation system is operated in reduced capacity mode, the
                      following activities has to be carried out:

                      • Reduce demin / raw water addition through 41FIC3410108 to lean
                        brine buffer tank to keep the level at 40%.

                      • The levels of raw brine buffer tank, saturation pits and condensate tank
                        are controlled by level controller, so no adjustments have to be done.

                      • The temperature of raw brine is controlled by temperature controller,
                        no adjustment has to be done.

                      For long time operation of less 50% plant capacity one saturation pit as
                      well as one transfer pump can be taken out of service.

2.8        PART 8: NORMAL SHUTDOWN
                      The brine saturation system and lean /raw brine treatment should not be
                      shutdown unless it is unavoidable

                      Note:       If a shutdown of complete brine system can be scheduled in
                                  advance, the brine concentration should be reduced in good
                                  time to approx. 280 g/l in order to avoid crystallisation of salt
                                  as a result of temperature decrease in the brine system.

2.8.1      SHUT DOWN FOR LONGER PERIOD
                      The following procedure is used for shut down of the brine system:

                      • Please follow note in chapter 2.8 "Normal shutdown“.

                      • Please refer to chapter 3.8.2 of Operating Manual "Shutdown for a
                        longer period" of brine system inside C/A Plant.

                      • Stop raw brine heating to 60 °C by closing steam reducing valve
                        41PV9410602 of steam reducing unit 41X-94102 and subsequent
                        closing of steam regulating valves 41TV0200202 and 41TV0200203.

                      • Shut off steam condensate pump.

                      • Stop brine purge

                      • Take raw brine transfer pump 41P-01001A-C on manual mode and
                        slowly decrease frequency to 0. Lean brine flow control valves
                        41FV0100110/20 at saturation pits will slowly close automatically. If
                        they are closed, take them in manual mode with set point 0.

                      • Take automatic isolation valve in raw brine line 41XV0200101 on man-
                        ual mode and close it slowly.

                      Note:       Shut down raw and lean brine transfer pumps as well as
                                  valves connected to lean and raw brine transfer lines slowly
                                  (closure time > 1 minute) to avoid liquid hammer and pressure
                                  fluctuations.

                      • Take lean brine transfer pump 41P-02002A-C on manual mode and
                        slowly decrease frequency to 0.

                      • Shut off lean- and raw brine transfer pumps.

2.9        PART 9: EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN

2.9.1      EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN OF UNITS
                      In case of power failure, lean- and raw brine transfer pumps, raw brine
                      pumps and condensate pump will be de-energised and the brine circula-
                      tion will be stopped. In this system, no electric drives are connected to
                      emergency power supply system.

                      • Brine flow to lean brine buffer tank continues, as lean brine pump is on
                        emergency power and flushing of the electrolysers for approx.1 h to re-
                        move chlorine is done.

                      • The level in the lean brine buffer tank will increase.

                      • As lean brine buffer tank is operated at level 40%, there is enough ca-
                        pacity to store the lean brine without overflow of brine.

                      • Close manual 20“ isolating valve between lean brine transfer pump
                        and lean brine transfer line to avoid siphon off of brine from lean brine
                        buffer tank.

2.9.1.1    Interlock Description
                      Please refer to ANNEX A8, INTERLOCK DESCRIPTION.

2.9.1.2    Alarm And Interlock Trip Settings
                      Please refer to ANNEX A19, LIST OF THRESHOLD VALUES.

2.9.2      EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN DUE TO GENERAL REASONS
                      Please refer to chapter 2.8, NORMAL SHUTDOWN.

2.9.3      START-UP FROM EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN
                      Once power supply is established, start brine circle as mentioned in chap-
                      ter 2.6.3.

                      • Check that the density of raw brine (saturated brine) going to the raw
                        brine buffer tank has NaCl concentration in the range of 300 - 310 g/l.

2.10.5     SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS, SPECIFIC INSTRUCTIONS PER UNIT
                      The brine in the saturation pits and in the raw / lean brine treatment has
                      a pH value of 8.0 - 9.5.

2.10.5.1   Handling Hazardous Materials
                      No hazardous chemicals are handled in the brine saturation and raw /
                      lean brine treatment system.




2.10.5.1.1 Danger caused by brine/sodium chloride
                      • Respiratory protection is required when dusts are generated!
                      • Wear nitrile rubber gloves in case of full or splash contact risk.
                             • Layer thickness: 0.11 mm
                             • Breakthrough time > 480 minutes


                      • Wear eye protection!



2.10.5.1.2 Danger caused by ultra pure brine
                      Ulta pure brine is fed into the electrolysers.

                      Danger caused by ultra pure brine (pH 8-11)!
                      Harmfull! Very corrosive. Causes severe burns. May cause serious
                      permanent eye damage. Very harmful by ingestion. Harmful by skin
                      contact or by inhalation of dust.

                      Observe following safety phrases:

                      • In case of contact with eyes, rinse immediately with plenty of water and
                        seek medical advice!
                      • Wear rubber or PVC gloves. Wear eye/face protection!
                      • In case of accident or if you feel unwell, seek medical advice immedi-
                        ately!

3.2        PART 2: DESCRIPTION OF PROCESS

3.2.1      TECHNOLOGICAL PRINCIPLES
                      The brine primary system of each train is designed to produce 500 m3/h
                      of polished brine containing less than 0,5 ppm of suspended solids. The
                      system can be operated at a turndown ratio up to 40%.

                      For satisfactory operation of membrane cell electrolysers, ultra pure brine
                      is a must.

                      The brine primary system comprises of the following systems:

                      • Brine Precipitation & Chemical/Na2CO3 Preparation,
                      • Brine Clarification,
                      • Brine Filtration (Anthracite Media),
                      • Brine Polishing (Precoat Filtration).


                      The Brine Precipitation System and the Brine Clarification System is
                      designed to precipitate and to remove impurities from brine, principally
                      calcium, and magnesium. The clarified brine at outlet of clarifier will con-
                      tain approx. 20 - 50 ppm of suspended solids.

                      The Chemical/Na2CO3 Preparation System is designed to supply 10%
                      Na2CO3 solution (sodium carbonate) in required quantity for the precipi-
                      tation of calcium impurities present in the saturated brine stream.

                      The suspended solids the saturated brine stream have to be removed
                      down to 0,5 ppm prior to feeding the brine to brine secondary system
                      which can handle only dissolved impurities.

                      In order to achieve this, a 2 stage brine filter system has been envisaged.

                      • The "heavy duty" - 1st stage - filters (Brine Filtration with Anthracite
                        Media filters). The brine filtration system is designed to produce fil-
                        tered brine containing 5 ppm suspended solids.
                      • Brine Polishing - 2nd stage - filtration (Precoat Filtration). The brine
                        polishing system is designed to produce polished brine containing less
                        than 0,5 ppm suspended solids.

3.2.2.1    Brine precipitation, Unit 031 (032)
                      Saturated brine from brine saturation unit (raw brine for buffer tank) is
                      pumped by raw brine pump 41P-02001A-C via raw brine recuperator
                      41E-02102 (41E-02202) and raw brine heater 41E-02101 (41E-02201) to
                      the precipitation tank 41R-03101A/B (41R-03202A/B). Pump A feeds to
                      tanks of train 1 and pump B to tanks of train 2 while pump C is common
                      stand-by. The pumps are frequency controlled by level of corresponding
                      clarified brine tanks. The brine overflows from the tank
                      41R-03101A (41R-03201A) to the tank 41R-03101B (41R-03201B).
                      Each of the precipitation tanks is equipped with an agitator 41MX03101
                      A/B (41MX03201 A/B), to keep the precipitates in suspension.

                      The major impurities in saturated brine like calcium (Ca2+) and magnesi-
                      um (Mg2+) are precipitated as calcium carbonate (CaCO3) and magnesi-
                      um hydroxide (Mg(OH)2).
                      Minor impurities such as strontium carbonate SrCO3 and aluminium hy-
                      droxide AL(OH)3 are also precipitated.
                      Excess of impurities (predominantly sulphates) in the brine are main-
                      tained by continuously purging of lean brine to the waste water system
                      and are dealt within the chapter 5.2 and 16.

                      Based on the salt quality, calculated quantities of sodium carbonate
                      (Na2CO3 as 10% solution) and sodium hydroxide (NaOH as 18% solu-
                      tion) are added to the precipitation tanks 41R-03101A/B (41R-03202A/B)
                      respectively.

                      During normal operation, sodium carbonate solution is added into the first
                      precipitation tank (A) using chemical pump 41P-03001A-C and sodium
                      hydroxide is added to the second tank (B) from the caustic pump
                      41P-26002A/B.
                      A provision has been made to take any one of the precipitation tanks out
                      of service/production (temporary for maintenance). In such a case caustic
                      soda is added to the brine stream downstream of the precipitation tank.

                      As the brine temperature is about at 60 °C, an excess of approx.
                      400 mg/l Na2CO3 and 150 mg/l NaOH is maintained in the raw brine, in
                      order to have proper precipitation.
