3.2.2.2    Chemical/Na2CO3 Handling, Unit 030
                      The 10% w/w sodium carbonate solution (Na2CO3) is prepared by dis-
                      solving Na2CO3 in lean brine in the chemical tanks 41V-03001 and 41V-
                      03002. One tank is used for supply of Na2CO3 solution to the brine sys-
                      tem while in the other tank a new batch of solution is prepared. At low lev-
                      el in the „supply“ tank a switch over to the other tank is required to ensure
                      constant feed to the brine system and a new batch has to be prepared in
                      the „old supply“ tank, etc.
                      Each of the tanks is equipped with an agitator 41MX03001 or
                      41MX03002 for mixing and a unloading table 41X-ö03001 or 41X-03002
                      for manual feeding Na2CO3. Chemical pumps 41P-03001A-C are provid-
                      ed for pumping the solution to the precipitator tanks of the two trains:
                      Pump A is connected to chemical tank 41V-03001, Pump B is connected
                      to 41V-03002 while Pump C is common stand-by.
                      The pallets with the 50 kg bags of Na2CO3 can be lifted with hoist
                      41HC03005 to the elevating platform 41HC03005 for shifting the bags to
                      the unloading table.

3.2.2.3    Brine Clarification, Unit 041 (042)
                      The raw brine containing precipitated impurities and excess chemicals
                      flows by gravity to the feed well of the clarifier 41R-04101 (41R-04201).
                      The rising velocity of brine in the clarifier is maintained as laminar flow.
                      Sufficient residence time (approx. 9 ½ hours) is provided for the precipi-
                      tates to settle out.

                      The brine containing approx. 20-50 ppm suspended solids overflows from
                      the clarifier to the clarified brine tank 41V-04101 (41V-04201). A raw wa-
                      ter seal of approx. 150 mm height is maintained above the brine to reduce
                      heat losses. The clarifier is provided with a suspended ring launder with
                      an extended inner wall. The extended inner walls helps to support the wa-
                      ter layer. To create the water layer raw water is added by spray nozzles
                      at practically zero pressure to prevent diffusion of the same water into the
                      brine.

                      In the clarifier more than 99% of solids settle down, and are pushed to-
                      wards the central cone of the clarifier by the rake arm 41R-04101-I01
                      (41R-04201-I01). Removal of the settled sludge at regular intervals
                      avoids large sludge build-up in the clarifier. The sludge (or underflow)
                      from the clarifier (as 10% solids concentration) is removed by a timer op-
                      erated on/off valve. The underflow flows by gravity to the sludge tank

                      by continuous agitation, with agitator 41-MX36001A-C.

                      In the sludge tank, the underflow is treated with 16% HCl stream from
                      EDC/VCM plant. Alternatively a provision has been made to use 16% HCl
                      from HCl head tank 41V-07007 (s. chapter 5, page 298). The treated
                      waste water stream from the sludge tank is routed via sludge pump
                      41P-36002A-C to battery limit (see also chapter 16).

                      To facilitate quicker settling, flocculating agent is added to the brine prior
                      to feeding to the clarifier. The flocculant helps in formation of larger flocs
                      which results in faster settling of the precipitates. Concentration of floccu-
                      lant in brine is maintained at approx. 1 ppm.

                      Flocculating agent is prepared to the flocculant preparation unit
                      41U-04150 (41U-04250). This unit consists of 2 flocculant preparation
                      tanks and 2 metering pumps. These tanks are provided with agitators.
                      While one of the tanks is used for feeding flocculant solution to the brine
                      stream, the other tank is used for preparation and swelling of the floccu-
                      lating agent. Swelling improves the performance of flocculating agent.
                      Feeding of flocculant to clarifier inlet is done by metering pumps. The floc-
                      culant feed rate is varied by stroke adjustment of the metering pumps.

3.2.2.4    Brine Filtration, Unit 050, 051 (052)
                      Brine from clarifier still contains approx. 20 - 50 ppm of suspended solids.
                      The removal of these suspended solids is done in the 9 identical anthra-
                      cite filters 41FT05101A-J (41FT05201A-J). 8 filters are in operation with
                      1 filter under backwash. When back washing of a particular filter is com-
                      pleted, the back washed filter in put into operation.

                      The brine filters are filled with anthracite media of 3 particle sizes. The top
                      layer consists of fine particles and act as the filter media. The lower layers
                      are meant for supporting the top layer. The complete bed rests on a per-
                      forated plate. Filter nozzles are fixed on these perforations. The filter noz-
                      zles prevent passing of any anthracite into the filtrate.

                      Clarified brine from the clarified brine tank 41V-04101 (41V-04201) is
                      forced through the brine filters by the clarified brine pump 41P-04101A/B
                      (41P-04201A/B). Brine enters the filter from the top. The suspended sol-
                      ids are retained on the top surface of the filter bed. The filtrate passes
                      through the filter nozzles to the lower part of filter housing. The filtered
                      brine from the filter flows under pump pressure to filtered brine tank
                      41V-05001. The filtered brine contains approx. 2 - 5 ppm suspended sol-
                      ids.

                      The filtered brine tank 41V-05001 is common for both trains and is level
                      controlled. To avoid disturbance in both clarifiers during load changes at
                      the electrolysers the flow rate of clarified brine to the antracite filters of
                      one train is kept constant while the other is changing according to the lev-
                      el in the filtered brine tank. The filtered brine tank can also overflow back-
                      wards to the clarified brine tanks 41V-04101 (41V-04201) and to the lean
                      brine buffer. Normally there is no overflow from filtered brine tank.

                      Sludge removal by back washing is done once in every 2,67 (2:40) hours,
                      i.e. each filter is on line for 24 hours before being taken out for backwash.
                      Exact frequency of back washing depend upon quality of clarified brine
                      and is decided during normal operation. Back washing is by means of fil-
                      tered brine using the backwash pump 41P-05104A/B (41P-05204A/B).
                      The backwash is taken to the backwash collecting tank 41V-05106
                      (41V-05206) from where it is continuously recycled into the brine system,
                      upstream of the clarifier using the backwash recovery pumps
                      41P-05106A/B.

                      If a filter is allowed to operate too long between two consequetive back
                      washes, the cake build up may be too high which means the resistance
                      to flow will be too high. In such a case only a small amount of brine passes
                      through this filter and the rest through the clean filters. This may result in
                      unsatisfactory filter operation.

                      Back washing of a brine filter is done in 4 steps / parts (please also refer
                      to ANNEX A8, INTERLOCK DESCRIPTION):

                      • Isolation of filter (Part III)
                      • Backwash (Part IV)
                      • Recycle/Preparation (Part I)
                      • Normal Operation (Part II)
                      Before taking a filter back in operation a visual check of clearness of brine
                      is required.

3.2.2.5    Brine Polishing, Unit 050, 051 (052)
                      The brine polishing system of each train consists of 3 identical filters
                      41FT05102A-C (41FT05202A-C). Two filters are in operation, one is
                      stand by. The purpose of the polishing filtration system is to remove final
                      traces of suspended solids from the filtered brine (2 - 5 ppm) to less than
                      0,5 ppm in polished brine.

                      From the filtered brine tank 41V-05001, the brine is pumped by the filtered
                      brine pumps 41P-05001A-C to the brine polishing filters 41FT05102A-C
                      (41FT05202A-C). Each filter will be handling 50% brine flow i.e. at the
                      rate of max. 255 m3/h. The flow rate to each filter is controlled depending
                      on electrolyser load.

                      During regeneration mode of one particular polishing filter, the stand by
                      polishing filter will go on-line.

                      To avoid plugging of micropores of the filter cloth by very fine suspended
                      solids, a precoat layer is applied on the outer surface of each filter cloth
                      before filtration is started.
                      A precoat suspension of alpha- (α-) cellulose in polished brine is prepared
                      in the precoat tank 41V-05105 (41V-05205), which is equipped with an
                      agitator 41MX05105 (41MX05205). Precoat circulation before taking a fil-
                      ter on-line is done by precoat pump 41P-05105 (41P-05205).

                      During polishing filtration, a small quantity of α - cellulose (2% to max. 5%
                      suspension) is added to the filtered brine as body feed.
                      A body feed suspension of α - cellulose in polished brine is prepared in
                      the body feed tank 41V-05107 (41V-05207), which is equipped with an
                      agitator 41MX05107 (41MX05207). The body feed is dosed into the fil-
                      tered brine stream by body feed metering pumps 41P-05107A/B
                      (41P-05207A/B).

                      The purpose of dosing body feed is to decrease the pressure drop in the
                      polishing filter and thereby increase the period between two successive
                      regenerations.

                      The polishing filter is a vertical pressure vessel made of mildsteel with
                      hard rubber lining. The filter vessel has a 30° cone for dry sludge dis-
                      charge.
                      Between the filter top cover and the main flange of the filter vessel, there
                      is an intermediate piece which supports the registers of filter candles. The
                      registers are arranged in groups. The filter candles itself consists of a
                      central tube for filtrate collection and concentric filter tubes. During filtra-
                      tion, the liquid is pressed from outside through the filter cloth forming a
                      uniform cake out of the α - cellulose and solids from the brine.

                      Because of the concave-convex shape of the cross section of the filter el-
                      ements and the constantly present pressure differential, the filter cake
                      stays in place. The filtrate flows downwards through the concentric filter
                      tubes and rises in the central tube. It leaves the filter through the regis-
                      ters.

                      The polished brine from the filter outlet is discharged to the polished brine
                      tank 41V-05002.

                      From the polished brine tank the brine is pumped by polished brine
                      pumps 41P-05002A-C to the chlorine recuperator 41E-21104
                      (41E-21204). Here polished brine is heated from 55 °C to 60 °C by ex-
                      changing heat from hot chlorine gas stream from the cells (see chapter 7
                      Chlorine Cooling). The polished brine then passes through the brine re-
                      cuperator 41E-07103 (41E-07203). Here, the brine is further heated to
                      approx. 70 - 75 °C, by exchanging heat from lean brine stream.

                      The polished brine then goes for further treatment to the secondary brine
                      purification system (to the ion exchange columns 41FT06101A-C
                      (41FT06201A-C) - see following chapter 4, Secondary Brine Purification).

                      The polished brine tank overflows (5-10% of actual flow rate) continuous-

                      The pressure drop across the filter increases with increasing cake thick-
                      ness. The pressure drop across is constantly monitored and must not ex-
                      ceed 2.0 bar. As soon as the pressure drop approaches 2 bar, the filter
                      shall be taken out for back washing/cleaning. Normally, one filter is back
                      washed after approx. 48 hours of filtration, depending on quality of brine
                      and pressure drop across the filter whichever is earlier.

                      The back washing of candles is done with air/polished brine through the
                      FCS based sequence control. The sludge and precoat deposited over the
                      candle is dried with the help of air and finally the dry sludge is discharged
                      from the filter to a sludge container 41X-05101A-C (41X-05201 A-C).

                      The regeneration/back washing of the polishing filter is done in the follow-
                      ing steps (please also refer to ANNEX A8, INTERLOCK DESCRIPTION:

                      • Filling of the filter with brine.
                      • Homogenisation.
                      • Precoating and circulation.
                      • Taking the filter into stand by mode.
                      • Taking the stand by filter into operation.
                      • Isolation of the filter to be taken out for back washing.
                      • Draining of the filter under air pressure (1 bar g)
                      • Final draining of the filter under air pressure (1 bar g).
                      • Drying using air at 3-4 bar g each group/row of polishing filter candles.
                      • Depressurising of filter.
                      • Filter cake disposal to sludge container.

                      For more information also refer to vendor documentation of Requisition
                      8408205-CB-ME-0041.

3.2.3      PROCESS CHEMISTRY

3.2.3.1    Brine Precipitation/Clarification
                      The major impurities in brine which need to be removed are calcium
                      (Ca2+) magnesium (Mg2+) and sulphates (SO42-). Calcium (Ca2+) and
                      Magnesium (Mg2+) are precipitated out by treatment with 10% sodium
                      carbonate solution (Na2CO3) and 18% sodium hydroxide solution (NaOH)
                      respectively.

                             CaCl2 + Na2CO3 → CaCO3↓ + 2NaCl

                             Heat of reaction ∆ Hr (at 25 °C) = -26.08 Kcal/mol

                             MgCl2 + 2 NaOH → Mg(OH)2↓ + 2 NaCl

                             Heat of reaction ∆ Hr (at 25 °C) = -61.40 Kcal/mol

                      Satisfactory operation of the clarifier and brine filters depends on proper
                      crystal growth in the precipitation tank. The crystal size in the precipitation
                      tank depends on level of excess chemicals in the raw brine stream. A too
                      high or too low excess chemical can hamper crystal growth and thereby
                      settling characteristics in the clarifier. An excess of approx. 400 mg/l
                      Na2CO3 and 150 mg/l NaOH are maintained in the brine stream in order
                      to have proper precipitation.

                      CaCO3 produces a small hard crystal which act as seeds for Mg(OH)2
                      precipitation.

                      The desirable pH value for the raw brine stream upstream/downstream of
                      the precipitation tank is pH = 9 - 11.
                      A too high pH (>12) of the raw brine stream is not desirable as it may re-
                      sult in dissolution of Silica & Aluminium.
                      A too low pH (< 7 - acidic brine from saturation) of the raw brine stream
                      is not desirable as it may result in pick up of heavy metals associated with
                      the salt.
                      At low pH (acidic), Ca2+ and Mg2+ will not be precipitated as it will be in
                      dissolved form.

                      In order to facilitate proper and faster settling of the precipitates in the
                      clarifier. Sodium polyacrylates as flocculant is added which helps in for-
                      mation of larger flocs.


                                                            Doc. ID-Code                          Rev.
Copyright 2005 Uhde GmbH
                                                      8408205-CB-PR-MNL-0102                       02
                                         PVC Arvand
                                       Operating Manual

                 SAZE H
                 C O NSU LTANTS             C/A Plant                 Arvand Petrochemical

Job Code:        PVC Arvand       Job Code:                        Owner Job Code: PVC Arvand
                                                                                     Page 249 of 967


                      The brine flow in the clarifier is maintained laminar. The brine flows down
                      under the feed well and rises up and overflows into the overflow launder.
                      Under such calm laminar environment, the flocs of precipitate settle down
                      easily. This ensures that the supernatent clarified brine overflowing the
                      clarifier contains 20 - 50 ppm suspended solids.

                      A water seal is provided over the brine, to minimise heat loss from the top
                      surface which would otherwise hinder proper settling of the precipitates.
                      A 150 mm layer of water on the brine surface reduces heat losses from
                      the surface by about 45%.

3.6.1      GENERAL PRECONDITION

3.6.1.1    Prerequisites for Start-up
                      Following things are to be ensured before charging salt into the brine sys-
                      tem:

                      • Complete brine circuit, i.e. Saturator → Raw brine buffer tank → Pre-
                        cipitation tank → Clarifier → Brine filters → Polishing filters → Ion ex-
                        changer → Cell header bypass → Anolyte tank → Dechlorination →
                        Lean brine buffer tank → Saturator, is running at 60 - 70 °C.
                      • All controllers will be working in AUTO mode.
                      • All interlocks are active.
                      • Anthracite filter sequence is streamlined and ready for backwash op-
                        eration.
                      • Polishing filter sequence is streamlined. The filters are regenerated,
                        precoated and ready for operation.
                      • Chemicals for precipitation (see chapter 3.7.1.1) and flocculation (see
                        chapter 3.7.1.2) are available/prepared.
                      • Clarifier rake arm is in operation.
                      • Ion exchange columns are ready for operation; with ion exchange resin
                        filled in and duly regenerated.
                      • Required laboratory analysis procedures for salt / brine is established
                        along with the laboratory equipment/instrument.

                      For initial start-up please refer to Part 6, Normal Start-Up and Part 7, Nor-

3.7        PART 7: NORMAL OPERATION

3.7.1      NORMAL ROUTINE OF OPERATION
                      The normal operating actions in the primary brine consist of routine activ-
                      ities to ensure the smooth operation of the system.

                      The following activities must be performed on either a regular document-
                      ed basis or on request from the control room:

                      • Collection, analysis and recording of brine system parameters,
                      • Preparation of flocculating agent (batch) (see chapter 3.7.1.3),
                      • Preparation of Na2CO3 solution (see chapter 3.7.1.3),
                      • Preparation of alpha-cellulose precoat and body feed (see chapter
                        3.7.1.3),
                      • Ensure sufficient availability of consumable chemicals,
                      • Inspection of precipitator, clarifier and filter discharges.


                      FCS operator must ensure field and control operations are performed
                      punctually in order to ensure continued supply of brine. These include:

                      • Observation of run time of filters and subsequent preparation of pre-
                        coat for regeneration,
                      • Observe pressure, valve position or quality changes which may be in-
                        dicators of an upset,
                      • Sufficient inventory of salt in saturators, brine and demineralised water
                        (WDS) for regeneration and shift changeovers,
                      • Alteration of system parameters based on field observations and
                        measurements.

3.7.1.1    Operation of Na2CO3 -Solution
                      • The Na2CO3-solution preparation system should be charged with
                        Na2CO3 powder and dissolved before required.
                      • The chemical tank should be filled with lean brine and agitator and
                        blower for dust removal started before addition of Na2CO3 powder.
                      • Powder should be gradually added to avoid clumping. Occasional
                        measurement should be made of concentration to ensure it is in the
                        rage.



3.7.1.2    Operation of Flocculant Preparation System
                      • The flocculant preparation system should be charged with flocculant
                        and expanded before required.
                      • The flocculating tank should be filled with raw water and agitator start-
                        ed before addition of flocculating powder.
                      • Powder should be gradually added to avoid clumping. Occasional
                        measurement should be made of concentration to ensure it is in the
                        range.

3.7.2      TROUBLE SHOOTING
                      The following trouble shooting procedure discusses upset conditions of
                      the brine system which are considered to be important.

                      Interlocks, as described in interlocking description prevent the brine sys-
                      tem from damage. In case of an upset, however, there is usually enough
                      time for the operators to eliminate the problem. The information given be-
                      low cannot claim to be a complete list of all possible disturbances. The
                      necessary actions are summarised in the following table.

3.7.3      PERFORMANCE CHECK
                      From time to time a representative sample of the salt as delivered to the
                      plant must be taken and analysed. The results of the analysis are a meas-
                      ure for estimating the loading time of the ion exchangers, chemical con-
                      sumption, etc.

                      While it is essential that the above analysis is performed by the laboratory
                      personnel, the brine quality must be supervised by the shift personnel al-
                      so. The activities include:

                      • Checking the clarified brine concentration:
                        The desired values in normal operation are
                        300 - 310 g/l NaCl.
                        ~ 400 mg/l Na2CO3
                        ~ 150 mg/l NaOH
                      • Checking the polished brine quality:
                        The outlet brine from the brine polishing filters must be checked regu-
                        larly. The filter must be cleaned immediately if any turbidity of the brine
                        is observed.
                        If this cannot be corrected by cleaning, the filter should be opened to
                        check whether the filter bags are damaged. In this case the electrolysis
                        load will have to be decreased.
                      • Checking the pH value:
                        For this purpose, samples of raw brine, of pure brine, of anolyte and of
                        lean brine must be analysed with the aid of a laboratory instrument.
                        In case of deviations the pH indicators must be examined.
                        Maintenance work on the pH instruments should be performed regu-
                        larly (at least twice a week as deviations might be caused by fouling of
                        the electrodes).
                      • Checking the free chlorine content in raw brine:
                        The lean brine should be analysed following upset to determine free
                        chlorine concentration.


                      Please refer also to the Analytical Manual.

3.7.4      REDUCED CAPACITY OPERATION
                      Each train of the plant including brine primary system is designed to op-
                      erate from 100% train capacity down to 40% train capacity for the case of
                      low demand of chlorine. Preferred stand-by mode of operation is at full
                      circulation rates, which allows better control of the heat balance.

                      When the brine primary system of one train is operated in reduced capac-
                      ity mode, following activities are to be carried out:

                      • Reduce flocculant agent addition to the clarifier.
                      • Reduce demin / raw water addition to lean brine to keep level in lean
                        brine buffer tank constant.
                      • Brine flow to precipitation tank will be reduced automatically controlled
                        by level of clarified brine tank.
                      • Brine flow to anthracite filter of one train will be reduced automatically
                        controlled by level of filtered brine tank while the flow at the other train
                        will be constant (set point to be reduced if flow in other train < 40% of
                        normal flow).
                      • Brine flow to polishing filters will be reduced depending on electrolyser
                        load.
                      • Brine flow to ion exchange columns (2 lines per train) will be adjusted
                        by reducing flow to the electrolysers (frequence controlled polished
                        brine pump keeps pressure to electrolysers constant).

3.7.5      EFFLUENT AND RISK OF ENVIRONMENT
                      The clarifier under flow sludge after treatment with 16% HCl in the sludge
                      tank 41R-04101 (41R-04201) is routed via sludge pump 41P-36002A-C
                      to B.L.

                      Any excess HCl or NaOH in the effluent stream is neutralized with NaOH
                      or HCL downstream of the sludge tanks, prior to effluent discharge to
                      plant battery limit. CO2 gas evolved from the sludge tank is send to the
                      vent scrubbar 41T-36001 before vented to atmosphere, at a safe loca-
                      tion. Hence, there is no risk to environment due to the effluents generated
                      from the brine precipitation. Please refer to chapter 16, Waste Water
                      Treatment.

                      The anthracite filter backwash is recycled back into the brine system up-
                      stream of the clarifier. The sludge eventually leaves the system in the
                      clarifier underflow.

                      Lean brine is continuously purged at a controlled rate to remove sul-
                      phates from the brine system. The effluent stream is discharged to the
                      Plant battery limit. Hence, there is no risk to environment due to this ef-
                      fluent stream.

                      Dry sludge generated during regeneration of brine polishing filter com-
                      prises of solids, alpha cellulose and brine. The moisture content of the dry
                      sludge is approx. 30%. The sludge is collected in sludge containers, and
                      disposed outside B.L.

3.8        PART 8: NORMAL SHUTDOWN

3.8.1      NORMAL SHUTDOWN
                      The brine system of each train should not be shutdown unless it is una-
                      voidable.

                      Note:       This may be necessary in order to perform repair and mainte-
                                  nance work on the brine system. If the brine system of one
                                  train has to shut down the other train can still be in operation.
                                  If a shutdown of both trains can be scheduled in advance, the
                                  brine concentration should be reduced in good time to approx.
                                  280 g/l NaCl in order to avoid crystallisation as a result of the
                                  temperature decrease in the system.



3.8.2      SHUTDOWN FOR LONGER PERIOD
                      The following procedure is used for shutting down the brine system of one
                      train. This is also applicable if both trains have to shut down:

                      • Reduce chemical addition to precipitation tank slowly according to the
                        plant load. Chemicals addition can be stopped totally if there is no fur-
                        ther brine saturation.
                      • If both trains have to shut down the concentration of the feed brine has
                        to be decreased to 280 g/l NaCl during cell load reduction.
                      • After deenergising of the electrolysers they should be flushed with pure
                        brine in order to remove the chlorine from the cells (see also chapter
                        5.8).
                      • When free chlorine is no longer present in the brine, acidifying of the
                        anolyte can be interrupted.
                      • Depending on shut down time, drain electrolysers (see chapter 5.8).
                      • Open the interconnection between pure brine header and anolyte
                        header and in the cell room to bypass the electrolysers.
                      • Stop the polished brine pump.
                      • Stop the lean brine pump.

                               filtered brine pump in order to keep the polishing filter on-line
                               at reduced flow rate. The outlet can be recycled back to fil-

                               the agitator in precipitation tanks body feed tank and clarifier
                               rake arm.

3.9        PART 9: EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN

3.9.1      EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN OF UNIT
                      In case of power failure, all motor driven equipment will be deenergised
                      and the brine circulation will be stopped. The polished brine pump will re-
                      start on emergency diesel.
                      Pure brine from head tank will flow by gravity to the cells and the anolyte
                      to the anolyte tank.

                      The continued operation of the clarifier motor will prevent overloaded re-
                      start conditions due to continued settling in the clarifier.



3.9.1.1    Interlock Description
                      Please refer to ANNEX A8, INTERLOCK DESCRIPTION.



3.9.1.2    Alarm And Interlock Trip Settings
                      Please refer to ANNEX A19, LIST OF THRESHOLD VALUES.



3.9.2      EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN OF UNIT DUE TO GENERAL REASONS
                      Please refer to chapter 3.8, Normal Shutdown.

3.9.3      START-UP FROM EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN
                      Once power supply is established all pumps/motors connected to emer-
                      gency power can be switched over to normal power supply.

                      • Brine circuit has to be established.
                      • If required start addition of chemicals to precipitation tank and floccu-
                        lant dosing and alpha cellulose dosing.
                      • Start agitators in the respective tanks (precipitation tanks, flocculant
                        tank, body feed tank etc.).
                      • Maintain the temperature of pure brine in the system to 70 - 75 °C.
                      • If required raise the salt content in brine to 270 - 280 g/l or greater for
                        start-up of cells.

3.10.5     SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS, SPECIFIC INSTRUCTIONS PER UNIT
                      The hazardous chemicals handled in the brine primary system are caus-
                      tic soda (18% NaOH), Hydrochloric acid (16% HCl) and sodium carbon-
                      ate solution.

                      All personnel working with or near caustic soda and hydrochloric acid
                      must be thoroughly instructed as to the hazard involved when dealing
                      with these chemicals. All work should be performed by properly instructed
                      personnel and under experienced supervision.

                      Should an accident occur inspite of careful operation of the plant, imme-
                      diate first aid is imperative.

3.10.5.1   Handling hazardous materials

3.10.5.1.1 Danger caused by brine/sodium chloride
                      • Respiratory protection is required when dusts are generated!
                      • Wear nitrile rubber gloves in case of full or splash contact risk.
                             • Layer thickness: 0.11 mm
                             • Breakthrough time > 480 minutes


                      • Wear eye protection!



3.10.5.1.2 Danger caused by caustic soda/catholyte
                      Caustic soda/catholyte is handled in this system.

                      Danger caused by caustic soda/catholyte!
                      Harmfull! Very corrosive. Causes severe burns. May cause serious
                      permanent eye damage. Very harmful by ingestion. Harmful by skin
                      contact or by inhalation of dust.

                      Observe following safety phrases:

                      • In case of contact with eyes, rinse immediately with plenty of water and
                        seek medical advice!

4.2        PART 2: DESCRIPTION OF PROCESS

4.2.1      TECHNOLOGICAL PRINCIPLES
                      The brine secondary system of each train is designed to produce
                      ~ 500 m3/h of pure brine containing less than 20 ppb of calcium & mag-
                      nesium.

                      In addition, brine conditioning (heating or cooling) is made prior to feeding
                      to the cell room.



4.2.2      UNIT DESCRIPTION

                      P&ID:       06101

                                  06102

                                  06103

                      Train 2:

                      P&ID:       06201

                                  06202

                                  06203

                      Note:        The equipment numbers in the following description refers to
                                   train 1. Equipment numbers of Train 2 are in brackets.

                      The polished brine from the polished brine tank 41V-05002 is pumped via
                      polished brine pumps 41P-05002A-C (Pump A connected to Train 1,
                      Pump B connected to Train 2 and Pump C is common stand-by) for fur-
                      ther treatment to the secondary brine purification and pure brine heat
                      conditioning.

                      To ensure constant feed-pressure to the electrolysers the polished brine
                      pumps are frequency controlled by 41PIC0610402 (41PIC0620402).

4.2.2.1    Secondary Brine Purification
                      Polished brine coming from the brine polishing filters 41FT05102A-C
                      (41FT05202A-C) contains approx. 5 -10 ppm of calcium and magnesium
                      cations. These impurities have to be removed to a concentration of less
                      than 20 ppb to make the brine suitable for the membrane cells. The puri-
                      fication is performed in 4 ion exchange columns arranged in 2 lines (per
                      train). Each line is designed to handle 50% of the total brine capacity for
                      one train.

                      The columns are filled with Lewatit TP208, a chelating cation exchange
                      resin, with a very high selectivity for calcium, magnesium and strontium
                      cations. Calcium and magnesium ions present in the brine are absorbed
                      by the ion exchange resin. Ion exchange nozzles ensure the resin remain
                      in the columns.

                      In normal operation, polished brine after recovering heat from hot chlorine
                      gas stream in the chlorine recuperator 41E-21104 (41E-21204) (see
                      chapter 7 Chlorine Cooling) and from hot lean brine stream in the brine
                      recuperator 41E-07103 (41E-07203) (see chapter 5 Anolyte), passes
                      through the 2 lines of Ion exchange columns. Each line consists of 2 Ion
                      exchange columns in series i.e. 41FT06101A/B (41FT06201A/B) and
                      41FT06101C/D (41FT06201C/D). Each column acts in a merry-go-round
                      operation in each line. The brine flow rate through each line of ion ex-
                      change columns is regulated through a flow controller installed in each
                      line.
                      A resin trap 41FT06104A/B (41FT06204A/B) is installed downstream of
                      the ion exchange columns, as a measure to protect the electrolyser cells
                      in case of ion exchange nozzle breakage.
                      The pure brine from the outlet of the ion exchangers flows to the brine
                      heat exchangers 41E-06101 (41E-06201) and 41E-06102 (41E-06202).

                      An on-line calcium/magnesium (hardness) analyser is installed for con-
                      stantly monitoring the quality of pure brine at outlet of the lead ion ex-
                      change columns. In case of a break through, it enables the operating staff
                      to take appropriate action to prevent any damage to the electrolyser
                      membranes.




                                                         Doc. ID-Code                          Rev.
Copyright 2005 Uhde GmbH

                      Under normal conditions, the expected service/operation time of a col-
                      umn is 90 hours. This depends on the quality of polished brine. At 10 ppm
                      hardness, the lifetime is 39 hours, at 5 ppm it is 78 hours. The columns
                      are regenerated & conditioned at every 72 hours, for safety reasons be-
                      fore the break through point is reached.
                      If the leading ion exchange column is exhausted, it is taken out of opera-
                      tion. This column is then put in the regeneration & conditioning mode,
                      while the lagging ion exchange columns takes over the leading position.
                      Subsequently the regenerated & conditioned column is put in the lagging
                      position as an additional safety measure.

                      Hence following modes of operation is possible (in each line).

                      A           1st ion exchanger Column 1

                                  2nd ion exchanger Column 2

                      B           1st ion exchanger Column 2

                                  2nd ion exchanger Column 1

                      The operation of the columns is controlled through FCS. The regenera-
                      tion & conditioning procedure of the ion exchange columns is fully con-
                      trolled by sequence control and is executed from FCS (see ANNEX A8,
                      INTERLOCK DESCRIPTION). The regeneration of one column can only
                      be started if no other column (even from the other train) is in regeneration
                      mode.

                      The solution for regeneration (32% HCl) and for conditioning
                      (18% NaOH) are filled in the HCl tank 41V-06103 (41V-06203) and
                      NaOH tank 41V-06102 (41V-06202) respectively.

                      Polished/demineralised water (WDS) is used as motive liquid for the acid
                      mixing jet 41J-06103 (41J-06103) and caustic mixing jet 41J-06102
                      (41J-06202), which transfers dilute acid (7% HCl) and dilute caustic
                      (4% NaOH) respectively into the ion exchange column.

4.2.2.2    Pure Brine Heat Conditioning
                      For optimum performance, the electrolysers must be operated at a spec-
                      ified temperature which is a function of feed temperature, electrical load
                      and membrane history. The exact temperature however depends on
                      plant load, condition of membrane and coatings. Please refer to
                      chapter 6.

                      The pure brine downstream from the ion exchange columns passes par-
                      allel through brine heater 41E-06101 (41E-06201), and brine cooler 41E-
                      06102 (41E-06202).

                      Depending on operation mode (heating or cooling) steam is used in brine
                      heater or cooling water is used in brine cooler.

                      From the heat exchangers the brine is sent to the cell room pressure con-
                      trolled. A small part of the brine is sent to the pure brine head tank in order
                      to ensure complete filling and maintaining brine temperature in the ves-
                      sel.

                      Steam is used in brine heater 41E-06101 (41E-06201) to raise the tem-
                      perature of pure brine.
                      Steam pressure is reduced to approx. 2.3 bar a (approx. 120 °C) by the
                      pressure control valve 41PV9410502. During plant start-up the heat ex-
                      changer for single electrolyser 41E-06103 (41E-06203) will be used in
                      addition to heat up the brine up to 70 - 75 °C.

                      Normal operation of the plant is possible without steam heating (when
                      load of the electrolyser is greater than 4 kA/m2). Hence, under normal
                      conditions, steam supply to the brine heater 41E-06101 (41E-06201) is
                      stopped. Heating of pure brine is necessary for start-up and during elec-
                      trolyser low load operation.

                      At the time of shutdown, it is necessary to cool the electrolysers by feed-
                      ing cold brine. During shutdown, the brine cooler 41E-06102 (41E-06202)
                      is operated for cooling the brine to cells.

                      During start-up and shutdown of a single electrolyser, brine heat ex-
                      changer 41E-06103 (41E-06203) will be used for heating or cooling of
                      pure brine to the electrolyser.

4.2.3      PROCESS CHEMISTRY
                      The ion exchange columns are filled with Lewatit TP208, a chelating cat-
                      ion-exchange resin, with a very high selectivity for calcium & magnesium
                      cations. The selectivity of the resin decreases for cations like strontium,
                      barium and heavy metals.

                      The ion exchange reaction can be written as follows:

                             Ca++ + 2 Na* (Resin) => Ca** (Resin) + 2Na+

                      This reaction continues until equilibrium is achieved and the break
                      through point is reached. At the break through point calcium & magnesi-
                      um cations pass through the resin bed without adsorption. The saturated
                      resin is then regenerated to its original state by another ion exchange re-
                      action using consecutively 7% hydrochloric acid and 4% caustic soda so-
                      lution.

                      The reaction during regeneration can be represented as follows:

                             Ca** (Resin) + 2HCl => 2 H* (Resin) + CaCl2

                      During the reactions, a volume contraction of approx. 40% from the initial
                      volume of the resin in the sodium form takes place.

                      After removing the calcium from the resin, the conversion into the sodium
                      form takes place by treating with caustic soda solution (conditioning):

                             2 H* (Resin) + 2NaOH => Na* (Resin) + 2H2O

                      The conversion into sodium form is followed by a volume expansion to its
                      original volume.

                      During several regeneration & conditioning processes, a small portion of
                      the resin beads will be fractured due to repeated and excessive expan-
                      sion and contraction. It may be expected that about 1 - 2% of the resin will
                      be fractured after every 200 regeneration cycles. These fines can in-
                      crease the pressure drop across the column which causes further fractur-
                      ing. Hence this is removed from the bed by back washing.

                      The exchange capacity of the resin is about 8 grams calcium/l of resin at
                      the following conditions.


                                                            Doc. ID-Code                          Rev.
Copyright 2005 Uhde GmbH
                                                      8408205-CB-PR-MNL-0102                       02
                                         PVC Arvand
                                       Operating Manual
                                                                        National Petrochemical comany
                 SAZE H
                 C O NSU LTANTS              C/A Plant                   Arvand Petrochemical
                                                                              Company
Uhde Project No: 03-3039           Sazeh Project No: 8047            Owner Project No: 8408205
Job Code:        PVC Arvand        Job Code:                         Owner Job Code: PVC Arvand
                                                                                       Page 279 of 967


                      Brine temperature                     = min. 60 °C

                      pH value                              = min 9.5

                      Brine composition                     = 300 - 310 g/l of NaCl,

                      Ca & Mg (at inlet)                    = (normal) 5 ppm to (max.) 10 ppm

                      The exchange capacity of the resin is reduced at lower brine tempera-
                      tures and lower pH values.

                      Some limitations and precautions in the operation of the ion exchanger
                      have to be taken into account.

                      Free chlorine in the feed brine acts as a strong oxidizing agent and will
                      irreversibly reduce the resin exchange capacity. Therefore, available
                      chlorine levels in the feed brine should be kept at an absolute minimum.
                      Free chlorine can be formed by a reaction of chlorate with hydrochloric
                      acid. Since brine always contains a certain amount of chlorate and hydro-
                      chloric acid is used for regenerating the ion exchange resin, it is very im-
                      portant to flush out chlorate bearing brine with polished/demineralised
                      water prior to regeneration. Small amounts of free chlorine in hydrochloric
                      acid - ranging from 1 - 5 ppm as found during production in HCl synthesis
                      is found to be harmless for the resin.

                      In case of an excessive pressure drop through a column, i.e. the minimum
                      brine flow rate cannot be maintained, another precaution to be taken is
                      the back washing of this column. Due to accumulation of solid particles in
                      the resin bed during service/operation the pressure drop increases and
                      may result in fracturing of resin beds. Thus this column has to be taken
                      out of service/operation and the resin in the column must be back washed
                      in order to flush out the smaller particles.

4.3.6      LIST OF ONLINE ANALYZER
                      41-ANA01, 41-ANA02 and 41-ANA03

                      PID 20001

                      The Ca/Mg Analyser 41-ANA01 is used to monitor the calcium and mag-
                      nesium content in pure brine at outlet from the lead ion exchangers of
                      train 1 while 41-ANA02 is monitoring train 2.

                      Analyser 41ANA-03 is measuring the calcium and magnesium content of
                      pure brine after the heat exchangers to the cell room of each train by
                      turns. Also the calcium and magnesium analysis of 16% HCl can be se-
                      lected.

                      Each line of ion exchangers (each train has 2 ion exchange lines with
                      2 columns each) has a sample flow loop, the Ca/Mg analyser is equipped
                      with internal sample selection values which changes between each line
                      of one train. The analyser is used solely to measure by turns the brine
                      from the lead column.
                      During regeneration, the final step of preparation involves checking the
                      functionality of the freshly regenerated (but still off-line) column before re-
                      turning to service. During this step the Ca/Mg Analyser is dedicated to the
                      off-line column.

                      During the last step of the regeneration, the operator is required to check
                      the Ca/Mg analyser value. If the analyser shows Ca/Mg concentration in
                      pure brine to be less than 20 ppb the operator presses the "Back to Op-
                      eration" push button to confirm his acceptance of the completed regener-
                      ation.

                      If the analyser shows Ca/Mg level > 20 ppb, the operator must collect a
                      manual sample and do the analysis in a lab. If the lab results do not match
                      with the indicated value, the analysis is to be checked.

                      The operator can decide to either return the ion exchanger to service or
                      to perform another complete regeneration.



                      Please refer also to ANNEX A18, LIST OF ONLINE ANALYSER.

4.6        PART 6: NORMAL START-UP



4.6.1      GENERAL PRECONDITION
                      Following prerequisites are to be ensured before passing polished brine
                      through the ion exchange columns:

                      • Polished brine is filled in the polished brine tank 41V-05002 up to high
                        level. The suspended solids content in polished brine is less than
                        1 ppm. The calcium and magnesium content in polished brine is
                        approx. 5 - 10 ppm.
                      • Temperature of polished brine to the ion exchange columns is
                        min. 60 °C.
                      • Ion exchange columns in both line 1 and line 2 are regenerated and
                        are kept ready for operation. In case of start-up from prolonged shut-
                        down, the ion exchange resin in all the columns should be back
                        washed.
                      • All controllers including ion exchange sequence are put to AUTO
                        mode.

4.6.2      FINAL PREPARATION
                      • Once the above prerequisites are fulfilled, start the polished brine
                        pump and allow the brine to pass through following path:
                        Polished brine pump 41P-05002A-C → Chlorine recuperator
                        41E-21104 (41E-22104) → Brine recuperator 41E-07103 (41E-07203)
                        → Ion exchange columns (2 lines) 41FT06101A/B (41FT06201A/B) &
                        41FT-06101C/D (41FT-06201C/D) → Brine heat exchangers
                        41E-06101/41E-06102 (41E-06201/41E-06202) → Cell room bypass
                        → Anolyte System.
                      • The residual Ca + Mg content in pure brine (i.e. downstream of first ion
                        exchange column in both the lines) should not exceed 20 ppb, which
                        is a limit for feed brine to cells. In case this exceeds 20 ppb, the 1st col-
                        umn should be taken out for regeneration. At this time only 2nd column
                        is in line which is sufficient for full load operation. The regenerated col-
                        umn is then taken in line as 2nd column.
                      • The pure brine from ion exchange columns is heated by using steam
                        in brine heat exchanger 41E-06101 (41E-06201) up to 70 - 75 °C re-
                        quired for the cell feed brine.
                        During first start-up or after long shutdown, brine heat exchanger for
                        single electrolyser 41E-06103 (41E-06203) can be used (in addition to
                        above exchanger) to heat the brine in short span.
                      • Pure brine at 70 - 75 °C goes via cell room bypass to the anolyte sys-
                        tem and with an amount of approximately 5% of total brine feed to pure
                        brine head tank which is allowed to overflow back to polished brine
                        tank. The system is now ready to feed pure brine to the cells.

                      Follow procedures as outlined in chapter 4.6.2 „Final Preparation“.

4.7        PART 7: NORMAL OPERATION

4.7.1      NORMAL ROUTINE OF OPERATION
                      Secondary Brine Purification

                      The ion exchange system operates on a FCS programme and records
                      the run time of the leading column in each train. When this designated run
                      time is reached (approx. 72 h), an announcement is made on the FCS
                      and a regeneration can be started. Several field and control room actions
                      are required to enable the smooth execution of a ion exchanger regener-
                      ation.

                      These entail the following:

                      • No other ion exchange tower is in regeneration (also not from other
                        train).
                      • Acknowledge sufficient volume for effluents in waste water system and
                        condensate tank.
                      • Acknowledge successful regeneration before releasing for service.


                      In addition to the FCS timer logic, there is a Ca/Mg analyser which meas-
                      ures the hardness of the pure brine behind the lead column. When 20 ppb
                      is reached, an alarm is made and the operator can confirm the measure-
                      ment by laboratory analysis or commence a regeneration. Prompt action
                      is required in order to avoid high Ca/Mg values in the feed brine and sub-
                      sequent damage to membranes.

                      Maintenance of the Ca/Mg analysers is performed by the instrumentation
                      staff on a regular basis.

                      Back washing of the IOX can be selected at will. If high differential pres-
                      sure across the towers is observed (approx. 1barg) the column should be
                      back washed.

                      Pure Brine Heat Conditioning

                      The pure brine to the electrolysers is pressure controlled by
                      41PIC0610402 (41PIC0620402). During normal operation the pure brine
                      flow out of the ion exchanger columns is split through the brine heater
                      41E-06101 (41E-06201) and brine cooler 41E-06102 (41E-06202). The
                      flow distribution is done manually by block valves at the heat exchanger.

                      Depending on operation mode (heating or cooling) steam is used at the
                      heater while cooling water is blocked at the cooler and vice versa.

                      During heating the brine temperature to the electrolysers is controlled by
                      41TIC0610408 (41TIC0620408).

                      For operating temperatures of the electrolyser please refer to chapter 5.

                      Samples are to be taken from the various sample points provided, as per
                      schedule (refer to part 4.13.1 “SAMPLE TAKING”).

                      The various parameters observed in FCS during normal operation must
                      be continuously monitored.

                      In the field, following parameters should be monitored:

                      • Temperature of pure brine to brine heat exchanger (41TI0610301 /
                        41TI0620301).
                      • Pressure drop across each ion exchange columns in 2 trains
                        41PI0610201 / 02 / 03 / 04
                        41PI0610301 / 02 / 03 / 04
                        41PI0620201 / 02 / 03 / 04
                        41PI0620301 / 02 / 03 / 04.
                      • Flow of demineralised Water (WDS) to polished brine pump seals
                        (41FI0500202, 41FI0500203 and 41FI0500204).
                      • Regular sampling of steam condensate for impurities to detect brine
                        break through of heat exchanger.



4.7.4      REDUCED CAPACITY OPERATION
                      The brine secondary system of each train is designed to operate from
                      100% train capacity to 40% train capacity.

                      When the brine secondary system is operated in reduced capacity mode,
                      following activities are to be carried out:

                      • Reduce brine flowrate through the ion exchange columns by reducing
                        flow to electrolysers.
                      • When brine flowrate is reduced below 50% of the total brine throughput
                        per train, isolate 1 of the 2 lines of ion exchange columns by closing
                        flow control valve after iox-train.
                      • In case electrolyser outlet temperature drops below 70 °C, start heat-
                        ing pure brine using brine heater 41E-06101 (41E-06201). Please also
                        refer to chapter 6.7, page 434.

4.7.5      EFFLUENT AND RISK OF ENVIRONMENT
                      The acidic effluent, generated during regeneration and rinsing with
                      demin. water of the ion exchange resin, is routed to the waste water col-
                      lection pit 41X-36001A/B. This acidic effluent stream is neutralised with
                      18% NaOH solution in the waste water system, prior to discharge to B.L.

                      The alkaline effluent, generated during conditioning and caustic rinsing
                      with polished/demineralised water of the ion exchange resin, is routed to
                      the condensate tank 41V-34001. From here, the alkaline effluent stream
                      is recovered in the brine system.

                      Steam condensate generated during pure brine conditioning in the brine
                      heat exchangers 41E-06101 (41E-06201) and 41E-06103 (41E-06203)
                      during plant start-up and also during plant low load operation
                      (C.D. < 4 kA/m2) is cooled with raw water. The cooled condensate is col-
                      lected via pipe in local effluent collecting pits. From these pits it is pumped
                      to the waste water collection pit 41X-36001A/B.

4.8        PART 8: NORMAL SHUTDOWN



4.8.1      NORMAL SHUTDOWN
                      The secondary brine system of each train should not be shutdown unless
                      it is unavoidable.

                      This may be necessary in order to perform repair and maintenance work
                      on the brine system. If the secondary brine system of one train has to
                      shutdown the other train can still be in operation.

                      Please refer to chapter 3.8.2 „Shutdown for a Longer Period“ of brine sys-
                      tem.



4.9        PART 9: EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN

4.9.1      EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN OF UNIT
                      In case of power failure, all motor driven equipment will be deenergised
                      and the brine circulation will be stopped.
                      Pure brine from the head tank will flow by gravity to the cells. The polished
                      brine pumps are connected to the emergency power system, and these
                      will restart on power failure.

4.10.5     SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS, SPECIFIC INSTRUCTIONS PER UNIT
                      The hazardous chemicals handled in the brine secondary system are
                      caustic soda (18% NaOH) & hydrochloric acid (16% HCl). All personnel
                      working with or near caustic soda & hydrochloric acid must be thoroughly
                      instructed as to the hazard involved when dealing with these chemicals.

                      All work should be performed by properly instructed personnel and under
                      experienced supervision.

                      Should an accident occur inspite of careful operation of the plant, imme-
                      diate first aid is imperative.

                      Please also refer to chapter 1.8, Safety Instructions.

5.2        PART 2: DESCRIPTION OF PROCESS

5.2.1      TECHNICAL PRINCIPLES
                      The anolyte system of each train is designed for completely dechlorina-
                      tion of depleted brine (anolyte) saturated with chlorine coming out of the
                      cell room. For this a 2-stage dechlorination system is used i.e. vacuum
                      dechlorination followed by chemical dechlorination.

                      Heat is also recovered from the lean/depleted brine before returning to
                      the saturation pits by the use of heat recuperation. A part stream of the
                      lean brine of both trains is split off as a purge stream in order to control
                      buildup of impurities within the brine loop.

                      Sodium hypochlorite can be decomposed with HCl then returned to the
                      anolyte and the evolved chlorine is recovered.

                      32% HCl is diluted with polished/demineralised water (WDS) in an auto-
                      matic batch process to 16% and stored in the HCl head tank (common for
                      both trains) for distribution by gravity throughout the plant.



5.2.2      UNIT DESCRIPTION
                      The depleted brine (anolyte) coming from the cells is saturated with chlo-
                      rine. Before the brine is re-saturated with salt (NaCl) and purified, it is to
                      be completely dechlorinated. For this a 2-stage dechlorination system is
                      used.

                      Note:       The system consists of two trains. Equipment numbers are for
                                  train 1, equipment numbers for train 2 are in brackets.




                                                          Doc. ID-Code                          Rev.
Copyright 2005 Uhde GmbH
                                                    8408205-CB-PR-MNL-0102                       02
                                         PVC Arvand
                                       Operating Manual
                                                                       National Petrochemical comany

5.2.2.1    Two-stage Dechlorination
                      In the 1st stage chlorine is desorbed by means of vacuum. The chlorine
                      content in brine after vacuum dechlorination is 10 - 30 mg/l.

                      In the 2nd stage the residual chlorine in brine is chemically neutralised by
                      means of sodium bisulfite (NaHSO3) solution. The 10% NaHSO3 solution
                      is added in a slight excess of approx. 10 - 15 ppm (w/w) to ensure that no
                      free chlorine is passing to the process steps downstream.

                      The depleted brine (anolyte) flows by gravity from the electrolyser cells
                      into the anolyte tank 41V-07101 (07201).

                      The brine leaves the cells at pH of 2.5 - 4.5. To improve the dechlorina-
                      tion, the pH of the anolyte is reduced to 2.0 using HCl (acidification - feed
                      from HCl head tank 41V-07007), before entering the anolyte tank. The
                      analyser AI0710101 (0720101) monitors the pH value of anolyte in the
                      main header after acidification; and thereby controls the HCl addition rate
                      to the anolyte.

                      16% HCl (hydrochloric acid) is prepared by diluting 32% HCl with dem-
                      ineralised water (WDS) in the HCl dilution ejector 41J-07003. The result-
                      ant 16% HCl is stored in HCl head tank 41V-07007 (common for both
                      trains). Demineralised water (WDS) required for dilution of 32% HCl is
                      added through ratio controller FFIC0710306. From the HCl head tank
                      41V-07007, 16% HCl flows under gravity to the following consumers:

                      • To anolyte acidification of train 1 and 2
                      • Acidification of pure brine to cells of train 1 and train 2 (see also chap-
                        ter 6)
                      • To sludge tanks 41V-36001 A, B, C (see also chapter 16)
                      • The calcium and magnesium content in the 16% HCl is measured by
                        Ca/Mg Analyser 41.ANA03.
                      Bleaching lye/Sodium hypochlorite (NaOCl) produced in the Waste Gas
                      Dechlorination can be recovered into the anolyte stream, too. Before
                      recovery, it is treated with HCl to destroy the sodium hypochlorite. An ex-
                      cess of acid must drive the decomposition reaction. Chlorine gas evolved
                      during hypo destruction is recovered in the chlorine gas header.




                                                          Doc. ID-Code                          Rev.
Copyright 2005 Uhde GmbH
                                                    8408205-CB-PR-MNL-0102                       02
                                         PVC Arvand
                                       Operating Manual
                                                                      National Petrochemical comany
                 SAZE H
                 C O NSU LTANTS             C/A Plant                 Arvand Petrochemical
                                                                           Company
Uhde Project No: 03-3039          Sazeh Project No: 8047           Owner Project No: 8408205
Job Code:        PVC Arvand       Job Code:                        Owner Job Code: PVC Arvand
                                                                                     Page 301 of 967


                      The anolyte tank is provided with an overflow line to the Anolyte Drain
                      Tank 41V-7105 (7205). The purpose of the anolyte drain tank is to receive
                      anolyte during draining of electrolysers. The anolyte collected in the
                      anolyte drain tank is pumped by means of Anolyte Recovery Pump
                      41P-07105 (41P-07205), to the anolyte header.

                      There is no overflow to the environment from either tank - if the available
                      sum of empty volume in both the anolyte tank and the anolyte drain tank
                      is less than the volume of the Pure Brine Head Tank 41V-06101 (06201),
                      the pure brine feed will be stopped via interlock (see ANNEX A8).

                      The anolyte tank is working under the pressure of the chlorine system,
                      while the anolyte drain tank is connected to the waste gas unit of each
                      train.

                      From the Anolyte Tank 41V-07101 (07201), the anolyte is sucked into the
                      vacuum tank 41V-07102 (07202), where most of the dissolved chlorine is
                      removed (1st stage of the dechlorination system). In the vacuum tank,
                      anolyte is sprayed over a baffle plate and is allowed to boil under vacuum.
                      In this process of spraying and boiling, chlorine is desorbed.

                      Chlorine from vacuum tank is sucked by vacuum pump 41P-07151A/B
                      (07251A/B) via Vapour Condenser 41E-07101 (07201). The water con-
                      tent of the chlorine gas is reduced by condensation in the vapour con-
                      denser. Chlorine gas is separated from the condensate in the
                      Condensate Separator 41FT07102 (07202). The condensate is returned
                      to the anolyte tank.

                      The required vacuum in the vacuum tank is maintained by vacuum pump
                      unit 41U-07150 (07250). The vacuum pump unit is consisting of two vac-
                      uum pumps and a condensate separator with integrated heat exchanger
                      to cool the recycled seal water/condensate. The condensate from this
                      unit returns through an overflow connection to the anolyte tank.
                      During normal operation the pressure developed is approx. 0.6 bar a and
                      only one vacuum pump is running. During start-up both the vacuum
                      pumps will be operated in parallel the vacuum achieved is approx.
                      0.4 bar a.




                                                         Doc. ID-Code                          Rev.
Copyright 2005 Uhde GmbH
                                                   8408205-CB-PR-MNL-0102                       02
                                         PVC Arvand
                                       Operating Manual
                                                                       National Petrochemical comany
                 SAZE H
                 C O NSU LTANTS              C/A Plant                 Arvand Petrochemical
                                                                            Company
Uhde Project No: 03-3039           Sazeh Project No: 8047           Owner Project No: 8408205
Job Code:        PVC Arvand        Job Code:                        Owner Job Code: PVC Arvand
                                                                                      Page 302 of 967


                      The dechlorinated brine from the vacuum tank is pumped by means of
                      Lean Brine Pumps 41P-07101 A/B (07201 A/B) through brine recuperator
                      41E-07103 (07203) and Raw Brine Recuperator 41E-02101 (41E-02201)
                      to the lean brine buffer tank. Downstream of the brine recuperators the
                      lean brine streams of both trains are combined. Vapour condensate from
                      the caustic evaporation unit and the hydrogen systems is added to the
                      lean brine stream to the Raw Brine Recuperators. Demin / service water
                      is also added after the Raw Brine Recuperators. This is to replenish the
                      water loss through the membranes during electrolysis of brine.

                      At the suction side of the lean brine pumps caustic soda (NaOH 18%) is
                      added to increase the pH from 2 to 8.5 - 9.5 and then sodium bisulfite
                      solution (NaHSO3 10%) is added, to remove any chlorine residual.
                      (2nd stage of the dechlorination system).

                      The addition of caustic soda from the 18% caustic pumps 41P-26002 A/B
                      is controlled by pH measurement 41AICR0710201 (0720201) acting on
                      FV0710206 (720206) and FV710207 (720207), feeding caustic soda to
                      the suction side of the lean brine pumps.

                      The addition of the sodium bisulfite solution is controlled by Redox meas-
                      urement 41AICR0710202 (0720202) acting on FV0710204 (720204) and
                      FV0710205 (0720205), fed to the suction side of the lean brine pumps.

                      The sodium bisulfite needed for the dechlorination is added as a 10% so-
                      lution, which is prepared batchwise in Bisulfite Tank 41V-07004 (common
                      for both trains). The solution is prepared by dissolving NaHSO3 from Big
                      Bags with service / raw water in the agitated tank.

                      Bilsulfite Filling Pump 41P-07003 is pumping sodium bisulfite also to the
                      EDC plant and to Bisulfite Head Tank 41V-07003 (common for both
                      trains).

                      From the Bisulfite Head Tank the solution can be distributed by gravity to
                      the suction side of the lean brine pumps of the two trains for brine dechlo-
                      rination and to the waste water treatment plant, as required.

5.2.2.2    Brine purge
                      Since the level of sulphates should not exceed 12 g/l Na2SO4 (min. 6 g/l
                      Na2SO4) in pure brine, a part stream of lean brine is continuously purged
                      downstream of brine recuperator 41E-07103 (07203). The flowrate of this
                      purge stream is determined by the level of sulphates in pure brine and is
                      controlled by FIC0710211 (0720211).

                      This lean brine purge will also take care of maintaining the chlorate
                      (NaClO3) level below 10 g/l which would otherwise be harmful for mem-
                      brane.

                      The heat of the brine purge stream going to battery limits is removed in
                      the Purge Brine Cooler 41E-07004 with cooling water.



5.2.3      PROCESS CHEMISTRY
                      The formation of sodium bisulfite (meta bisulfite) to sodium bisulfite is ac-
                      cording to:

                             Na2S2O5 + H2O → 2NaHSO3



                      The free chlorine in the depleted brine stream (anolyte) is neutralized by
                      chemical dechlorination.

                             Cl2 + NaHSO3 + NaOH → Na2SO4 + 2NaCl + 2H2O

                      The pH of the anolyte stream is to be maintained at approx. pH = 8.5-9.5
                      for effective chemical dechlorination. A too low pH (< pH = 2) will result in
                      decomposition of chlorates. A too high pH will result in dissolution of sil-
                      ica in the saturator pits.

                      Similarly, a too low redox potential means loss of chemicals (sodium bi-
                      sulfite). A too high redox potential will result in escape of free chlorine in
                      the lean brine. This is harmful to the ion exchange resin, because free
                      chlorine in the brine acts as a strong oxidising agent and will irreversibly
                      damage the ion exchange capacity of the resin.
