5.6        PART 6: NORMAL START-UP

5.6.1      GENERAL PRECONDITION
                      Following prerequisites are to be ensured before start up of anolyte sys-
                      tem.

                      • Pure brine is available in Pure Brine Head Tank 41V-06101 (06201)
                        and the brine head tank is overflowing into the polished Brine Tank
                        41V-05002.
                      • Temperature of pure brine is maintained at 70 - 75 °C.
                      • NaCl concentration in pure brine is greater than 280 g/l.
                      • 16% HCl is available in HCl Head Tank 41V-07007, 10% sodium bi-
                        sulfite (NaHSO3) is available in Bisulfite Head Tank 41V-07003.
                      • All controllers in AUTO mode.
                      • All interlocks are active.
                      • Following systems are in operation:
                        Cooling water, demineralised water, raw water, instrument air, nitro-
                        gen, waste gas dechlorination system.
                      • Following systems are ready for operation:
                        Rectifiers, electrolysers, chlorine system, hydrogen system.



5.6.2      FINAL PREPARATION
                      Check communication system.

5.6.3      INITIAL START-UP
                      Once the above prerequisites are fulfilled, following activities are to be
                      carried out:

                      • Start utilities supply to the following consumers:
                             • Cooling water supply to vapour condenser, vacuum pump unit
                               heat exchanger and purge brine cooler.
                             • Demineralised water supply for seal flushing of lean brine pump &
                               vacuum pump and bisulfite filling pump.
                      • Start both vacuum pumps 41P-07151 (07251) and 41P-07251 (07252)
                        according to manufacturer's instruction.
                        Establish required vacuum during start-up to approx. 0.4 bar a at the
                        suction of vacuum pumps and put PICAHL0710102 (0720102) in
                        AUTO.
                      • Open the bypass between pure brine header and anolyte header in the
                        cell room, thus bypassing pure brine flow to the electrolysers.
                      • When level in anolyte tank is increasing open slowly 41LV0710104
                        (41LV0720104) to fill vacuum tank. Pure brine flows from brine heat
                        exchanger → Pure brine header → Cell room Bypass → Anolyte head-
                        er → Anolyte tank → Vacuum tank.
                      • When the vacuum tank is filled up to 30 - 40% level, start the lean brine
                        pump and put controller 41LIC0710105 (0720105) in AUTO mode.
                        Also put 41LIC0710104 (0720104) on AUTO mode for level control of
                        anolyte tank. Throttle flow through cell room bypass if required.
                      • Once circulation is established and circulation through the electrolys-
                        ers is possible, the bypass valve between pure brine header and
                        anolyte header should be closed.


                      The above activities ensure complete running of the system.

                      The anolyte system of each trains is designed to operate from 100% train

5.9        PART 9: EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN

5.9.1      EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN OF UNIT
                      In case of power failure, some motor driven equipment will be de-ener-
                      gised and the brine circulation will be stopped.

                      The motor drives of the lean brine pump, vacuum pump and bisulfite filling
                      pump are connected to the emergency power system. The lean brine
                      pump will restart automatically while the other pumps have to be started
                      manually.

                      In the event of failure of vacuum dechlorination system or when dechlo-
                      rination system is not operating satisfactorily, the complete dechlorination
                      of the depleted brine (lean brine) is to be performed by bisulfite solution.
                      This is necessary for satisfactory operation of the polishing filters and ion
                      exchange resin.

                      To ensure minimum circulation at the electrolysers in case of o power fail-
                      ure for a larger period a emergency recycle is possible:

                      Lean brine pump → Pure brine head tank → Electrolysers → Anolyte
                      tank → Vacuum tank.

                      This recycle has to be started if electrolysers are still filled with chlorinated
                      anolyte and if level in the polished brine tank is too low to keep the pol-
                      ished brine pumps running. To establish the circulation the inlet of the
                      brine recuperator has to be blocked and the line to the head tank has to
                      be opened. Continue circulation until anolyte out of electrolysers is free of
                      chlorine.

6.2.1      TECHNOLOGICAL PRINCIPLES
                      12 electrolysers of type UHDE BM 2.7-163 are arranged in the cellroom
                      of each train. Each electrolyser consists of 163 single elements (20,
                      fig. 6-1) of bipolar type arranged in 12 cell racks (21).

                      The electrolyser steel structure and piping is designed to accommodate
                      5 additional single elements each, thus totalling 168 single elements per
                      electrolyser.

                      leaving the cells is depleted.

                      The chlorine gas is generated at the anode. The two-phase mixture of

                      catholyte compartment via the over flow pipe (discharge pipe) into the
                      catholyte cell header where the hydrogen gas is separated from the
                      catholyte.

6.2.1.2    Cell pressure control
                      Maintaining a constant pressure difference between the cathode and
                      anode compartment is essential for safe operation of the cells. The
                      hydrogen pressure is always kept approximately 40 mbar higher than the
                      chlorine pressure. This ensures that the membrane only touches the
                      anode and is kept in this defined state. The hydrogen pressure is
                      automatically controlled as differential pressure to the chlorine pressure.

                      In case the pressure of chlorine or hydrogen increases excessively
                      several safety measures will react:

                      • automatic valves to the waste gas dechlorination/hydrogen stack;
                      • safety valves also to the waste gas dechlorination/hydrogen stack.


                      The main pressure indicators are provided in the FCS. On every single
                      electrolyser a local U-tube-manometer is installed for local indication of
                      the pressure.

6.2.2      UNIT DESCRIPTION

6.2.2.1    Process feed headers
                      The ultra pure brine main feed header (3, fig. 6-5), provides the ultra pure
                      brine feed connection from the purified brine pump. It has a by-pass
                      connection via the anolyte cellroom by-pass with the anolyte main header
                      (1), at the end of the pipe. This flow serves to keep a partial recirculation
                      of brine in the main header in case of no electrolyser is in operation.

                      The catholyte main feed header (6) provides the catholyte to the cells. It
                      has also a by-pass connection via catholyte cellroom by-pass with the
                      catholyte main header (4). The purpose is similar to that described for the
                      feed brine.

                      The flow rates of ultra pure brine and catholyte to each electrolyser are
                      adjusted and monitored through flowmeters. For ultra pure brine feed
                      flowmeters 41FT0811101 - 41FT0812201 (...0821101 - ...0822201) and
                      for catholyte feed flowmeters 41FT0811102 - 41FT0812202 (...0821102
                      - ...0822202) are provided. These flowmeters are equipped with one low
                      flow alarm (AL) and one low low flow alarm switch (SALL). The SALL
                      alarm initiates an interlock.The interlock ramps down the load of the
                      individual electrolyser, starts a timer and finally switches the individual
                      electrolyser off (time delayed).

                      The cell feed headers for brine and catholyte are located underneath the
                      electrolyser. Each cell feed header has a connection to 4 inlet distribution
                      pipes which can be individually isolated by the inlet distribution pipe
                      isolation valves (B-is-ID and C-is-ID). Each inlet distribution pipe has 42
                      possible connection points to the single elements. Air vent valves are
                      provided at each inlet distribution pipe. Draining of one or all group of
                      single elements is done reverse through the cell feed headers which are
                      further connected to the drain main headers (for anolyte- 9; for catholyte-
                      10, s. fig. 6-5).

                      For individual filling of the electrolysers separate brine and catholyte main
                      filling headers are provided (for brine - 2; for catholyte - 5). At the
                      feedstation of every single electrolyser you can switch over from the
                      feeding to the filling lines of ultra pure brine and catholyte (upstream of
                      the respective flowmeters).

                      The draining main headers for brine (18) and catholyte (17) are
                      connected to anolyte drain tank and to the catholyte tank. Filling or
                      draining of individual electrolysers can thus be performed through these
                      main filling or main draining headers.

                      On the vent valve of the inlet distribution pipe of each electrolyser a level
                      tube can be fixed to monitor the electrolyte level in the electrolyser during
                      filling or draining.

                      The anolyte returns by gravity flow from the anolyte cell header to the

                      element, a common outlet for chlorine gas and anolyte is provided

                      element discharge pipe and anolyte cell header.

                      separated from the anolyte. The vertical header connects at the top with
                      the chlorine gas main header (13) and at the bottom with the respective
                      anolyte main header (1).

                      The catholyte returns by gravity into the catholyte tank from the catholyte
                      cell header via the catholyte main header (4). Common outlet for
                      hydrogen gas and catholyte is provided through a corrugated,
                      semitransparent hose connected between single element bottom outlet

                      headers are continuously flushed with nitrogen.

                      brine heat exchanger to fill the single elements with ultra pure brine,
                      adjusted to the process temperature by heating or cooling.

                      fill the single elements with tempered catholyte.

                      line is provided. Nitrogen can be purged into the line in order to flush the
                      hydrogen main header system prior to start-up or after shutdown of the
                      electrolysis plant. Nitrogen is automatically fed at low pressure of the
                      hydrogen main header, signalized by 41PI0810313 (41PI0820313).

                      In addition, all anolyte and catholyte cell headers are connected to the
                      nitrogen system. If an electrolyser trips the anolyte and catholyte cell
                      header of this particular electrolyser are purged with nitrogen.
                      It is imperative to ensure that nitrogen is always available.

6.2.2.3     Description of the single elements

6.2.2.3.1    Electrolysis single element design and function
                      The 163 single elements of one electrolyser are suspended in a steel
                      frame. For current transmission, the single elements of an electrolyser
                      are pressed against the fixed contact points of the frame by means of a
                      preloaded clamping device. The piping is located underneath the cells.


                      The cell elements are of the so-called single element design, the half-
                      shells being welded to the electrodes. Titanium is used for the anodes
                      and nickel for the cathodes (s. fig. 6-7).

                      The brine and the catholyte are admitted at the bottom of the single

                      detrimental effect.

                      Each single element is sealed at the flange by bolting, and insulated to
                      preclude current transmission. The contacts required for current
                      transmission are located outside the electrolytes and only minor
                      compressive forces are necessary to transmit the current to the
                      neighbouring single elements.

                      This design ensures that the housing and electrode are at the same
                      potential, whereby corrosion within the single element is prevented.

                      Some chemical reactions can be made to occur, via ionic mechanism, by
                      the application of electric energy to a suitably conceived reactor system
                      called electrochemical cell.

                      Central to the operation of any single elements is the occurrence of ionic
                      reactions which produce or consume electrons at isolated phases on the
                      single element. These phases are called electrodes, and must be good
                      electric conductors. In operation, a single element (or a series of single
                      elements) is connected to an external voltage source (rectifier unit), and
                      charge is transferred by electrons between electrodes through the
                      external circuit.

                      The electric circuit through the single element is completed by
                      electrolytes which support charge transfer by ionic conduction.
                      The electrode at which an electron-producing ionic reaction occurs
                      (e.g., Cl-  1/2 Cl2 + e-) is the anode; the electrode at which an electron
                      consuming reaction occurs (e.g., H2O + e- 1/2 H2 + OH-) is called the
                      cathode. The direction of electron flow in the external circuit is always
                      from anode (+) to cathode (-).

6.2.2.4    Principles of the membrane process
                      The ion exchange membrane itself is the heart of the single element
                      system. It acts as partition between the anode and the cathode
                      compartment of the single element. The effectiveness of the membrane
                      as a separation device between the anode and the cathode
                      compartments defines the current efficiency of the single element. The
                      chemical composition of the membrane, based on fluorocarbon matrices,
                      defines the range of catholyte concentration at which an optimum
                      operating performance is given.

                      Membranes are currently available to produce catholyte concentrations
                      around 32 % NaOH with optimum performance. The physical and
                      electrochemical properties and ion exchange capability can vary widely.
                      A minimum of 3 years life expectancy are routinely quoted from an
                      economical standpoint.

                      The ion exchange membrane is impermeable for liquid and gas. It is
                      selectively permeable to Na+-cations and the passage of OH- -ions back
                      into the anode compartment is blocked, thus allowing a high current
                      efficiency (Ce).

                      The membrane effectively allows the passage of Na+-cations only and
                      prevents almost completely the diffusion of anions from the anode
                      compartment to the cathode compartment, thereby making it possible to
                      obtain caustic soda of a very high purity.

                      One Faraday of electricity produces one half equivalent of Cl2
                      (theoretically, when no oxygen is discharged on the anode, and when
                      feed brine is acidified) in the anode compartment and one half equivalent
                      of H2 and current efficiency equivalent of NaOH in the cathode
                      compartment. The value of current efficiency, becomes a determining
                      factor in the economics of the ion exchange membrane process.


                      In practice alkaline feed brine, i.e. without addition of HCl, is supplied to
                      the single element. In that case one Faraday of electricity will produce
                      less than one half equivalent of Cl2 in the anode compartment. This is
                      because a small amount of electricity is consumed by the discharge of
                      OH- anions at the anode to form oxygen. Chlorine gas will thus contain
                      about 1.5 vol.% O2. However it is not possible in practice to avoid O2
                      generation at the anode completely. Even adding the equivalent amount


                                                          Doc. ID-Code                          Rev.

                                                 PVC Arvand
                                               Operating Manual

                              of HCl necessary to neutralize the total amount of OH- which migrates
                              from the cathode to the anode compartment, the oxygen content in
                              chlorine cell gas may not be less than about 0.2 vol.%. This depends on
                              the electrocatalytic properties of the anode activation layer too.

                              In addition, a small part of the chlorine generated in the anode
                              compartment is transformed to hypochlorite (OCl-) and chlorate (ClO3-)
                              anions in case a sufficient amount of OH- anions are present in the
                              anolyte. When the anolyte from the cells is acidified outside the cell with
                              the equivalent amount of HCl, the transformed amount of chlorine is
                              recovered back.




6.2.2.4.1         Electrolyser load and protection
Current flow                  The capacity of the whole plant depends on the load of the electrolysers.
                              Each electrolyser has its own rectifier, enabling control of load to each
                              electrolyser.



Polarisation rectifier        Each electrolyser is supplied with a polarisation rectifier, connected to the
                              bus bars inside the switches. The polarisation rectifier feeds a small
                              amount of current (approx. 27 A) to the electrolyser to prevent damage to
                              the cathode coating in the presence of chlorine (shut down conditions). A
                              diode prevents reverse current flow into the polarisation rectifier when the
                              main rectifier is running.



Feed of electrolytes to       According to the load the flow of electrolytes to the electrolysers have to
the electrolysers             be adjusted. The feeds are indicated by flow indicators.

                              A minimum flow is necessary to ensure good flow distribution to each
                              single element.

                              As the flow of electrolytes is essential and current feed without insufficient
                              feed is dangerous these flowmeters are interlocked with cell switches/
                              rectifier unit.

                      Despite the fact that, standard electrode potential for this reaction is +

                      of O2 are formed. This is due to the high oxygen overpotential at the
                      anode coating by which the discharge potential of O2 is higher than that
                      of the Cl2.

                      The rate of O2 generation depends on the available concentration of OH-
                      ions in the anolyte, i.e. on the pH-value. At low cell current efficiencies,
                      i.e. when higher amounts of OH- migrate into the anode compartment,
                      the pH-value increases, thus also oxygen and chlorate formation.

                      When a production of chlorine cell gas with low content of oxygen is
                      required, the feed brine to the electrolysers must be acidified in order to
                      reduce the pH-value of the electrolyte in the anode compartment.
                      Simultaneously the chlorate generation in the single element is
                      minimized, which implies the advantage that less chlorate must be
                      destroyed outside the single element. Disadvantage of feed brine
                      acidification is the danger of anolyte overacidification (pH min. 2) with
                      harmful consequences for the membrane. In that case more control and
                      monitoring of this system is necessary.

6.2.3.2    Electricity requirements and production rate
                      The quantitative relation between the amount of product separated at the
                      electrodes and the amount of electrical current passing through a
                      electrolytic solution is given by the two fundamental laws of Faraday,
                      which are the basis of all electrochemical calculations:

                      1. The quantities of substances liberated at the electrodes are directly
                         proportional to the quantity of electricity passing through the
                         electrolyte.
                      2. The masses of different substances liberated by the same quantity
                         of electricity are in the proportions of their chemical equivalents.

                      It was found that the quantity of electricity which is needed to separate
                      one mol of substance from an electrolytic conductor is
                      96485 ampereseconds. Consequently, a quantity of electricity of 96485
                      ampereseconds will liberate, theoretically

                      • 0.5 mol Cl2 = 35.453 grams of chlorine
                      • 1 mol NaOH = 39.997 grams of sodium hydroxide
                      • 0.5 mol H2 = 1.0079 grams of hydrogen

                      In practice, electricity requirements for the electrolysis of alkaline
                      chlorides are not expressed in terms of ampereseconds, but in terms of
                      kilo-ampere-hours, i.e. 3.6 x 106 ampere-seconds (26.8 kAh per kg-
                      equivalent).

6.2.3.3    Cell voltage
                      The operating cell voltage is substantially higher than the equilibrium or
                      decomposition voltage obtained from theoretical considerations.

                      The cell voltage may be expressed as several components:

                      • decomposition voltage, ∆E
                      • anode overpotential
                      • cathode overpotential
                      • structural voltage drop (ohmic loss)
                      • electrolyte and gas voltage drop (ohmic loss)
                      • membrane voltage drop (ohmic loss + membrane polarisation)


                      The decomposition voltage is a thermodynamic quantity, the energy
                      required to decompose an aqueous solution of sodium chloride into
                      chlorine, hydrogen and sodium hydroxide. It is independent of single
                      element design, electrodes, current density, etc. and is typically 2.24 V at
                      90 °C.

                      The anodic and cathodic overpotentials represent the additional energy
                      (voltage) above the decomposition voltage, necessary to make the
                      reaction proceed at a practical rate.



                      The cell voltage also includes a number of ohmic or resistive losses, due
                      to the passage of electricity through

                      • the metal structure
                      • the gas-filled electrolytes
                      • the membrane (separator).

                      A numeric example of the contribution of these several components to the

                      Uhde single element (activated Ni-cathodes) at 5 kA/m², 90 °C, 32 %
                      NaOH, 210 g/l NaCl

                      • Decomposition voltage                                                approx. 2.24 V
                      • Anode overpotential                                                  approx. 0.06 V
                      • Cathode overpotential                                                approx. 0.07 V
                      • Structural and contact voltage drop                                  approx. 0.04 V
                      • Electrolyte and gas voltage drop (1.2 mm gap)                        approx. 0.13 V
                      • Membrane voltage drop (Flemion F 8020)                               approx. 0.48 V

                      Total cell voltage drop                                                           3.02 V

                      This is because some components of the cell voltage, specially the
                      cathode overvoltage, does not increase linear with the current density
                      (s. fig. 6-9).

                      However, at current densities above 1.5 kA/m² the relation is quite linear
                      by which the dependence of the operating cell voltage with the current
                      density (i) can be expressed for practical purpose quite well as:

                             U single element = Uo + k i



                      In this case Uo is not equal to decomposition voltage ∆E (s. page 346),
                      but will be a higher value.



                      The values for Uo and k depend on the different single element
                      parameters and electrolysis conditions described above.

                      Typical values measured in a commercial cell plant equipped with Uhde
                      bipolar single elements are as follows:

                             Uo = 2.39 V

                             k = 0.126 V m2 /kA



                      These values correspond to activated Ni cathodes, 1.2 mm electrode
                      gap, membrane type Flemion F 8020, 32 % NaOH, 210 g NaCl/l, and
                      90 °C temperature.

                      For example the real cell voltage, measured from cathode to the
                      neighbouring element cathode is calculated

                             5 kA/m2 : U single element = 2.39 + 0.126 x 5 = 3.02 V

                      operating conditions. If the measurements are done at different
                      temperatures, concentrations and current densities, correction factors
                      must be applied.

                      For example a cell voltage is measured at 33 % NaOH and 85 °C. To
                      refer this value to 32 % NaOH and 90 °C a corrective value of

                      • Correction for concentration from 33 to 32 %wt NaOH:                            -0.033 V
                      • Correction for temperature from 85 to 90 °C:                                    -0.080 V

                      Correction for temperature and concetration:                                      - 0.113 V



                      Thus, 0.113 V has to be deducted from the measured value.

6.6.2.1.1    Procedure for "Off-Load Pinhole Detection - Bubble Test I"
                      Before carry out any action on the electrolyzer / plant, read the operating
                      procedure carefully and if you are not fully understaning the procedure,

                      unclear to you.

                      This test is to check the amount of pinholes in each element in an empty

6.6.2.1.2    Procedure for "Off-Load Pinhole Detection - Bubble Test II"
                      Before carry out any action on the electrolyzer / plant, read the operating
                      procedure carefully and if you are not fully understaning the procedure,
                      you are not allowed to start. First clarify with your shift leader anything
                      unclear to you.

                      ONLY if the procedure is clear to you, you are allowed to proceed.

                      The purpose of the bubble test II is to find out, whether there are pinholes
                      in the gas zone of the membranes, when the single elements are filled
                      with electrolytes. The bubble test II is carried out, when:

                      • It results from "Bubble test I” (s. chapter 6.6.2.1.1, page 371). Only the
                        single elements, which have bubbled between 75 and 120 seconds,
                        have to be checked.
                      • The H2-concentration in the Cl2-gas rises during operation or when the
                        H2-concentration in the Cl2-gas exceeds 0.1 vol% at 1.8–2.2 kA/elec-
                        trolyzer. In this case all single elements of the concerning electrolyzer
                        have to be checked.

6.6.2.1.3    Procedure for the "On-Load Pinhole Detection - Voltage Test"
                      Before carry out any action on the electrolyzer / plant, read the operating
                      procedure carefully and if you are not fully understaning the procedure,
                      you are not allowed to start. First clarify with your shift leader anything
                      unclear to you.

                      ONLY if the procedure is clear to you, you are allowed to proceed.

                      Pinholes can cause low voltages due to the fact that penetrating caustic
                      causes the anolyte pH to rise to such a level that water electrolysis takes
                      place at a lower anode potential.

                      The water electrolysis rate is only considerably increased above pH > 7
                      and the voltage decreases accordingly.

                      The "On-Load Pinhole Detection - Voltage Test" is not sufficiently
                      sensitive if the anolyte compartment is not free of chlorine before start-up
                      because backflowing OH--ions react to hypochlorite and to chlorate so
                      that the pH value remains low (pH < 7).

                      Normally the anolyte colour is yellow-greenish (chlorine). But in case of a
                      considerable pinhole the catholyte will flow into the anolyte compartment
                      and the anolyte overflow will be colourless because the produced
                      chlorine will be absorbed in the course of the subsequent hypochlorite
                      formation.


                                          On-Load Pinhole Detection - Voltage Test

                              1.8–2.2 kA/electrolyzer

6.6.2.1.6        Polarization Test (Short circuit test)
                         Before carry out any action on the electrolyzer / plant, read the operating
                         procedure carefully and if you are not fully understanding the procedure,
                         you are not allowed to start. First clarify with your shift leader anything
                         unclear to you.

                         ONLY if the procedure is clear to you, you are allowed to proceed.


Purpose                  This test is to detect rough problems with elements or cabling before
                         starting up the main rectifier. Such rough problems are short circuit or
                         false wiring from element to junction box/multiplexer. In addition those
                         elements having minor differences compared to an average element can
                         be detected and must be observed more carefully during the start-up of
                         the electrolyzer.

6.6.2.1.7     Analytical tests and analytical indicators
                       The frequency and limited values of the analytical tests and indicators
                       should be taken from chapter 6.13.1, page 590.

Tests                  Tests:

                              a) H2 in Cl2
                                 A high content is an indication for a hole in the gas zone of the
                                 membrane.
                                 Shut down and proceed bubble test II if the content of H2 in
                                 Cl2 > 0.1 % vol/vol at 2.7 kA electrolyser.
                              b) O2 in Cl2
                                 A high content is an indication for a hole in the liquid zone of the
                                 membrane.
                                 Shut down and proceed Low load test if the content of O2 in
                                 Cl2 > 2.5 % vol/vol at more than 2.7 kA/electrolyser.


Indicators             Indicators:

                              a) H2 in the gas mixture in the catholyte cell header can be an indica-
                                 tor for a leakage of the catholyte cell header isolation valve when
                                 the electrolyser is disconnected from the main system.
                              b) NaCl in NaOH (32 %wt)
                                 A high content is a indication for a hole in the membrane.
                                 Shut down and investigate, if the NaCl content > 100 ppm in NaOH
                                 at >10 kA/electrolyser.
                              c) NaOCl and NaClO3 in anolyte
                                 A high content of NaOCl and NaClO3 in anolyte in combination
                                 with high content of O2 in Cl2 is a indication for a hole in the mem-
                                 brane. Shut down and contact Uhde for further instructions. Inform
                                 Uhde about the level of the above mentioned values.
                              d) Anolyte pH
                                 A high anolyte pH is a indication for a hole in the liquid zone of the
                                 membrane. When catholyte flows into the anolyte compartment of
                                 the single element during normal operation the anolyte pH is about
                                 2.3-4.5. If the value exceeds pH 6 at >4 kA/electrolyser or pH 5 at
                                 >10 kA/electrolyser, shut down and contact Uhde for further in-
                                 structions. Inform Uhde about the level of the above mentioned va-
                                 lues.

                                                             Doc. ID-Code                          Rev.
 Copyright 2005 Uhde GmbH                              8408205-CB-PR-MNL-0102                       02
                                         PVC Arvand
                                       Operating Manual
                                                                        National Petrochemical comany
                 SAZE H

Job Code:        PVC Arvand        Job Code:                         Owner Job Code: PVC Arvand
                                                                                       Page 395 of 967


Explanation           Explanation:

                      Pinholes can cause increased back flow of caustic soda from the cathode
                      to the anode side. This increases the formation of by-products.

                      Pinholes in the gas zone will lead to H2 transport from the catholyte to the
                      anolyte compartment, which may be checked by measuring the H2
                      content of chlorine. The sensitivity of the analytical test a) is higher at low
                      load (e.g. 0-2.7 kA/electrolyser) compared to normal operation level since
                      less chlorine is produced, but H2 transport is independent of the
                      electrolyser load because the differential pressure remains the same.

6.6.3.2    E-STATE ELECTROLYZER to D-STATE procedure:
           Heating-up of a single electrolyzer
                      Before carry out any action on the electrolyzer / plant, read the operating
                      procedure carefully and if you are not fully understaning the procedure,
                      you are not allowed to start. First clarify with your shift leader anything
                      unclear to you.

                      ONLY if the procedure is clear to you, you are allowed to proceed.

                      Check that the electrolyzer is as defined in the E-STATE
                      ELECTROLYZER (chapter 6.6.1.2, page 361). If not, this procedure is not
                      allowed to be performed.

                      Procedure can be carried out for one or two electrolyzer(s) at the same
                      time.

6.6.3.3     Start-up of the cellroom or of a single electrolyser

6.6.3.3.1    D-STATE to C INTERMEDIATE ELECTROLYZER procedure:
             Start-up of a single electrolyzer to low load
                      Before carry out any action on the electrolyzer / plant, read the operating
                      procedure carefully and if you are not fully understaning the procedure,
                      you are not allowed to start. First clarify with your shift leader anything
                      unclear to you.

                      ONLY if the procedure is clear to you, you are allowed to proceed.

                      Check that the electrolyzer is as defined in the D-STATE (chapter 6.6.1.2,
                      page 361). If not, this procedure is not allowed to be performed.

                      This procedure is used for the start-up of one or more electrolyzer(s)
                      while at least one electrolyzer is already producing.

                      In exceptional plant shutdowns (e.g. loss of instrument air, FCS
                      interruption) with a differential pressure > 100 mbarg or < -20 mbarg the
                      Membrane Tear Test (chapter 6.6.2.1.8, page 396) has to be carried out
                      on each electrolyzer before restart.

                      Procedure can be carried out for one or more electrolyzer(s) in parallel
                      and/or subsequently as described in the following.

                              rectifier cooling and all other

                              stable.

6.6.3.3.2     B-STATE to C INTERMEDIATE CELL ROOM procedure:
              Start-up of the cell room to low load
                      Before carry out any action on the electrolyzer / plant, read the operating
                      procedure carefully and if you are not fully understaning the procedure,
                      you are not allowed to start. First clarify with your shift leader anything
                      unclear to you.

                      ONLY if the procedure is clear to you, you are allowed to proceed.

                      Check that the cell room is as defined in the B-STATE (chapter 6.6.1.2,
                      page 361). If not, this procedure is not allowed to be performed.

                      In exceptional plant shutdowns (e.g. loss of instrument air, FCS
                      interruption) with a differential pressure > 100 mbarg or < -20 mbarg the
                      Membrane Tear Test (s. chapter 6.6.2.1.8, page 396) has to be carried
                      out on each electrolyzer before restart.

6.7.1.6    D-STATE to B-STATE procedure:
           Intergration of an ELECTROLYZER to the main circulation system
                      Before carry out any action on the electrolyzer / plant, read the operating
                      procedure carefully and if you are not fully understaning the procedure,
                      you are not allowed to start. First clarify with your shift leader anything
                      unclear to you.

                      ONLY if the procedure is clear to you, you are allowed to proceed.

                      Check that the electrolyzer is as defined in the D-STATE
                      (chapter 6.6.1.2, page 361). If not, this procedure is not allowed to be
                      performed.

6.7.2      TROUBLE SHOOTING

6.7.2.1    Fault state diagnosis
                      Errors are monitored in the control room by FCS

                      Alarm messages are displayed at the screen.

                      Alarm messages are only displayed for as long as they are impending.

                      You acknowledge the alarm messages by touching the individual
                      messages.




6.7.2.2    Running of the plant in safe condition
                      All controllers are in the range, no alarm message is impending.

                      High and low alarms for every controller are indicated. If one of the alarms
                      is displayed the operator must react.

                      If the alarm messages can not be eliminated or if there are further
                      problems the interlocks will cause the accordant shut-downs, refer to
                      chapter 6.9.1.1, page 558.

6.7.2.3         Faults of the electrolysis
                            The following table describes upset conditions of the electrolysis that are
                            considered to be serious.

                            Interlocks as described above (s. chapter 6.9.1.1, page 558) protect the
                            electrolysis cells from damage. In case of an upset, however, there is
                            usually time enough for operators to eliminate the problem. The
                            necessary actions are summarized in the following table.

6.7.2.4        Reduce the NaCl concentration of the ultra pure brine
                        For reducing the NaCl concentration of the ultra pure brine you have the
                        following two options:

                        1. reduce the NaCl concentration in the filling line
                        2. reduce the NaCl concentration in the feeding line




                        Reduce NaCl concentration in filling line

Filling line            1. Check the flow meter 41FI0810503 (41FI0820503).
                        2. If the flow rate is too low adjust flowrate by hand valves in
                           demineralized water feeding line.




                        Reduce NaCl concentration in feeding line

Feeding line            Increase the bypass flow from lean brine to raw brine: check the controller
                        41DIC0200101, switch over to manual mode and increase the feed rate.

6.7.2.5        Increase the NaCl concentration of the ultra pure brine
                        For adjustin the NaCl concentration of the ultra pure brine there are two
                        options:

                        1. increase the NaCl concentration in the filling line.
                        2. increase the NaCl concentration in the feeding line.



                        Increase NaCl concentration in the filling line

Filling line            1. Check the flow meter 41FI0810503 (41FI0820503).
                        2. If the flow rate is too high adjust flow rate by hand valves in
                           demineralized water feeding line.




                        Increase NaCl concentration in the feeding line

Feeding line            Reduce the bypass flow from lean brine to raw brine: check the controller
                        41DIC0200101, switch over to manual mode and reduce the feed rate.



6.7.2.6        Conduct in total power supply failure
                        In case of a total power supply failure the plant will stop instantly. In this
                        case various interlocking devices avoid a dilution of the caustic in the
                        electrolysis cells.

                        If brine and caustic circulation are stopped, the pure brine and caustic
                        from corresponding head tanks will still flow and replace the gas volume
                        in the elements until overflow occurs. After about 5 min. both tanks are
                        empty. The free volume in the anolyte tank and catholyte tank is big
                        enough to collect the volume of the head tanks.




                                                            Doc. ID-Code                          Rev.
 Copyright 2005 Uhde GmbH                             8408205-CB-PR-MNL-0102                       02
                                         PVC Arvand
                                       Operating Manual
                                                                       National Petrochemical comany
                 SAZE H
                 C O NSU LTANTS              C/A Plant                 Arvand Petrochemical
                                                                            Company
Uhde Project No: 03-3039           Sazeh Project No: 8047           Owner Project No: 8408205
Job Code:        PVC Arvand        Job Code:                        Owner Job Code: PVC Arvand
                                                                                      Page 471 of 967


                      Proceed as follows:

                      • As soon as the rectifier current is cut off (by total power supply failure)
                        the interlock signal shall close demineralized water to the caustic cir-
                        culation.
                        Check if water flow is interrupted; if not, close manually.
                      • Ensure that polarisation rectifier is in proper operation after diesel has
                        started.
                      • Check if nitrogen purges to the anolyte and catholyte main/cell hea-
                        ders are on. If not, start purge from FCS (from field).
                      • Check the purging valves N2-pu-CH and N2-pu-AH. They must be
                        open. If not open them manually by pressing the push buttons on the
                        service gangway in the cellroom.
                      • Check the overflow of the single elements. If not, check the level of the
                        head tank, establish brine and caustic circulation.
                        It can be started with emergency power for filling the head tanks.
                      • Stop brine and caustic feed when the single elements overflow normal-
                        ly.
                      • If the hydrogen pressure is < 30 mbar, nitrogen purge to hydrogen sy-
                        stem starts automatically by interlock.
                      • Check if emergency power supplied pumps have started and establish
                        ultra pure brine flow of 20 m³/h and a caustic flow of 20 m³/h per elec-
                        trolyser.
                      • For dechlorination of brine adjust bisulphite addition.
                      • If the expected time for shutdown is < 4 h and > 1 h, monitor the catho-
                        lyte concentration. Do not allow caustic concentration to fall below
                        25 %.
                        Maintain caustic flow or flush occasionally with fresh caustic.
                        Check concentration periodically.
                      • Before restart heat up to 70 °C.

                      Please also refer to chapter 5.9, page 317 establishing for emergency bri-
                      ne circulation.

6.7.2.7    Conduct in case of control loop failure
                      A control loop failure can e.g be caused by a cable break. An accordant
                      message will be displayed in the FCS. The affected valve will run to
                      failsave position.



6.7.2.8    Defective positioner (control valves)
                      If the positioners are defective there is no indication in the FCS.

                      You recognize a defective positioner by exceptional process parameters
                      which emerge in consequence of the defective position of the valve, e.g.
                      at a heat exchanger the steam valve is closed (0% in the FCS) but
                      temperature increases.



6.7.2.9    Defective limit switches
                      Possible reasons for a defective limit switch can be cable break or a
                      damage at the limit switch itself.

                      At normal operation the limit switch gives a signal between 4 - 20 mA. If
                      the limit switch is defective, no signal will be given (0 mA). An accordant
                      message „Limit switch out of order“ will be displayed in the FCS.

                      All limit switches feature failsave-design.

6.7.2.10   Indicators for damages within the single element or electrolyser
                      Beside the tests (s. chapter 6.13.2, page 593) there are chemical and
                      physical indicators for damages within the single element and/or the
                      electrolyser.



                      Indicator for membrane damages in liquid phase:

                             a) high element voltage (done by operator or electrical engineer)
                             b) dynamic voltage change (dU/dt-interlock, apparent in the FCS)
                             c) total electrolyser voltage alarm (US++ interlock, apparent in the
                                FCS)
                             d) differential voltage (apparent in the FCS)
                             e) colour of anolyte overflow (observation in the cellroom by operator)
                             f) anolyte pH (sampling in the cellroom, apparent in the FCS)
                             g) NaCl in NaOH (sampling in the cellroom)
                             h) NaOCl and NaClO3 in anolyte (sampling in the cellroom)


                      Indicator for false operation:

                             a) NaCl in anolyte (sampling in the cellroom)
                             b) NaOH concentration (sampling in the cellroom)

6.7.3.1.4    Maximum brine impurities for operation
                      Impurities!
                      Impurities can interfere with the function of the electrolysis!

                      The maximum impurity levels shall not be exceeded.

                      Be aware of the following facts.

                      Soluble impurities in the anolyte can diffuse into the membrane, assisted
                      by the electric field and/or water transport through the membrane.

                      The impurities may pass harmlessly through the membrane or selectively
                      displace sodium in the membrane‘s functional unit, thereby reducing the
                      number of active sites available for sodium and potassium ion transport.

                      The impurities may precipitate and physically disrupt the membrane.
                      Some compounds (like earth alkalimetal cations M++) that are soluble in
                      the acidic anolyte form insoluble compounds in an alkaline environment.
                      Since the membrane is relatively alkaline, precipitation of insoluble salts
                      or complexes can occur in membrane, often near the cathode side
                      surface which is the current efficiency controlling layer. The precipitated
                      material permanently damages the membrane and causes an irreversible
                      decline in current efficiency.

                      Performance will be reduced during brine purity upsets, and the original
                      performance will not be completely recovered after return to normal
                      conditions. Return to normal ultra pure brine purity will not restore original
                      performance. Damage from multiple upsets is cumulative.

                      • Do not exceed the maximum impurity levels! The following table outli-
                        nes limits, effects on operation and control of key ultra pure brine im-
                        purities (s. table 6-8, page 481).
                      • Take notice of maximum impurity levels according to sampling sche-
                        dule.

6.7.3.1.5    Maximum impurities for operation and circulation
                      Impurities!
                      The impurities can cause damage the anode or cathode coating. Some
                      of the impurities e.g. organic components are catalyst toxins or can
                      damage the catalyst by chemical reaction.

                      The maximum impurity levels must not be exceeded.

                      Be aware of following facts.

                      Soluble impurities in the anolyte or catholyte can move through the
                      membrane by diffusion. Especially during shut down, and circulation
                      without electrical field, the impurities can pass the membrane.

                      The plant can circulate with brine and caustic as long as the impurities are
                      within the limits.

                      • For shut down and circulation monitor and record all impurities accor-
                        ding to the sampling schedule.
                      • If one or more caustic impurities are beyond the limits, add fresh cau-
                        stic to the system to dilute the impurity.
                      • For initial start-up analyze the caustic before filled into the catholyte sy-
                        stem and check all levels of impurities regularly.
                      • If the impurities are not within the limits (s. table 6-9, page 485) drain
                        all electrolyzers.
                      • Do not exceed the maximum impurity levels! The following table inclu-
                        des the maximum allowed impurities and limits in concentration of bri-
                        ne and catholyte.

6.7.3.2     Check points

6.7.3.2.1    Checks in the cell room
                      Risk of death from electrical current in the cell room!
                      Risk of electric shock!

                      • Do not touch parts of different potentials.
                      • Do not simultaneously touch a valve and live parts.
                      • Pay attention to the measures described in detail in chapter 4.5.1,
                        page 5.


                      Toxic, corrosive harmful substances!
                      Risk of serious injury or even death!

                      • Wear eye/face protection!
                      • Wear acid-resistant gloves (sulfuric acid) / neoprene or PVC gloves
                        (caustic soda).
                      • Wear suitable protective clothing.

6.7.4      REDUCED CAPACITY OPERATION
                      This plant section has been designed to operate at max. 100 % load to a
                      minimum turn down of 40 %.

                      During load reduction adjust flow rates of ultra pure brine and caustic
                      according to table 6-6, page 476.

                      In the annex you find the operation data sheets.

                      Fill in the following operation data sheets and file them for 10 years.

                      Furthermore please feed the data into the data base „Management
                      program for assembly and operating data obtained in Uhde chloralkali
                      membrane electrolysis plants“ and send them regularly back to the Uhde
                      GmbH according to the contractual agreements.

6.8        PART 8: NORMAL SHUTDOWN

6.8.1      NORMAL SHUTDOWN

6.8.1.1    A-STATE to B-STATE procedure: Shut-down of the cell room
                      Before carry out any action on the electrolyzer / plant, read the operating
                      procedure carefully and if you are not fully understaning the procedure,
                      you are not allowed to start. First clarify with your shift leader anything
                      unclear to you.
                      ONLY if the procedure is clear to you, you are allowed to proceed.

                      Check that the cell room is as defined in the A-STATE (chapter 6.6.1.2,
                      page 361). If not, this procedure is not allowed to be performed.

                      The A-STATE (plant is in operation) is the starting point for a planned
                      shutdown of all electrolyzers. If the expected shutdown time is less than
                      or equal to 4 hours the electrolyzers are kept hot at min. 75 °C in
                      circulation and with the polarization rectifiers kept switched on.

                      If the expected shutdown time is longer than 4 hours or the ultra pure
                      brine or the catholyte supply has to be stopped, bring the plant to E-
                      STATE CELL ROOM and see B-STATE to E-STATE CELL ROOM
                      procedure (chapter 6.8.1.1.1, page 515).

                      In exceptional plant shutdowns (e.g. loss of instrument air, FCS
                      interruption) with a differential pressure greater than 100 mbarg or lower
                      than -20 mbarg the Membrane Tear Test has to be carried out on each
                      electrolyzer before restart. For Membrane Tear Test please refer to
                      chapter 6.6.2.1.8, page 396

6.8.1.1.1    B-STATE to E-STATE CELL ROOM:
             Cooling of all electrolyzers without draining
                      Before carry out any action on the electrolyzer / plant, read the operating
                      procedure carefully and if you are not fully understaning the procedure,
                      you are not allowed to start. First clarify with your shift leader anything
                      unclear to you.
                      ONLY if the procedure is clear to you, you are allowed to proceed.

                      Check that the cell room is as defined in the B-STATE (chapter 6.6.1.2,
                      page 361). If not, this procedure is not allowed to be performed.

                      If the impurities in ultra pure brine and caustic are within the limits of the
                      specification for circulation without current (chapter 6.7.3.1.5, page 484)
                      and if the expected shutdown time of the brine and/or of the caustic
                      circulation is more than 4 hours and less than 24 hours, bring the plant to
                      E-STATE CELL ROOM.

                      If these requirements cannot be met, bring each electrolyzer via E-
                      STATE CELL ROOM / ELECTROLYZER to F-STATE.

                      If the expected shut down time of the brine circulation is greater than 24
                      hours or if the expected shut down time of the caustic circulation is
                      greater than 24 hours or the ultra pure brine or caustic composition in the
                      cells cannot be kept within the limits of the specification for circulation
                      without current (chapter 6.7.3.1.5, page 484), then tranfer the plant via E-
                      STATE ELECTROLYZER to F-STATE ELECTROLYZER. The
                      composition in the cells can be kept within the limits for instance by
                      temporarily circulating fresh ultra pure brine or caustic into the cells. After
                      exchanging completely the volume in the cells, the cells can be
                      maintained without circulation for another 24 hours.

                      This means that the cells need to be circulated with fresh electrolytes for
                      a minimum time of 1-2 hours according to the flow table(s)
                      (chapter 6.7.3.1.2, page 476).

6.8.1.2    A-STATE to D-STATE ELECTROLYZER procedure:
           Shut-down of a single electrolyzer
                      Before carry out any action on the electrolyzer / plant, read the operating
                      procedure carefully and if you are not fully understaning the procedure,
                      you are not allowed to start. First clarify with your shift leader anything
                      unclear to you.
                      ONLY if the procedure is clear to you, you are allowed to proceed.

                      Check that the cell room is as defined in the A-STATE (chapter 6.6.1.2,
                      page 361). If not, this procedure is not allowed to be performed.

                      Procedure can be carried out for one or more electrolyzer(s) at the same
                      time. Limitation is the capacity of the drain system which may be different
                      from plant to plant. The anolyte and catholyte drain systems are designed
                      for the capacity of two electrolyzers. For shut down of more than two
                      electrolyzers or a non-working anolyte or catholyte drain system, the
                      whole plant has to be shut down. To shut down the entire plant use the
                      A-STATE to B-STATE procedure (s. chapter 6.8.1.1, page 507).

                      If the ultra pure brine or the catholyte supply has to be stopped, bring the
                      electrolyzer to E-STATE.

6.8.2      SHUTDOWN FOR LONGER PERIOD

6.8.2.1    D-STATE to E-STATE ELECTROLYZER procedure:
           Cooling down and preparing for draining of a single electrolyzer
                      Before carry out any action on the electrolyzer / plant, read the operating
                      procedure carefully and if you are not fully understaning the procedure,
                      you are not allowed to start. First clarify with your shift leader anything
                      unclear to you.
                      ONLY if the procedure is clear to you, you are allowed to proceed.

                      Check that the electrolyzer is as defined in the D-STATE
                      (chapter 6.6.1.2, page 361). If not, this procedure is not allowed to be
                      performed.

                      If the impurities in ultra pure brine and caustic are within the limits of the
                      specification for circulation without current (chapter 6.7.3.1.5, page 484)
                      and if the expected shutdown time of the brine and/or of the caustic
                      circulation to the particular electrolyzer is more than 4 hours and less than
                      24 hours, bring the plant to E-STATE ELECTROLYZER.

                      If these requirements cannot be met, bring the particular electrolyzer via
                      E-STATE ELECTROLYZER to F-STATE.

                      If the expected shutdown time of the brine circulation is greater than 24
                      hours or if the caustic circulation is greater than 24 hours or the ultra pure
                      brine or caustic composition in the cells cannot be kept within the limits of
                      the specification for circulation without current (s. chapter 6.7.3.1.5,
                      page 484), bring the ELECTROLYZER via E-STATE ELECTROLYZER
                      to F-STATE. The composition in the cells can be kept within the limits for
                      instance by temporarily circulating fresh ultra pure brine or caustic into
                      the cells. After exchanging completely the volume in the cells the cells
                      can be maintained without circulation for another 24 hours. This means
                      that the cells need to be circulated with fresh electrolytes for a minimum
                      time of 1 hour according to the flow table(s) (chapter 6.7.3.1.2, page 476).

6.8.2.4    F-STATE to F-STATE SUBCASE 2: Electrolyzer empty longer than 10 days
                      Before carrying out any action on the electrolyzer / plant, read the
                      operating procedure carefully and if you do not understand the procedure
                      completely, you are not allowed to start. First clarify with your shift leader
                      anything unclear to you.
                      ONLY if the procedure is clear to you, are you allowed to proceed.

                      Check that the electrolyzer is as defined in the state "drained electrolyzer"
                      (chapter 6.6.1.2, page 361). If not, this procedure is not allowed to be
                      performed.

                      The procedure must be carried out electrolyzer by electrolyzer. Before
                      starting this procedure Uhde Customer Service must be informed and
                      consulted for each case when this procedure is planned to be executed.
                      The procedure is going to be carried out seldom and includes water filling
                      and draining of the electrolyzers which requires temporary installations in
                      the plant and needs therefore to be planned carefully.

6.9        PART 9: EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN

6.9.1      EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN OF UNIT
                      In case of power failure, all motor driven equipment will be deenergised
                      and the brine circulation will be stopped.
                      Only pure brine from the head tank will continue to flow by gravity to the
                      cells. The following motor drives are connected to the emergency power
                      system, and these will restart on power failure .


6.9.1.1    Interlock description
                      Please refer to ANNEX A8, INTERLOCK DESCRIPTION.



6.9.1.2    Alarm settings and Interlock trip settings
                      Please refer to ANNEX A19, LIST OF THRESHOLD VALUES.

6.9.2       EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN OF UNIT DUE TO GENERAL REASONS
                      Follow procedure as outlined in chapter 6.9.1 “EMERGENCY
                      SHUTDOWN OF UNIT”.



6.9.2.1     Behaviour of the plant in the event of emergency

6.9.2.1.1    EMERGENCY SHUT-OFF switches
                      Correct functionality of these EMERGENCY-SHUT-OFF switches can be
                      of vital significance.

                      The EMERGENCY SHUT-OFF switches serve to shut-down the plant in
                      cases of emergency immediately.

                      The EMERGENCY SHUT-OFF switches are installed in following
                      positions:

                      • One EMERGENCY SHUT-OFF switch in the control room,
                      • seven EMERGENCY SHUT-OFF switches in the cell room, five swit-
                        ches on the cell house platform, two switches at the bottom of the cell
                        house.


                      In the event of an emergency, press one of the EMERGENCY SHUT-OFF
                      switches, which will activate following procedures:

                      • All rectifiers are stopped.
                      • The DC-isolators open up.
                      • Following procedures see “Interlock description“.

6.9.2.1.2    Total power failure
                      In case of a total power supply failure the plant will stop instantly. In this
                      case various interlocking devices avoid a dilution of the caustic in the
                      electrolysis cells.

                      If brine and caustic circulation are stopped, the pure brine and caustic
                      from corresponding head tanks will still flow and replace the gas volume
                      in the elements until overflow occurs. After about 5 min. both tanks are
                      empty. The free volume in the anolyte tank and catholyte tank is big
                      enough to collect the volume of the head tanks.

                      In case of total power supply failure proceed as described in
                      chapter 6.7.2.6, page 470. Please also refer to chapter 5.9.1, page 317
                      for establishing emergency brine circulation.




6.9.2.1.3    Behaviour of a single electrolyser in the event of emergency
                      If one of the EMERGENCY SHUT OFF switches is pushed

                      • the rectifier will be stopped
                      • DC-Isolators will be opened
                      • HCl valve to the electrolyser (HCl-re-FS) will be closed
                      • N2-purge valve at catholyte header (N2-pu-CH) will open; but only if
                        the isolation valves are open.
                      • N2-purge valve at anolyte header (N2-pu-AH) will open; but only if iso-
                        lation valves are open.

                      Afterwards the isolation valves can only be closed manually from the
                      gangway.

6.10       PART 10: SAFETY EQUIPMENT
                      The hazardous chemicals handled in the brine secondary system are
                      caustic soda (18 % NaOH) & hydrochloric acid (16 % HCl). All personnel
                      working with or near caustic soda & hydrochloric acid must be thoroughly
                      instructed as to the hazard involved when dealing with these chemicals.

                      All work should be performed by properly instructed personnel and under
                      experienced supervision.

                      Should an accident occur inspite of careful operation of the plant,
                      immediate first aid is imperative.

6.10.4     GENERAL SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS

6.10.4.1   General exposure
                      The plant’s construction is state-of-the-art and is built in accordance to
                      recognized safety regulations. Nevertheless, dangers for the operators or
                      other persons can occur during operation.

                      The plant is to be used only:
                      • for the intended use
                      • in technically perfect condition,
                      • and with awareness of safety and hazards.

                      When operating the plant, health-, work-, safety-, accident prevention-,
                      fire prevention- and environmental regulations currently in force need to
                      be observed. Personnel working within the plant needs to be familiar with
                      these regulations.

                      Work tasks at the plant must always be carried out with care and
                      circumspection.
                      The work shall be well planned (i. e. safe job analysis) and shall start only
                      after the release of the applicable work permits.

                      Personnel working at the plant must have access to the operating manual
                      at all times. In addition to the operating manual, customary and general
                      public rules pertaining to accident control and to safety at the workplace
                      have to be observed. All personnel assigned to work at the plant must
                      have either read the operating manual before beginning work, in
                      particular the chapter ”Safety”. This applies in particular to personnel who
                      work only occasionally with the chloralkali membrane electrolysis plant,
                      e.g. for maintenance purposes.

                      Responsibilities of the personnel need to be determined before starting
                      the work process.

                      The workplace has to be arranged and maintained in a state which allows
                      safe work. This particularly applies to the material, the spaciousness, the
                      stability, the surface, the stepping, the lighting and ventilation, and to the
                      protection from harmful environmental factors next to the custody from
                      dangers caused by other persons working at the plant too.

                      The personnel shall wear protective clothes, preventing them from

                      Emergency escape mask has to be carried all the time.

                      The wearing of jewelry and loose long hair during the work at the plant is
                      prohibited. This can lead to risks of injury.
                      Full face mask and goggles have to be carried all the time.
                      Personnel needs to be equipped with corresponding means of
                      communication in order to make themselves understood between control
                      room and plant!

                      In the event of drastic changes in the operational behaviour of the plant,
                      it needs to be stopped immediately and secured against start up. Report
                      the alteration to the management. Whenever the personnel at the plant
                      locates that the plant or the electrical installation is not working flawlessly,
                      the defect has to be repaired immediately.
                      If this does not lie within the responsibility of the personnel concerned, or
                      if the personnel has not the sufficient expert knowledge, the defect has to
                      be reported without delay.

                      Spare parts must satisfy the technical requirements specified by Uhde.
                      This is always guaranteed when genuine spare parts from Uhde GmbH
                      are used.
                      The inspection intervals specified in the maintenance manual are to be
                      observed.

                      The operator has to take care of the proper usage of the electrical
                      installations and equipment according to the electrotechnical rules.

                      The cables to be connected, have to be unambiguously and durably
                      marked, since mistakes can be a source of danger.

6.10.4.2   Intended use and unintended use

6.10.4.2.1 Intended use of the chloralkali membrane electrolysis plant
                      The chloralkali membrane electrolysis plant is designed exclusively to
                      produce chlorine and caustic soda in accordance with the Uhde single
                      cell membrane process.
                      The chloralkali membrane electrolysis plant must be operated only with
                      original equipment and spare parts by Uhde and their suppliers.
                      The chloralkali membrane electrolysis plant can only be operated in line
                      with its intended usage, if maintenance tasks are carried out regularly and
                      within the set intervals.
                      In order to use the chloralkali membrane electrolysis plant within the limits
                      of its designated use only, you need to follow the instructions set out in
                      this operating manual, in the maintenance manual and in the instructions
                      of the suppliers in their entirety.

6.10.4.2.2 Unintended use of the chloralkali membrane electrolysis plant
                      Using the chloralkali membrane electrolysis plant for purposes other than
                      those outlined in the chapter 6.10.4.2.1, page 565 is considered contrary
                      to its designated use.
                      Employment of personnel which is not sufficiently qualified is considered
                      contrary to designated use.
                      Constructional alterations at the plant and at the equipment are prohibited
                      without written permission of the manufacturer.
                      The same applies for alterations to and interference with the FCS.
                      Contravention of these prohibitions results in the expiry of the warranty.
                      Uhde cannot be held liable for any damage resulting from unintended
                      use.

6.10.4.2.3 Intended use of the electrolysis
                      The electrolysis system serves exclusively for the electrolysis of ultra
                      pure brine and caustic soda to produce chlorine gas, hydrogen gas and
                      caustic soda solution.

                      The electrolysis of other solutions or the electrolysis of brine and caustic
                      soda, when their compositions do not comply with the technical data is
                      considered contrary to its designated use.
