6.10.5.1   Handling hazardous materials

6.10.5.1.1 Danger caused by chlorine
                      The hazardous chemical handled in this system of the plant is chlorine.

                      Toxic! Danger caused by chlorine!
                      Toxic by inhalation, ingestion and through skin contact. Inhalation can
                      cause serious lung damage and may be fatal. 1000ppm (0.1%) is likely to
                      be fatal after a few deep breaths, and half that concentration fatal after a
                      few minutes. May irritate or burn skin.
                      Irritating to eyes, respiratory system and skin.

                      Observe following safety phrases:

                      • In case of accident or if you feel unwell, seek medical advice immedi-
                        ately!
                      • Wear protective gloves. Wear protective glasses!


                      Avoid release to the environment!

                      Very toxic to aquatic organisms!

6.10.5.1.9 Danger constituted by electrical current!
                      Fatal electrical voltages can occur in the cell room!

                      Danger constituted by electrical current!



                      If working on the electrolyser is required proceed as follows:

                      • For rapid unloading drain the electrolyser according to the instructions
                        in this operating manual.
                      • If working on the electrolyser is required remove the protective cover
                        only if the electrical voltage is < 120 V.
                      • If working on the electrolyser is required at impressed voltages of
                        > 60 V work tasks must only be carried out by skilled electricians wea-
                        ring appropriate personal protection equipment.


                      Please observe:

                      At unintentional contact of electrically charged areas voltages up to 120 V
                      are allowed.

                      Work tasks at live conditions without protective equipment are allowed at
                      voltages up to 60 V.

                      Observe the following dangers:

                      1. Simultaneously contact of a shutdown and a neighbouring running
                         electrolyser!
                         One person could touch the end of the operating electrolyser and
                             simultaneously some electrolyte (the only grounded material) of
                             the shutdown one. Mortal danger!

                      2. Simultaneously contact of two differently charged surfaces at a
                         running electrolyser.
                         If somebody spreads his arms, his span may be 1.5 m and he
                         touches operating elements of one eletrolyser, he could be exposed
                         to a maximum of 60 V between his hands.

6.10.5.1.10 Danger constituted by explosion!
                      Chlorine and hydrogen are produced together in two separate
                      compartments of the single element and can lead, if mixed, to form
                      explosive mixture. Also oxygen and hydrogen can lead, if mixed, to form
                      explosive mixture. Therefore special care is to be taken to keep these
                      chemicals apart from each other.

                      In case of explosion additional danger is caused by huge amounts of
                      spraying caustic soda and brine and by flying around objects!

6.10.5.2   Unit safeguarding system

6.10.5.2.1 Protective devices
                      The protective devices serve health and safety of the personnel working
                      on the plant and also protect the plant against damage.

                      Correct functionality of these protective devices is vital.

                      It is therefore essential that the operator/maintenance pesonnel check
                      the protective devices' functionality, as described in the maintenance
                      manual.

                      The chloralkali membrane electrolysis plant is equipped with the following
                      protective devices:

                      • EMERGENCY SHUT-OFF switches
                      • interlocks
                      • protective covers above rotating parts of pumps, above the compres-
                        sor and to the sides of each electrolyser

                      Prior to commissioning the plant, you have to ensure that all protective
                      devices are mounted and fully functional.

                      The plant must not be operated, if one or more of the originally mounted
                      protective devices were dismounted or if they were rendered inoperative.

                      The protective devices may only be removed

                      • after complete shutdown and
                      • when the plant is depressurized and
                      • after having secured the plant against inadvertent start-up.

6.10.5.2.2 Chlorine detectors
                      One relevant hazardous gas being handled in the plant is chlorine, which
                      constitutes a toxic hazard.

                      Chlorine detectors installed at the Arvand PVC Complex will identify
                      releases to help protect operating personnel at site and the general public
                      from chlorine exposure.

                      The detectors are not intended to monitor personnel exposure nor to
                      precisely localize or quantify leaks in the absence of other input which
                      must be provided in the diagnostic process initiated at the Main Control
                      Room of the plant upon warning or alarm signals annunciated from the
                      detectors.

                      In the cellroom there are 6 chlorine detectors each positioned 1 m above
                      the ground which are analyzing the chlorine concentration in the air.

                      Furthermore there are 3 hydrogen detectors under the roof of the
                      cellroom.




6.10.5.2.3 Insulation of the electrolysers
                      An important aspect of safety in designing an electrolyser is the electrical
                      insulation and personnel protection from any electrical shocks.

                      Each single element is equipped with a set of PTFE insulation plates
                      which are safely connected to the supporting legs. Additionally the
                      supporting beams of the steel structures are covered with a PTFE foil.

                      The pressure plates of each block are insulated against the compression
                      screws fixed in the steel structures. The steel structure itself is supported
                      on insulators.

                      The above measures are required, if the distance between two
                      electrolysers is less than the required safety range of 2.5 m.

                      Each complete electrolyser is equipped with surrounding protective

                      <120 V DC to work on the electrolyser. It is not allowed to remove the

                      gangway (within 1.25 m distance) are insulating covered against contact
                      or provided with an insulating coating.

                      It is recommended to split the gangway into reasonable sections to
                      improve the finding of earth faults if any and safety against electrical-
                      hazards.

6.10.5.2.7 Insulation of piping, earthing
                      The piping in the cellroom is mainly made from plastics.

                      Protection against indirect contact is required if materials of auxiliaries
                      can produce dangerous potentials against live parts or other conductive
                      materials of different potential in case of failure.

                      Cellroom cranes must have a minimum of 2 insulations between the hook
                      and the travelling hoist and/or insulation of the complete crane or parts
                      against earth. In this case the power supply has to have galvanic
                      separation.

                      Electrical supply systems for auxiliary and control voltages must have
                      galvanic separation.

6.10.5.2.9 Safety aspects of single element design
                      Connection of single elements in series :

                      Since the same current is passing through each single element, this
                      enables the measurement of the particular voltage across each single
                      element. Also the open contacts between two adjacent single elements
                      can be checked since this is included in the voltage from cathode pan to
                      cathode pan.

                      The cell voltage is a very valuable measurement because it indicates any
                      deviation of :

                      • current distribution
                      • electrolyte concentration by flow changes
                      • temperature
                      • gas hold ups
                      • possibility of pinholes in membranes, etc.

                      Each single element is sealed individually by flanges and bolts, which are
                      visible from outside and easily accessible.

                      Inlet and outlet hoses are provided for each single element. They are also
                      sealed individually with good visibility and access for retightening, if
                      necessary. The hoses are translucent, so that the flow can be observed.
                      This is important during start-up to ensure right from the beginning the
                      proper function of the single element. It is actually possible to distinguish
                      under low load conditions between green outlet of anolyte (normal) and
                      white, when all chlorine is absorbed by alkaline brine caused by a hole in
                      the membrane.

                      PTFE based gaskets individually sealed prevents the hazardous
                      chemicals from leaking out of the containment.

6.10.5.3   Directions of safe operation and inspection

6.10.5.3.1 Conduct in an emergency
                      In the event of an emergency, press one of the EMERGENCY SHUT-OFF
                      switches.

                      The EMERGENCY SHUT-OFF switches serve to shut-down the plant in
                      cases of emergency immediately.

                      The EMERGENCY SHUT-OFF switches are installed in following
                      positions:

                      • One EMERGENCY SHUT-OFF switch in the control room,
                      • seven EMERGENCY SHUT-OFF switches in the cell room, five swit-
                        ches on the cell house platform, two switches at the ground floor of the
                        cell house.



6.10.5.3.2 Conduct in case one single electrolyser fails
                      If a single electrolyser fails due to the interlock „Shutdown of single
                      electrolyser“ (Differential voltage deviation is high high) or due to interlock
                      i.e. I2603 „Single electrolyser load reduction“ (pure brine flow/catholyte
                      flow is low low) the current supply will be shut down, the polarisation
                      rectifier will continously operate and the N2 supply will be open.

                      In this case you must proceed as at the shutdown of a single electrolyser
                      for brief periods. Proceed as follows:

                      1. Check that the polarisation rectifier is feeding ~ 27 A.
                      2. Check that N2 is purging to anolyte and catholyte cell header:
                         The valves N2-pu-CH, N2-pu-AH must be opened by pressing the
                         push button „N2 valve open“ on the service gangway.
                      3. Reduce brine and catholyte flow of the concerned electrolyser to the
                         required flow rate (s. table 6-6, page 476).
                      4. Check acid addition to brine is stopped. The valve HCl-re-FS must
                         be closed.
                      5. Close the valve HCl-fe-FS if necessary.
                      6. Check overflow of all single elements.

6.10.5.3.3 Conduct after an emergency at the electrolysis
                      1. Reset the EMERGENCY SHUT OFF switches.
                      2. Check that no interlock signal is active.
                      3. Check that the rectifiers are ready to switch on.
                      4. Follow the regular start-up prerequisites and procedure.


6.10.5.3.4 Safety information for working on the electrical system
                      The electrical system is only to be assembled, modified and maintained
                      within the ambit of electrotechnical rules by electricians or under direction
                      and supervision of an electrician.

                      The operating voltage which is required for the system may cause fatal
                      injuries if live parts are touched.

                      A short circuit may lead to the formation of sparks and fires.

                      The system connection has to be dimensioned sufficiently in order to
                      prevent overload.

                      Switch the train of the plant off at once in the event of defects in the
                      electric supply.

                      It is prohibited to work on current-carrying active parts of the electrical
                      system.

                      Before starting work on the electrical system, switch the plant to voltage-
                      free status and secure it from being unexpectedly switched on again.

                      Adhere to the following safety regulations when carrying out work on the
                      electrical system:

                      1. Clearing
                      2. Securing the system against inadvertent switch-on.
                      3. Check that there is no voltage present
                      4. Ground and short-circuit
                      5. Cover live components


                                                          Doc. ID-Code                          Rev.

                                                                                       Page 585 of 967


                      If it is necessary to carry out adjustments, maintenance and repair work
                      at equipment and instrumentation without safety purpose while keeping
                      the system connected to the mains first switch the relevant equipment
                      over to MANUAL operating mode.

                      Only use original fuses with specified current rating.

                      The electrical system has to be and is to be kept in a secure state. The
                      installation’s electrical system must be checked periodically. Defects
                      such as loose connections etc. are to be reported and corrected
                      immediately.

                      The control cabinet and all of the system’s clamping and connector boxes
                      must always be kept closed. Access for inspection and maintenance of
                      electrical equipment is restricted to authorized personnel.

                      When protective covers have to be removed it has to be ensured that,
                      within the safety range of 2.5 m no live parts or conductive material of
                      dangerous potential difference can be contacted. The insulation of
                      gangways shall be checked regularly. According to the conditions of work
                      further safety measures have to be taken.

                      The active components of the electrical system have to be protected from
                      direct contact. This has to happen through insulation, placement,
                      arrangement or the installation of fixed facilities according to their voltage,
                      frequency, manner of use and the place where they are operating.

                      Protection against direct contact are those measures, that persons can
                      not come into contact with live parts like busbars, single element
                      elements, etc. The protection can be done in whole or in part. The latter
                      ensures only protection against accidental touching.

                      The electrical system has to have protection from indirect contact
                      according to its voltage, frequency, manner of use and the place where it
                      is operating. So that, in the case of an error occuring within the electrical
                      system, protection from dangerous shock-hazard voltages is given.

                      Protection against indirect contact are those measures, which protect
                      persons against hazards resulting from a contact to conductive materials
                      in case of insulation failures.

                      In electrochemical plants it is generally not possible due to technical and
                      operating reasons (VDE 0100, part 410 item 8.1) to avoid any direct
                      contact to live parts.

                      Therefore, one or more of the following measures have to be applied to
                      achieve a partial protection.

                      • insulation of operating gangways and walls.
                      • sufficient distance between parts of dangerous potential differences
                        without protection.
                      • installation of protective covers.
                      • covering of live parts or conductive materials and/or earth.
                      • wearing of insulating shoes (and gloves if necessary).

                      When working at live objects please observe the following instructions:

                      • Use isolated tools!
                      • You are specially trained for this work and you have been instructed
                        for the dangers, especially for the dangers of electric arcs.
                      • Wear your personal protective equipment (insulating boots, electrician
                        gloves).
                      • Before start of work put up warning signs in the cellroom and on the
                        gangways.
                      • Never work alone. Always work together with at least a second person.
                      • Before start of work ensure having necessary work permits.

6.10.5.3.5 Safety information for maintenance, set-up and fault correction
                      Carry out the maintenance tasks specified in the maintenance manual in
                      due time.

                      Maintenance, inspection and repair work may only be carried out by
                      personnel qualified to do so.

                      Adhere to the following safety regulations before carrying out
                      maintenance:

                      1. Work permit has to be given.
                      2. Be careful with the different media. Pay attention to safety
                         information to the media (s. chapter 6.10.5.1, page 568).
                      3. Make sure that the equipment is pressureless.

                      4. Before beginning maintenance, inspection or repair work, isolate
                         electrically the relevant part of the plant to voltage-free status and
                         secure it from being unexpectedly switched on again.


                      Plan your work properly and carry out safe job analysis if required.

                      If screw connections must be removed for maintenance, inspection or
                      repair, screw them in again once work has been completed and make
                      certain that they are secure.

                      Observe the applicable product safety regulations when using oils and
                      grease.

                      Once maintenance, inspection and repair work has been completed, the
                      protective devices are to be checked for operability.

    1 INTRODUCTION
                 Uhde AdministratorTM belongs to the system of Uhde IntegratorTM. Therefor it links
                 different data of the plant to achieve an integrated system to fulfill the long-term
                 needs of the clients.

                 The program comprises a relational database for the management of cell elements,
                 operating and analytical data obtained in the Uhde Chlor-Alkali Electrolysis Plant.

                 The program provides for complete documentation of the assembly, operating and
                 analytical data and for the maintenance activities required for halfshells and
                 membranes.

                 The program was developed using Microsoft Access 97.

                 Users should be familiar with personal computers and the operating systems
                 Windows 95, Windows 98; Windows NT or Windows°XP

  3.4 SEARCH FUNCTIONS
                The submenu “Search functions“ (Fig. 19) provides for simple generation of
                “Assembly data“ outputs arranged in groups according to various criteria. It is
                accessed via the main menu.




                Fig.°19: Search functions

                Some of the search functions, e. g. “Passive Elements” or “Active Elements” will
                generate the search results directly after the respective button has been clicked.
                Other queries, e. g. “Membrane Type” or “Membrane No.” open an new form, which
                allows to specify further criteria for the search.

                                  Example:      Search for anode No.

                                  Item:         A 874?

                                  Input:        A 874*

                                  Output:       A 8741 to A 8749

                Pressing the “Update Display” button will then generate the search results.

               The following search criteria (selection) are available:

                     Element Number: Input of element no. generates the complete history of the
                     particular element.

                     Anode Number: Input of the anode no. generates the complete history of the
                     component.

                     Cathode Number: Input of the cathode no. generates the complete history of
                     the component.

                     Duplicate Anodes: Search function for detecting input and installation data
                     errors (double entries etc.).

                     Duplicate Cathodes: Search function for detecting input and installation data
                     errors (double entries etc.).

                     Membrane Type: Selects elements with a certain type of membrane.

                     Membrane Number: Input of membrane no. generates the complete history of
                     the particular membrane.

                     Duplicate Membranes: Search function for detecting input and installation data
                     errors (double entries etc.).

                     Group: Searches all elements of a certain group.

                     Active Groups: Displays all groups defined by the database user.

                     Assembly date: Selects all elements assembled on a specific day.

                     Commissioning date: Selects all elements commissioned on a specific day.

                     Decommissioning date: Selects all elements decommissioned on a specific
                     day.

                     Disassembly date: Selects all elements disassembled on a specific day.

                     Assembly Remarks: Selects elements bearing a remark in this column.

               Further search criteria are available in the program.



               The submenu is closed by clicking the “Main menu“ button to return to the main
               menu (Fig. 1).

   3.5 STANDARDIZED VOLTAGE
                 The submenu “Standardized Voltage“ is accessed via the main menu (Fig. 1).




                 Fig. 20: Standardized Voltage



                 Voltage and other operating data required to calculate the standardized voltage are
                 to be entered by clicking the buttons “Data input“. Input has to be given for complete
                 electrolyzers or single elements.

                 All other buttons permit data extraction related to these inputs. These extractions
                 are classified as follows:



                        Tables and diagrams showing standardized voltages of complete electrolyzer
                        sets (Total Plant, Train, Electrolyzer, Groups or Elements)

                        Tables and diagrams showing standardized voltages of single elements

                        Tables and diagrams showing standardized voltages of groups

                The basis for calculation of the standardized voltage is given by the following
                equations:

                For NaOH plants at 6 kA/m²

                                       6
                U std = U 0 +                    * (U meas ( U 0 )
                                  CDmeas , avg
                                                          CDmeas , avg
                               ( (90 ( Tmeas , avg ) *                   * 0.020
                                                               6
                                                          CDmeas , avg
                               + (32 ( c meas , avg ) *                  * 0.040
                                                               6

                with

                Ustd                  standardised voltage [V]

                U0                    zero voltage = 2.40 V

                Umeas                 measured voltage, for single element or for entire electrolyser divided
                                      by NE [V]

                CDmeas, avg           measured average current density [kA/m2] 1)

                6                     standard current density [kA/m²]

                Tmeas, avg            measured average NaOH outlet temperature [°C]

                90                    standard NaOH outlet temperature [°C]

                cmeas, avg            measured average NaOH outlet concentration [% w/w]

                32                    standard NaOH outlet concentration [% w/w]
                1)
                     Will be practically equal for each element of an electrolyser, as stray currents are usually very low.




                For each degree below 90°C, standard voltage is decreased by 20 mV at 6 kA/m²,
                vice versa

                For each percentage point above 32 % NaOH standard voltage is decreased by
                40 mV at 6 kA/m², vice versa

               For each degree below 90°C, standard voltage is decreased by 16 mV at 5 kA/m²,
               vice versa

               standard voltage is decreased by 33 mV at 5 kA/m², vice versa

    3.6 CURRENT EFFICIENCY
                 The submenu “Current Efficiency“ is accessed via the main menu (Fig. 1).




                 Fig.°21: Current efficiency



                 Current efficiency charts and calculation results are generated for individual
                 electrolyzers by clicking the respective buttons in this submenu.

                 The current efficiency is calculated on the basis of the anodic balance and is derived
                 from the operating data entered under the submenu “Standardized Voltage” and the
                 analytical values entered under the submenu “Analyses”.

                 Caution:

                 The current efficiency can only be calculated on the basis of current, voltage and
                 analytical values measured on the same day.



                 The basis for calculation of the standardized voltage is given by the following data
                 and equations:

7.2        PART 2: DESCRIPTION OF PROCESS

7.2.1      TECHNOLOGICAL PRINCIPLES
                      The chlorine cooling systems of the electrolyser trains are designed to
                      handle a total chlorine load of 585,000 t/a of both trains and 7920 h/a. The
                      system of each train can handle 50 % of total plant load with a turn down
                      ration of 40 % of the train capacity.

                      The electrolyser trains are connected to one chlorine cooling system
                      each.

                      The chlorine gas inlet to the system is saturated with water at an over-
                      pressure of 200 mbar and temperature of approx. 88 °C.

                      The chlorine cooling system is designed to deliver the water saturated
                      chlorine gas at an overpressure of approx. 120 mbar and a temperature
                      of 15 °C.

                      In order to improve the heat balance of the electrolysis process, the en-
                      ergy is recovered first against the brine system, than cooling water and
                      finally chilled water.



7.2.2      UNIT DESCRIPTION
                      There are two electrolyser trains each connected to its own chlorine sys-
                      tem.

                      Train 1: P&I Diagram 22101

                      Train 2: P&I Diagram 22201

                      Each train of the chlorine cooling system consists of:

                      • one chlorine recuperator
                      • one chlorine cooler I
                      • one chlorine cooler II
                      • one wet chlorine filter
                      • one under pressure safety vessel.

                                                          Doc. ID-Code                          Rev.
Copyright 2005 Uhde GmbH
                                                    8408205-CB-PR-MNL-0102                       02
                                         PVC Arvand
                                       Operating Manual
                                                                       National Petrochemical comany
                 SAZE H
                 C O NSU LTANTS              C/A Plant                 Arvand Petrochemical
                                                                            Company
Uhde Project No: 03-3039           Sazeh Project No: 8047           Owner Project No: 8408205
Job Code:        PVC Arvand        Job Code:                        Owner Job Code: PVC Arvand
                                                                                      Page 640 of 967


                      Note:       Equipment numbers are for train 1, equipment numbers for
                                  train 2 are in brackets.

                      The chlorine gas saturated with water, leaving the electrolysers is at a
                      temperature of approx. 88 °C. This along with the small amount of chlo-
                      rine gas from the brine dechlorination area enters the chlorine cooling
                      chapter.

                      The chlorine gas exchanges heat with polished brine in the chlorine recu-
                      perator 41E-21104 (41E-21204). The chlorine is cooled to approx. 65 °C.

                      From the chlorine recuperator the chlorine gas enters the chlorine cooler
                      I 41E-21105 (41E-21205). Here the chlorine gas is cooled to 40 °C by
                      means of cooling water.

                      By start-up of the plant, when the chlorine content is less and if the cell
                      pressure increases excessively, the chlorine gas is vented via regulating
                      valve 41PV0810310 (41PV0820310) to the waste gas dechlorination sys-
                      tem.

                      Chlorine is further cooled in chlorine cooler II 41E-21106 (41E-21206) to
                      15 °C by means of chilled water.

                      This is to reduce the water content in chlorine, and hence to reduce
                      H2SO4 consumption in drying tower. However lower temperatures (below
                      12 °C) may result in the formation of chlorine hydrate, a chlorine ice.

                      Then the chlorine gas enters the wet chlorine filter 41FT21101
                      (41FT21201). The function of this filter is to separate brine mist (aerosol)
                      carried along with the gas. These, if not removed from the chlorine
                      stream, will form Na2SO4 and crystallise inside the drying tower. Deminer-
                      alised water (WDS) is sprayed into the chlorine stream at the inlet to pre-
                      vent any crystallisation of NaCl on filter surface and consequent increase
                      in pressure drop.

                      Then the chlorine gas enters the chlorine drying system.

                      The chlorine condensates from the three heat exchangers and the wet
                      chlorine filter, flows by gravity to a condensate collection header, from
                      where it flows to the anolyte tank 41V-07101 (41V-07201).




                                                          Doc. ID-Code                          Rev.
Copyright 2005 Uhde GmbH
                                                    8408205-CB-PR-MNL-0102                       02
                                        PVC Arvand
                                      Operating Manual
                                                                      National Petrochemical comany
                 SAZE H
                 C O NSU LTANTS             C/A Plant                 Arvand Petrochemical

Job Code:        PVC Arvand       Job Code:                        Owner Job Code: PVC Arvand
                                                                                     Page 641 of 967


                      Protection of membranes against too low chlorine pressure is achieved
                      by under pressure safety vessel 41V-21101 (41V-21201), in which air
                      from waster gas dechlorination system is sucked through the water seal
                      when the chlorine system pressure is 20 mbar below the pressure of the
                      waste gas header.

7.6        PART 6: NORMAL START-UP



7.6.1      GENERAL PRECONDITION
                      Prior to start-up of the chlorine cooling chapter, following prerequisites
                      must be fulfilled:

                      • Following systems are in operation:
                        Cooling water circulation, chilled water circulation, instrument air, wa-
                        ste gas dechlorination unit.
                      • All controllers in AUTO mode.
                      • All interlocks are active.
                      • Following systems are ready for operation:
                        Rectifiers and electrolysers, chlorine drying system, chlorine compres-
                        sion system, HCl synthesis unit and chlorine consumers at battery limit
                        (B.L.) of the chlorine plant.



7.6.2      FINAL PREPARATION
                      Establish / confirm communication lines between field and Control Room.

7.6.3      INITIAL START-UP
                      • Open demineralised water to under pressure safety vessel 41V-21101
                        (41V-21201).
                      • Assure that polished brine is still running trough the chlorine recupera-
                        tor 41E-21104 (41E-21204).
                      • Adjust the cooling water flow rate to chlorine cooler I 41E21105
                        (41E-21205).
                      • Start the chilled water flow rate to chlorine cooler II 41E-21106
                        (41E-21206) (Put 41TV2110103 (41TV2120103) in AUTO).
                      • Adjust demineralised water flow rate to wet chlorine filter 41FT21101
                        (41FT21201).
                      • Fill up the Cl2 condensate pipe with water, till overflow to anolyte tank
                        is observed in the sight glass.
                      • Start chlorine drying system (see chapter 8.6.3).
                      • Now chlorine compressor is started and kept running on bypass
                        (see chapter 9.6.3).
                      • System is now ready for taking over Cl2 from cells.
                      • Controller for chlorine A-valve 41PIC0810309 (41PIC0820309) to
                        chlorine compressor is in manual mode closed.
                      • Energise cells according to chapter 6.6.3 start-up of first electrolyser,
                        energising the electrolyser.
                      • The chlorine gas is sent via B-valve 41PV0810310 (41PV0820310) to
                        the waste gas dechlorination unit (see chapter 10.6), prior to transfer-
                        ring the chlorine to the compressor.
                      • When the gas purity approaches 80% chlorine content (measured by
                        analysis):
                             • Build up Cl2 pressure by adjusting the set points of 41PIC0810310
                               (41PIC0820310) which will start closing B-valve 41PV0810310
                               (41PV0820310) to build up the pressure.
                             • At constant chlorine pressure (controlled by 41PIC0810310
                               (41PIC0820310) open control A-valve to chlorine compressor
                               (41PV0810309 (41PV0820309) slowly in manual mode.
                             • Opening of 41PV0810309 (41PV0820309) allows Cl2 to flow to
                               chlorine compression unit. Consequentely 41PV0810310
                               (41PV0820310) will close to keep the pressure.
                             • Put 41PIC0810309 (41PIC0820309) in auto mode (set point = ac-
                               tual valve).

                             • Adjust set pointt of 41PIC0810310 (41PIC0820310) 15 mbar hig-
                               her than 41PIC0810309 (41PIC0820309).
                             • Increase chlorine pressure up to 200 mbar controlled by
                               41PIC0810309 (41PIC0820309) while increasing the load of the
                               electrolysers. Keep set point of 41PIC0810310 (41PIC0820310)
                               always 15 mbar higher than set point 41PIC0810309
                               (41PIC0820309).
                             • Check for leakages in chlorine system by use of ammonia. The re-
                               action of ammonia vapour with escaping chlorine is a dense white
                               cloud. The most convenient way to use ammonia for this purpose
                               is to direct the vapour from a plastic squeeze bottle containing
                               aqua ammonia at the suspected leak. Do not squirt liquid aqua am-
                               monia on pipe fittings.
                               Never attempt to repair leaks by welding until all chlorine has been
                               purged from the system.

                      In case of an upset, however, there is usually time enough for operators
                      to eliminate the problem. The necessary actions are summarised in the

7.7.3      PERFORMANCE CHECK
                      During normal operation, the process parameters must be recorded/doc-
                      umented.

                      Also the following is to be checked in the field and recorded to ensure
                      safe operation of the plant:

                      • Pressure drop across the 3 heat exchangers 41E-21104 (41E-21204),
                        41E-21105 (41E-21205) and 41E-21106 (41E-21206) (once/shift)
                        through 41PI2110101 (41PI2120101), 41PI2110102 (41PI2120102)
                        and 41PI2110103 (41PI2120103).
                      • The sight glasses in the chlorine condensate outlet lines of all 3 heat
                        exchangers, under pressure safety vessel and the wet chlorine filter
                        have to be monitored for continuous flow of condensate.
                      • Analysis of the chlorine gas inlet to the chlorine cooling system from
                        the sampling point provided (see Analytical Manual) and results should
                        be checked and documented regularly.
                      • Availability of nitrogen and instrument air.



7.7.4      REDUCED CAPACITY OPERATION
                      The chlorine cooling unit of each train has been designed to operate at
                      maximum 100% load to a minimum turn down ratio of 40%.

                      No special operational procedures are to be followed for reduced capac-
                      ity operations since the temperature at chlorine cooler II outlet is control-
                      led by the chilled water flow rate. Also the demineralised water flow rate
                      to the wet chlorine filter may be kept same as that for normal operations.



7.7.5      EFFLUENT AND RISK OF ENVIRONMENT
                      No effluents are produced in the chlorine cooling system.

                      The chlorine gas released from 41PV0810310 (41PV0820310) during
                      starting and after shutdown is treated in the waste gas dechlorination unit.

                      Chlorinated condensates are recycled into anolyte dechlorination chap-
                      ter.

7.8        PART 8: NORMAL SHUTDOWN



7.8.1      NORMAL SHUTDOWN
                      • Ensure that waste gas dechlorination unit is ready to absorb major
                        quantities of chlorine from this plant section (i.e. check desired caustic
                        levels and suction pressure)
                      • Gradually decrease the load on the electrolysers (to approx. 20% of full
                        load).
                      • Shut down the HCl synthesis unit, if H2 supply to HCl Synthesis from
                        corresponding Train (see chapter 17.8).
                      • Shut down the electrolysers (see chapter 6.8).
                        Close 41PV0810309 (41PV0820309) and open 41PV0810310
                        (41PV0820310). Thereby depressurisation of the chlorine system
                        starts by venting chlorine gas to the waste gas dechlorination system.



7.8.2      SHUTDOWN FOR LONGER PERIOD
                      Follow the procedure described in 7.8.1. However, additionally the follow-
                      ing operations are required:

                      • Stop Chlorine compressor.
                      • Purge the chlorine lines and equipment with plant air.
                      • Purge the condensate collecting lines with demineralised water or raw
                        water/service water to avoid contact with chlorine vapours.
                      • Stop cooling waste / chilled waste flow through coolers.

7.9        PART 9: EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN

7.9.1      EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN OF UNIT
                      • If the interlock 08101 (08201) is activated a reduction of the load for all
                        rectifiers of Train 1 (Train 2) will be started by ramp and a timer „Shut-
                        down of all rectifiers“ Train 1 (Train 2) will also be started for a prede-
                        termined time.
                        If the predetermined time is finished all rectifiers of Train 1 (Train 2) will
                        be shutdown.
                        Then the valve 41PV0810309 (41PV0820309) will be closed and the
                        valve 41PV0810310 (41PV0820310) will be opened.
                        If after a predetermined time the valve 41PV0810310 (41PV0820310)
                        is not open, then ESD08103 (ESD08203) opens the valve
                        41HV2110101 (41HV2120101) to depressurise the chlorine system.
                      • In case of any emergency requiring shutdown of the plant, follow the
                        procedure for normal shutdown (see previous chapter 7.8).

7.10.5     SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS, SPECIFIC INSTRUCTIONS PER UNIT

7.10.5.1   Handling Hazardous Materials
                      Please refer to chapter 1.8, Safety Instructions.




7.10.5.1.1 Danger caused by chlorine
                      The hazardous chemical handled in this system of the plant is chlorine.

                      Toxic! Danger caused by chlorine!
                      Toxic by inhalation, ingestion and through skin contact. Inhalation can
                      cause serious lung damage and may be fatal. 1000ppm (0.1%) is likely to
                      be fatal after a few deep breaths, and half that concentration fatal after a
                      few minutes. May irritate or burn skin.
                      Irritating to eyes, respiratory system and skin.

                      Observe following safety phrases:

                      • In case of accident or if you feel unwell, seek medical advice immedi-
                        ately!
                      • Wear protective gloves. Wear protective glasses!


                      Avoid release to the environment!

                      Very toxic to aquatic organisms!



7.10.5.2   Directions for Safe Operation and Inspection
                      Safety of plant

                      The following considerations have been taken regarding the pressure in
                      the chlorine system:

                      • If the pressure in the chlorine system is 20 mbar below atmospheric,
                        air from emergency vent system plant is sucked through the water seal
                        of under pressure safety vessel.

                      The above safety systems are foreseen to actuate only during emergency
                      i.e. in case the pressure control system fails.

                      Pressure gauges have been provided upstream and downstream of the
                      heat exchangers and pressure differential transmitter across the wet
                      chlorine filter to monitor the pressure drop across these equipment.

                      Also, the temperature control of the chlorine gas leaving chlorine cooler
                      II is provided so that the temperature of chlorine to drying tower is main-
                      tained at 15 °C. Higher temperatures result in more H2SO4 consumption
                      in drying tower and lower temperatures (less than 12 °C) may result in
                      chlorine hydrate formations.

                      Safety of personnel

                      The hazardous chemical handled in this section of the plant is chlorine.
                      Should an accident occur, immediate first aid is imperative.

8.2        PART 2: DESCRIPTION OF PROCESS

8.2.1      TECHNOLOGICAL PRINCIPLES
                      The chlorine drying system has been designed for a chlorine load of
                      585,000 t/a and 7.920 h/a produced in two separate electrolyser Trains.

                      In this section, the moist chlorine from the chlorine cooling chapter is
                      dried by means of sulphuric acid to a final moisture content of
                      10 ppm w/w.

                      The drying is performed in two Trains. Each Train can handle 50% of the
                      total plant capacity. Each Train is connected to one electrolyser Train and
                      consists of two drying towers which are in parallel and designed for 50%
                      of the Train production each. The dry Cl2 from drying towers passes
                      through a dry Cl2 filter (per Train) to remove H2SO4 droplets.

                      After the dry Cl2 filter the chlorine is sent via cell pressure control valve
                      to compression.

                      The chlorine drying system of each train has been designed for a turn
                      down ratio of 40% of the capacity per Train.



8.2.2      UNIT DESCRIPTION
                      The drying is shown in the following P&I Diagrams.

                      Train 1: P&I Diagram 21102

                      Train 2: P&I Diagram 21202

                      Each Train of the chlorine cooling system consists of:

                      • two drying towers
                      • one dry chlorine filter
                      • two H2SO4 - 78% circulating pump

                      The H2SO4 -98% and H2SO4 -78% storage which is common for both
                      trains is shown in:

                      P&I Diagram 21001

                      The storage consists of:

                      • one sulphuric acid (78%) day tank
                      • one H2SO4-98% tank
                      • five H2SO4-98% metering pump (two for each train, one common
                        stand-by)
                      • four H2SO4-98% cooler (two for each train)
                      • two H2SO4-78% transfer pump
                      • two seal pot.
                      Note:       Equipment numbers are for train 1, equipment numbers for
                                  train 2 are in brackets.

                      The moist chlorine gas coming from chlorine cooling system is dried by
                      means of H2SO4-98% to a final moisture content of 10 ppm w/w.

                      The drying is performed in the drying towers 41T-21101 A/B
                      (41T-22201 A/B) which are in parallel and designed for 50% of the train
                      production each.

                      The design of the towers is based on Uhde technology. Each tower con-
                      sists of a packed section in which Cl2 gas is dried in the packing section
                      41T-21101 A/B-101 (41T-21201 A/B-101) by means of recirculated
                      78% H2SO4.

                      Each drying tower has its own circulating pumps 41P-21103 A/B
                      (41P-21203 A/B) and 41P-21103 C/D (41P-21203 C/D) and H2SO4-78%.
                      Cooler 41E-21101 A/B (41E-21201 A/B) to remove the heat of reaction.

                      Chilled water is used as cooling medium to cool H2SO4 feed to the drying
                      towers.

                      An important parameter for good drying efficiency is the absorption tem-
                      perature. Best drying performance of the tower is achieved at acid tem-
                      peratures between 15 °C to 20 °C.

                      Also each tower consists of a tunnel tray section at the top where
                      H2SO4-98% is added by mans of H2SO4-98% metering pumps
                      41P-21002 A-E.

                      The required H2SO4 -98% (received from B.L.) is stored in the
                      98% H2SO4 tank 41V-21002 which is common for both Trains.

                      H2SO4 -98% metering pumps 41P-21002 A/B are connected via
                      H2SO4 -98% cooler 41E-21103 A/B with the drying towers of Train 1.

                      H2SO4 -98% metering pumps 41P-21002 D/E are connected via
                      H2SO4 -98% cooler 41E-21203 A/B with the drying towers of Train 2.

                      H2SO4 -98% metering pump 41P-21002 C is spare for both Trains. The
                      required H2SO4 -98% will be speed controlled by means of the KA load.

                      The spent H2SO4 -78% from both Trains is collected in sulphuric acid
                      (78%) day tank 41V-21004.

                      This acid is chlorine saturated and this chlorine must be removed before
                      any further use of the acid can be made. A partly dechlorination is done
                      by plant air sparging. A set of sparger pipes are installed in the day tank.
                      The chlorine containing air from the day tank is take to waste gas dechlo-
                      rination unit of one selected train.

                      The 78% H2SO4 is pumped to battery limit by means of H2SO4 -78%
                      transfer pump 41P-21004 A/B.

                      The dry chlorine from Train 1 passes through dry chlorine filter
                      41FT21103 to remove H2SO4 droplets. The dry chlorine gas is then taken
                      to chlorine compression unit 41U-22150 (see the following chapter 9).

                      The dry chlorine from Train 2 passes through dry chlorine filter
                      41FT21203 (41FT21203) to remove H2SO4 droplets. The dry chlorine gas
                      is then taken to chlorine compression unit 41U-22250 (see the following
                      chapter 9).

                      At outlet of the dry chlorine filter is the cell pressure control valve
                      41PV0810309 (41PV0820309). This valve also acts as a backflow pre-
                      vention valve (backflow of chlorine through the drying tower can damage
                      of the drying tower and other equipment upstream).

8.2.3      PROCESS CHEMISTRY
                      No chemical reactions are involved in the chlorine drying system.

                      The adsorption of water by H2SO4 is a physical sorption process due to
                      the extreme hydroscopic nature of sulphuric acid. The water adsorbing
                      content of the acid is controlled by the partial pressure of water, hence the
                      adsorptive process occurs better at lower temperatures, linear over the
                      concentration range, however, an approximate value is -12.56 kJ /% in
                      the range 98 - 78%.

8.6        PART 6: NORMAL START-UP



8.6.1      GENERAL PRECONDITION
                      Prior to start-up of the chlorine drying section, following prerequisites
                      must be fulfilled:

                      • Following systems are in operation:
                        Chilled water circulation, waste gas dechlorination unit, instrument air,
                        nitrogen system, chlorine cooling system (see chapter 7.7).
                      • All controllers in AUTO mode.
                      • All interlocks are active.
                      • Plant air sparging in sulphuric acid (78%) day tank 41V-21004 and ni-
                        trogen purging in H2SO4 - 98% tank 41V-21002.
                      • Following systems are ready for operation:
                        Rectifiers and electrolysers, chlorine cooling, chlorine compression sy-
                        stem, HCl synthesis unit and chlorine consumers at battery limit (B.L.)
                        of the chlorine plant.
                      • 98% H2SO4 supply to the chlorine drying system.
                      • 78% H2SO4 receiving and transferring.
                      • Ensure dryness of chlorine lines and equipment.



8.6.2      FINAL PREPARATION
                      Establish / confirm communication lines between field and Control Room.

8.6.3      INITIAL START-UP

                      • Start chilled water circulation through H2SO4 - 98% cooler 41E-21103
                        A/B (41E-21203 A/B)
                      • Start chilled water circulation through H2SO4 - 78% cooler 41E-21102
                        A/B (41E-21202 A/B).
                      • Start H2SO4 - 98% metering pump 41P-21002 A/B and 41P-21002 D/
                        E and fill up the chlorine drying tower 41T-21101 A/B (41T-21201 A/B).
                      • Start H2SO4 - 78% circulation pump 41P-21103 A/B (41P-21203 A/B)
                        and feed H2SO4 to chlorine drying tower 41T-21101 A (41T-21201 A).
                      • Start H2SO4 - 78% circulation pump 41P-21103 C/D (41P-21203 C/D)
                        and feed H2SO4 to chlorine drying tower 41T-21101 B (41T-21201 B).
                      • Establish flow rates.
                      • Start chlorine compressor and keep it running on bypass (refer to
                        chapter 9.6.3).
                      • Energise cells according to chapter 6.6.3 start-up of first electrolyser,
                        energising the electrolyser.
                      • Initially chlorine gas is sent via 41PV0810310 (41PV0820310) to waste
                        gas dechlorination unit (see chapter 10.6) from the chlorine cooling sy-
                        stem, prior to transferring the chlorine to the compressor.
                      • When the gas purity approaches 80% chlorine content (measured by
                        analysis):
                             • Build up Cl2 pressure by adjusting the set points of 41PIC0810310
                               (41PIC0820310) which will start closing 41PV0810310
                               (41PV0820310) to build up the pressure.
                             • At constant chlorine pressure (controlled by 41PIC0810310
                               (41PIC0820310) open control valve to chlorine compressor
                               (41PV0810309 (41PV0820309) slowly in manual mode.
                             • Opening of 41PV0810309 (41PV0820309) allows Cl2 to flow to
                               chlorine compression unit. Consequentely 41PV0810310
                               (41PV0820310) will close to keep the pressure.
                             • Put 41PIC0810309 (41PIC0820309) in auto mode (set point = ac-
                               tual valve).
                             • Adjust set pointt of 41PIC0810310 (41PIC0820310) 15 mbar hig-
                               her than 41PIC0810309 (41PIC0820309).

                             • Increase chlorine pressure up to 200 mbar controlled by

                               always 15 mbar higher than set point 41PIC0810309

                             • Check for leakages in chlorine system by use of ammonia. The re-

                               cloud. The most convenient way to use ammonia for this purpose
                               is to direct the vapour from a plastic squeeze bottle containing

                               monia on pipe fittings.

                               purged from the system.

                        leaving chlorine cooler II is provided so that the temperature of chlorine
                        to drying tower is maintained at 15 °C. Higher temperatures result in

8.7.4      REDUCED CAPACITY OPERATION
                      The chlorine drying system has been designed to operate at maximum
                      100% load to a minimum turndown of 40%.

                      At reduced capacity operations, the sulphuric acid flow rates to the drying
                      towers should be adjusted to maintain the final concentration of the 78%
                      sulphuric acid in the day tank.

                      If the moisture in chlorine of one train is increasing at reduced capacity
                      operation (< 50% train capacity), one of the drying towers can be taken
                      out of service by closing the outlet valve in the chlorine line. In this mode
                      of operation the H2SO4-98% feed to this tower should be stopped.

                      The H2SO4-98% feed to the running tower has to be adjusted accordingly
                      by changing set point of 41SY2100101 (41SY2100102).

                      Continue H2SO4-78% circulation.

                      Please also refer to chapter 8.9.1.



8.7.5      Effluent and risk of environment
                      No effluent are produced in this section of the plant. The chlorine waste
                      air liberated by the air sparging of the chlorine saturated H2SO4 - 78% in
                      the H2SO4 - 78% day tank is treated in the waste gas dechlorination unit.

                      The 78% acid with a chlorine content of < 200 ppm is send to battery limits
                      for further treatment.

8.8        PART 8: NORMAL SHUTDOWN



8.8.1      NORMAL SHUTDOWN
                      • Ensure that waste gas dechlorination unit of the respective train is rea-
                        dy to absorb major quantities of chlorine from this plant section (i.e.
                        check desired caustic levels and suction pressure)
                      • Gradually decrease the load on the electrolysers of the respective train
                        (to approx. 20% of full load).
                      • Shut down the HCl synthesis unit (see chapter 17.8), if H2-supply is by
                        respective train.
                      • Shut down the electrolysers (see chapter 6.8).
                        Close 41PV0810309 (41PV0820309) and open 41PV0810310
                        (41PV0820310). Thereby depressurisation of the chlorine system
                        starts by venting chlorine gas to the waste gas dechlorination system.
                      • Stop the chlorine compressor (see chapter 9.8).
                      Note:       During Normal Shutdown the electrolyser trains should be shut
                                  down one by one.



8.8.2      SHUTDOWN FOR LONGER PERIOD
                      Follow the procedure described in chapter 8.8.1. However, additionally
                      the following operations are required:

                      • The acid circulation to drying towers and cooling are stopped.
                      • Purging of the plant section is done by means of plant air.

8.9        PART 9: EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN

8.9.1      EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN OF UNIT
                      In case of a problem in any one of the drying towers or its acid circulation
                      loop requiring maintenance, it is possible to isolate one drying tower since
                      the drying system has been designed to operate at half load with one (1)
                      drying tower per Train. This can be done in the following manner:

                      In case of a problem with one H2SO4 circulation loop:

                      • Reduce the load to half capacity (Train).
                      • Isolate the respective chlorine drying tower from the chlorine lines.
                      • Stop the H2SO4 circulation through that drying tower.
                      • Isolate the drying tower from the H2SO4 lines.
                      • The required section can be drained, flushed with raw water and main-
                        tenance can be carried out.
                      Note:       Drying tower itself still under chlorine pressure.

                      • After maintenance dry this section carefully.
                      • After the drying, start the circulation of acid and take the drying tower
                        in line.
                      • Increase slowly the load to full capacity (Train).


                      In case of a problem in one drying tower:

                      • Shutdown the respective train.
                      • Then stop acid circulation of respective train. Isolate H2SO4 lines at re-
                        spective tower and drain H2SO4 if required.
                      • Then isolate the chlorine lines from that drying tower by using tempora-
                        ry blinds at inlet and block valve at outlet.
                      • Start-up chlorine production again and increase the load to max. half
                        capacity.
                      • After the drying tower is completely isolated and drained start flushing
                        with air and raw water and maintenance can be carried out.

                      Safety of personnel

                      The hazardous chemical handled in this section of the plant is chlorine
                      and H2SO4. Should an accident occur, immediate first aid is imperative.




8.10.5.1.1 Danger caused by chlorine
                      The hazardous chemical handled in this system of the plant is chlorine.

                      Toxic! Danger caused by chlorine!
                      Toxic by inhalation, ingestion and through skin contact. Inhalation can
                      cause serious lung damage and may be fatal. 1000ppm (0.1%) is likely to
                      be fatal after a few deep breaths, and half that concentration fatal after a
                      few minutes. May irritate or burn skin.
                      Irritating to eyes, respiratory system and skin.

                      Observe following safety phrases:

                      • In case of accident or if you feel unwell, seek medical advice immedi-
                        ately!
                      • Wear protective gloves. Wear protective glasses!


                      Avoid release to the environment!

                      Very toxic to aquatic organisms!

8.10.5.2   Directions for Safe Operation and Inspection
                      Safety of plant

                      The following considerations have been taken regarding the pressure in
                      the chlorine system:

                      • If the pressure in the chlorine system is 20 mbar below atmospheric,
                        air from emergency vent system plant is sucked through the water seal
                        of under pressure safety vessel.
                      • In case the pressure in the system is exceeding 215 mbar overpressu-
                        re, chlorine is blown to the waste gas dechlorination unit through
                        41PV0810310 (41PV0820310).
                      • High pressure is limited to 245 mbar overpressure by means of chlori-
                        ne/anolyte header safety valves at the electrolyser 41SV0811102/
                        1202/1302/1402/1502/1602/1702/1802/1902/2002/2102/2202
                        (41SV08211102/1202/1302/1402/1502/1602/1702/1802/1902/2002/
                        2102/2202).
                      • In case of a high pressure in the chlorine system, an emergency sy-
                        stem depressurisation is possible by means of an interlock opens
                        41HV2110101 (41HV2120101) and vents chlorine to waste gas
                        dechlorination unit.


                      The above safety systems are foreseen to actuate only during emergency
                      i.e. in case the pressure control system fails.

                      Pressure gauges have been provided upstream and downstream of the
                      drying towers and pressure differential transmitter across the dry chlorine
                      filter to monitor the pressure drop across these equipment.

                      Also, the temperature control of the chlorine gas leaving chlorine cooler
                      II is provided so that the temperature of chlorine to drying tower is main-
                      tained at 15 °C. Higher temperatures result in more H2SO4 consumption
                      in drying tower and lower temperatures (less than 12 °C) may result in
                      chlorine hydrate formations.

9.2        PART 2: DESCRIPTION OF PROCESS

9.2.1      TECHNOLOGICAL PRINCIPLES
                      Chlorine Compressors

                      Chlorine gas from the chlorine drying section(s) at a pressure of 1.01 bara
                      is compressed to 5 bara in three stage centrifugal compressors.

                      Each compressor operates as a fluid flow machine. It compresses proc-
                      ess gas according to the dynamic principle. The mechanical energy sup-
                      plied by the driver is transmitted to the process gas in the impellers of the
                      compressor. After its discharge from the impellers the accelerated proc-
                      ess gas is collected in the volutes, where the acceleration is converted
                      into pressure.

                      Each train of the chlorine drying section has its dedicated compressor,
                      handling about 37,600 kg/h of dry chlorine gas, for a combined annual ca-
                      pacity of about 585,000 tons of chlorine at 330 days of operation. Turn-
                      down ratio is 40%.



                      Lube Oil System

                      The lube oil system is designed for closed circulation which is maintained
                      by pumps. The lube oil system supplies the following components of the
                      machine unit with lube oil:

                      • Gear unit
                      • Compressor


                      Seal Gas System

                      By means of valves the seal gas system controls the seal gas flow to the
                      gas face seal and monitors the flow by means of measuring instruments.

                      Compressor Closed Cooling Circuit and Interstage / After Cooling

                      The components of the compressor cooling circuit and the interstage / af-

                      cooling circuit exchanging heat with chilled water from the plant.

9.2.2      UNIT DESCRIPTION
                      Note:       1: There are two compression trains. The unit description re-
                                  fers to Train 1, equipment numbers for Train 2 are in brackets.

                      Dry chlorine gas from the chlorine drying section is fed to the suction of
                      the chlorine compressor.

                      The following description breaks the chlorine compression unit(s) 41U-
                      22150 (22250) down into 4 sub-systems:

                      • 3 stage centrifugal chlorine compressor
                      • Lube oil system
                      • Compressor closed cooling circuit and interstage / after cooling
                      • Seal gas system.




                      41U-22150 (41U-22250) - Chlorine Compressor

                      41U-22150 (41U-22250) is a 3 stage centrifugal compressor. Interstage
                      and after cooling is provided, between each compression stage, to re-
                      duce energy consumption and allow the compressor to run on recycle.
                      The coolers also prevent the chlorine temperature rising above 120°C,
                      the point at which chlorine / iron fires can start to occur.
                      In normal operation, chlorine and non-condensable gases reach com-
                      pressor suction at less than 30°C where the pressure is maintained at
                      about 1.01 bara by adjusting the suction pressure control valve
                      41PV2210106A (41PV2220106A).
                      The chlorine leaves the final stage of the compressor at approx. 70°C and
                      5 barg. From the compressor, the compressed gas flows through after
                      cooler 41E-22153 (41E-22253) to the manifolder of the common chlorine
                      distribution.

                      Compressor Lube Oil System

                      41V-22161 (41V-22261), 41V-22162 (41V22262), 41E-22161A/B
                      (41E22261A/B), 41FT22161A/B (41FT22262A/B), 41C-22161 (41C-
                      22261) and 41P-22161A/B (41P-22261A/B) are designed to maintain
                      compressor oil condition, temperature and pressure, under varying oper-
                      ating conditions.
                      Oil from the oil sump, 41V-22161 (41V-22261) is pumped by 41V-
                      22161A/B (41V-22261A/B) through 41E-22161A or B (41E-22261A or B)
                      and 41FT22161A or B (41FT22261A or B) (lube oil coolers and lube oil
                      filters) to 41V-22162 (41V-22262) , the lube oil overhead storage tank,
                      and the bearings of the chlorine compressor and the gear. The oil is main-
                      tained at sufficient pressure to guarantee an overflow of oil from 41V-
                      22162 (41V-22262) to 41V-22161 (41V-22261); helping to assure a sup-
                      ply of oil during compressor run down.
                      Oil temperature is maintained by adjusting the flow of oil through one of
                      the oil coolers. On start-up it is necessary to pre-heat the oil using
                      41EH22163 (41EH22263).
                      Adjusting an oil spill back from pump delivery 41P-22161A/B (41P-
                      22261A/B), to the lube oil reservoir, controls the oil pressure.



                      Compressor Closed Circuit and Interstage / After Cooling

                      41V-22001, 41P-22001A/B, 41E-22151 (41E-22251), 41E-22152 ( 41E-
                      22252), 41E-22153 (41E-22253) and 41E-22001 provide interstage and
                      after cooling for the chlorine compressor 41C-22151 (41C-22251).
                      The coolant is provided from a closed-circuit water loop where the water
                      can be maintained free from particulates. This is important to avoid foul-
                      ing on the water side.
                      41V-22001 provides an inventory of coolant that is driven through the
                      heat exchangers by 41P-22001A/B. Heat is ultimately removed from the
                      system by 41E-22001, which is cooled by chilled water.
                      The design of the closed loop cooling water system ensures that during
                      operation each cooler is operated with a lower cooling water pressure
                      than the chlorine pressure on the tube side.
                      This ensures that any breach of the cooler will result in the chlorine enter-
                      ing the water system rather than vice versa. Any chlorine entering the
                      closed loop will be detected by the redox analyser 41AI2200201 in the
                      loop.

Copyright 2005 Uhde GmbH

                                       Operating Manual

                                                                                      Page 692 of 967


                      Shaft sealing is required at each end of the shaft, and is accomplices
                      with Dry Gas Seals (DGS). Dry gas seals are basically mechanical face
                      seals, consisting of a mating (rotating) ring and a primary (stationary) ring
                      contained in a cartridge. A sealing gas is injected into the seal; the sealing
                      gas will be nitrogen, at a slightly higher pressure than the suction pres-
                      sure of the chlorine gas.

                      The suction pressure is controlled by the pressure controller
                      41PIC2210106A (41PIC2220106A) by recycling the chlorine gas from the
                      compressor discharge to the suction side.

                      The design of the compressor includes additional capacity, so that 10%
                      of the flow can be recycled continuously, thus providing additional safety
                      against surge.

                      The anti-surge control 41FIC2210102 (41FIC2220102) protects the com-
                      pressor from surging. Both the suction as well as the discharge pressure
                      of the compressor is controlled, which means that the compressor can
                      operate at a constant through put.

                      The chlorine gas leaving the compressor(s) is distributed to the following
                      process areas:

                      • BL to EDC plant
                      • BL to Isocyanate plant
                      • BL to Polymer plant
                      • BL to other PVC Plant
                      • BL to other complex
                      • Bleach lye production of C/A Plant
                      • Hydrochloric acid synthesis of C/A Plant.



9.2.3      PROCESS CHEMISTRY
                      At temperatures >70°C the NCl3 which is formed in the electrolysers from
                      ammonium ions in the brine starts to decompose into N2 and Cl2. Some
                      by-products such as HCl are also formed in the presence of hydrogen.




                                                          Doc. ID-Code                          Rev.
Copyright 2005 Uhde GmbH
                                                    8408205-CB-PR-MNL-0102                       02
                                         PVC Arvand
                                       Operating Manual
                                                                       National Petrochemical comany
                 SAZE H
                 C O NSU LTANTS              C/A Plant                 Arvand Petrochemical
                                                                            Company
Uhde Project No: 03-3039           Sazeh Project No: 8047           Owner Project No: 8408205
Job Code:        PVC Arvand        Job Code:                        Owner Job Code: PVC Arvand
                                                                                      Page 693 of 967


                      At temperatures above 120°C, carbon steel can ignite in the presence of
                      chlorine. This is a aggressive reaction that can quickly lead to a loss of
                      containment and release of chlorine to atmosphere. To avoid this the
                      temperature of chlorine coming from the stages of the chlorine compres-
                      sor should not exceed 115°C.

                      If chlorine gas gets in contact with oil or grease chlorinated hydrocarbons
                      are formed leading to stiffen the bearing oil to such an extent that bearing
                      lubrication is no longer guaranteed.


                      As long as the chlorine gas is dry, there will be no restriction with regard
                      to the chosen materials. In case of a higher moisture content >50 ppm se-
                      lective corrosion is to be expected. If the chlorine gas is wet and the tem-
                      perature exceed 150°C the corrosion resistance of cast iron and alloyed
                      steels will decrease rapidly.
