9.6.3      INITIAL START-UP
                      Put the lube oil system into operation:

                      • Level of oil in oil reservoir 41V-22161 (41V-22261) is in normal limits.
                      • Set all valves in the oil system to operation position.
                      • Switch on the oil heater 41EH-22163 (41EH-22263).
                      • Switch on the Oil Mist Fan.
                      • Open the valve in the bypass line of oil pressure controller
                        41PCV2210406 (41PCV2220406).
                      • Check the oil temperature in lube oil reservoir 41V-22161 (41V-
                        22261).
                      • Wait until the oil temperature in lube oil reservoir 41V-22161 (41V-
                        22261) has reached at least 10 °C.
                      • Establish the instrument air flow to shaft seal on oil side. Check flow at
                        41FI2210517 (41FI2220517)

                      Note:       Caution!
                                  Risk of damage or destruction of the gas face seals by
                                  contact with lube oil!
                                  First admit seal gas and than cut in the Main Lube Oil
                                  Pump 41P-22161A (41P-22261A).


                      • Put Main Lube Oil Pump 41P-22161A (41P-22261A) into operation.
                        Check whether stand by pump is ready for auto start.
                      • Continue keeping the valve in the bypass line of oil pressure controller
                        41PCV2210406 (41PCV2220406) fully open.
                      • Check the oil temperature in lube oil reservoir 41V-22161 (41V-
                        22261).
                      • Wait until the oil temperature in lube oil reservoir 41V-22161 (41V-
                        22261) has reached at least 35 °C.

9.7        PART 7: NORMAL OPERATION

9.7.1      NORMAL ROUTINE OF OPERATION
                      Compressor and Utilities

                      The monitoring system and the control system in the FCS check the ma-
                      jor operating values of the machine unit and the utilities. Alarms are sig-
                      nalled if inadmissible operating values are reached.

                      Note:        Malfunctions must be eliminated immediately, see chapter
                                   10.7.2 - Trouble shooting.

                      1. Carry out the following processes at the specified time intervals:
                             • Process hourly operation check
                             • Process daily operation check
                      2. Check whether the maintenance work according to maintenance
                         schedule has been carried out by the mechanical technician.

                      Hourly operation check

                      Responsibility: Operator

                      Prerequisites: Machine unit and utilities have been put into operation.

                      1. Regularly check the operating values of the monitoring system, the
                         control system and the machine unit.
                      2. Check the trends of the operations values over the last 8 hours.

                      This puts you in a position to quickly react to changes in the operating val-
                      ues and to recognize trends.

                      The hourly operation check is now completed.

                      Daily operation check

                      Responsibility: Operator

                      Prerequisites: Machine unit and utilities have been put into operation and
                      process hourly operation check has been carried out.


                                                           Doc. ID-Code                          Rev.

                      Process routine change over of cooling water pumps

                      (Recommendation: To be done after two month of operation of the main
                      pump A and after one month of operation of pump B, to ensure that the
                      stand by pump is in full working order.)

                      • Check whether stand by pump is available/ready to use
                      • Check oil level in stand by pump. Top up if necessary
                      • Check suction and delivery valves are open
                      • Note delivery pressure of running pump
                      • Check with FCS that it's ok to change over cooling water pump
                      • Operate start button on stand by pump (if local) or ask FCS operator
                        to start the pump

                        sure
                      • Confirm pump has started with the FCS operator
                      • If pump fails to start abort operation, inform FCS and report
                      • If stand by pump has started and pressure/amps are ok stop in service
                        pump or request FCS to stop pump
                      • Allow operating pump to settle and note delivery pressure
                      • Inform FCS that pump change over is complete. Revisit pump after
                        20 - 30 minutes to check for any problems
                      • Log which pump is running and which is on stand-by.

9.7.2         TROUBLE SHOOTING
                          The following table describes upset conditions of the chlorine compres-
                          sion that are considered to be serious.

                          Interlocks as described in interlocking description (ANNEX A8, INTER-
                          LOCK DESCRIPTION) prevent the chlorine compression from damage.
                          In case of an upset, however, there is usually time enough for operators
                          to eliminate the problem. The necessary actions are summarised in the
                          following table.

Table 9-1 Trouble Shooting: Chlorine Compression

     Troubles               Indication                  Effects                         Action
1. El. motor does No current                  Lost of production.        – Check el. power supply.
   not start.     consumption                                            – Check oil temperature.
                                                                         – Check oil pressure.
2. Insufficient     Analysis of               Compressor surging,        Increase molecular weight of gas.
   chlorine quality chlorine gas.             unsteady flow.

9.7.3      PERFORMANCE CHECK
                       During normal operation, all process parameters mentioned must be
                       monitored and recorded/documented, if necessary.

                       Monitoring the concentration of various constituents, especially H2 and
                       O2 in chlorine gas, observed in FCS by means of on-line analysers is im-
                       portant to keep a check on the performance of the electrolysers.

                       In addition, samples should be taken for analysis from the various sample
                       points provided in this section of the plant (refer to Analytical Manual) and
                       the results should be checked and documented regularly.



9.7.3.1    Operating Variables
                       The main operating variables to be monitored are:

                       • Chlorine flow
                       • Chlorine gas temperatures before and after coolers
                       • Chlorine gas pressures after each compressor stage
                       • Oil temperatures and pressure
                       • Cooling water temperatures
                       • Availability of nitrogen and instrument air.

9.7.4      REDUCED CAPACITY OPERATION
                      The chlorine compression section has been designed to operate at max-
                      imum 110% capacity and to a minimum turn down of 40%.

                      No special operational procedures are to be followed for reduced capac-
                      ity operations since the suction and discharge pressure of the chlorine
                      compressor are controlled so that the compressor operates at a constant
                      throughput.



9.8        PART 8: NORMAL SHUTDOWN
                      Prerequisites for normal shutdown of one compressor while the
                      other is still in operation

                      Prior to shutdown, following activities should be carried out:

                      • Gradually decrease the load on the electrolysers of the corresponding
                        train (to approx. 20% of full load)
                      • Send chlorine via 41PV0810310 (41PV0820310) to the waste gas
                        dechlorination unit
                      • Reduce the load on electrolysers to zero and shut down the rectifiers.

                      Prerequisites for normal shutdown of both compressors

                      Prior to shutdown, following activities should be carried out:

                      • Shutdown one compressor first
                      • Gradually decrease the load on the electrolysers of the corresponding
                        train (to approx. 20% of full load)
                      • Send chlorine via 41PV0810310 (41PV0820310) to the waste gas
                        dechlorination unit
                      • Reduce the load on electrolysers to zero and shut down the rectifiers.



9.8.1      NORMAL SHUTDOWN
                      • The chlorine compressor starts running on bypass and the supply of
                        chlorine gas to the B.L. is stopped.
                        The chlorine compressor can be stopped if required.
                      • The supply of nitrogen air to the chlorine compressor seals should con-
                        tinue.
                      • The oil cooling and circulation through the compressor should continue
                        until the bearing house temperature is brought down.
                      • The chlorine compressor, along with the suction and discharge lines
                        starts getting depressurised as 41PV2210105 (41PV2220105) opens
                        on stopping the chlorine compressor by means of interlock, connecting
                        the chlorine system to the waste gas dechlorination unit.
                      Note:       At ambient temperatures lower than 20°C and for shutdown for
                                  longer period the chlorine manifolder and the feed pipes to the
                                  consumers have to be depressurised, preferably to bleach lye
                                  production or also to the waste gas dechlorination unit to avoid
                                  condensation of chlorine in the pipework.

9.8.2      SHUTDOWN FOR LONGER PERIOD
                      In addition to the activities mentioned under chapter 9.8.1, following ac-
                      tivities should be carried out in case of a shutdown for long periods:

                      • Nitrogen purging of the chlorine lines and compressor is to be done, by
                        means of a hand switch 41HS2210101 (41HS2220101), which injects
                        nitrogen into the suction of the compressor, and purged out into the

9.9        PART 9: EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN

9.9.1      EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN OF UNIT
                      An emergency interlocking system has been provided by means of which
                      shutdown of a chlorine compressor trips all the rectifiers of the corre-
                      sponding train.

                      Also hand switches 41HS2210103 (41HS2220103) and 41HS2210104
                      (41HS2220104) are provided, which when pressed in case of an emer-
                      gency, trip the corresponding chlorine compressor.

                      By 41HS2200111-114 both compressors are stopped.

                      In case of an emergency requiring shutdown of one train, follow the
                      procedure mentioned below:

                      • Shutdown of one train of the electrolysers/rectifiers as per the emer-
                        gency shutdown procedures.
                      • Depressurisation of the chlorine system starts by the action of the in-
                        terlock which opens 41PV0810310 (41PV0820310), closes
                        41PV0810309 (41PV0820309) and also closes 41HIC2200101
                        (41HIC2200105).
                      • The corresponding chlorine compressor starts running on bypass
                        while the compressor of the other train continue the chlorine gas sup-
                        ply to battery limits.
                      • The chlorine compressor can be stopped, if required.
                      In case of an emergency requiring shutdown of the entire plant, follow the
                      procedure mentioned below:

                      • Shutdown the electrolysers/rectifiers as per the emergency shutdown
                        procedures.
                      • Depressurisation of the chlorine system starts by the action of the in-
                        terlock which opens 41PV0810310 (41PV0820310), closes

9.10.5     SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS, SPECIFIC INSTRUCTIONS PER UNIT

9.10.5.1   Handling Hazardous Materials
                      The hazardous chemical handled in this section of the plant is chlorine
                      and nitrogen (asphyxiation).

                      Should an accident occur inspite of careful operation of the plant, imme-
                      diate first aid is imperative.

                      For details of precautionary measures in case of accident involved with
                      handling these chemicals, please refer to chapter 1.8, Safety Instructions.




9.10.5.1.1 Danger caused by chlorine
                      The hazardous chemical handled in this system of the plant is chlorine.

                      Toxic! Danger caused by chlorine!
                      Toxic by inhalation, ingestion and through skin contact. Inhalation can
                      cause serious lung damage and may be fatal. 1000ppm (0.1%) is likely to
                      be fatal after a few deep breaths, and half that concentration fatal after a
                      few minutes. May irritate or burn skin.
                      Irritating to eyes, respiratory system and skin.

                      Observe following safety phrases:

                      • In case of accident or if you feel unwell, seek medical advice immedi-
                        ately!
                      • Wear protective gloves. Wear protective glasses!


                      Avoid release to the environment!

                      Very toxic to aquatic organisms!

9.10.5.2   Directions for Safe Operation and Inspection
                      Overview

                      This Chapter informs about the intended use of the machine unit and the
                      residual hazardous for persons and physical assets and property during
                      utilisation of the machine unit. User roles and spheres of responsibility
                      are defined. Hazard areas, general safety references and the operating
                      modes for the machine unit are shown. For references for safe utilisation
                      of the Chlorine Compressor 41C-22150 (41C-22250) please see Opera-
                      tion Instruction of MAN and related documents.

                      Safety concept

                      The Chlorine Compressor has been designed and constructed according
                      to the state of the art and the generally accepted safety rules. Despite
                      this, its use may cause danger to life and risk of injury to users or third
                      parties, or may adversely affect the machine unit and other capital goods
                      or assets.

                      The safety concept provides rules for the authorisation for utilisation and
                      the responsibility of the individual users of the machine unit. The stipula-
                      tions of the safety concept depend on the intended use of the machine
                      unit and the existing residual hazards. The present operating instructions
                      are an important component part of the safety concept.

                      Purpose of machine unit

                      The Chlorine Compressor has been exclusively designed and built for the
                      compression of chlor gas within the technical limits of application. The fol-
                      lowing applications shall be considered as improper use:

                      • any other use than the intended use without written approval of the
                        manufacturer
                      • any operation outside the technical limits of application.
                      For any injury to persons or damage to physical assets and property
                      caused by improper use of the operator / user of the machine unit shall
                      be liable, not the manufacturer.

                      rects malfunctions. This person is skilled with professional training in the

                      fitter and been instructed in special operation of the machine unit.

                      General safety references

                      To avoid all risks to persons and an impairment of the chlorine compres-
                      sor during the intended use, the following safety regulations must be ob-
                      served.

                      • The machine unit must not be used unless it is in technically satisfac-
                        tory and operative condition.
                      • The protective devices and safety equipment of the plant unit must not
                        be by-passed, changed or rendered inoperative.
                      • The machine unit may only be used for the intended purpose, duly ob-
                        serving these operating instructions, in particular the safety referenc-
                        es. The operating instructions are an essential part of the machine unit
                        and must be available there.
                      • Safety and warning signs on the machine unit must always be legible.
                      • Any malfunctions have to be corrected immediately, in particular if
                        safety is at risk.
                      • For operation of the machine unit the maintenance schedule must be
                        adhered to.
                      • Original spare parts only shall be used.
                      • For reasons of safety, revamps or modifications on the machine unit
                        shall not be permitted without consultation with and approval by the
                        vendor.
                      • For the performance of service and maintenace measures adequate
                        shop equipment must be available.
                      • Work on the machine unit shall only be carried out after purging the
                        machine unit with nitrogen.
                      Chlorine is present in the machine unit. This is a dangerous material and
                      provides properties that include danger to people and the environment
                      (see chapter 9.10.5.1.1, page 714 - Danger caused by chlorine).

                      Residual hazards

                      The machine unit ensures a maximum degree of safety. Despite this, its
                      use may cause danger to life of and risk of injury to users or third parties,
                      or may adversely affect the machine unit and other capital goods or as-
                      sets.

10.2       PART 2: DESCRIPTION OF PROCESS

10.2.1     TECHNICAL PRINCIPLES
                      The waste gas dechlorination system consists of two parallel trains and
                      act as a safety system of the C/A Plant, and cleans up the chlorine and
                      traces of HCl contained in the waste gases generated at various points in
                      the chlorine plant. Each electrolyser train is connected to one waste gas
                      unit. The dechlorination of the waste gas stream in each train is accom-
                      plished by scrubbing with 18% NaOH solution in 2 stage ejectors con-
                      nected in series followed by a final absorber. The resultant product is
                      bleaching lye (sodium hypochlorite) solution.

                      The waste gas treatment system is designed for following modes of op-
                      eration.

                      • During start-up each train of the waste gas dechlorination system is
                        designed to handle approx. 4000 m3/h of waste gas.
                      • In emergency situation each system is designed to absorb total chlo-
                        rine production at full train load for 10 minutes. The quantity of waste
                        gas handled is approx. 15.000 m3/h.
                      • Safely absorb the entire chlorine in the plant during case of power in-
                        terruption or blackout, independent of emergency power by the use of
                        a pressurised emergency caustic tank 41V-26105 and/or 41V-26205.
                      • During normal operation of the plant, the system is designed to handle
                        approx. 550 m3/h of waste gas per train. Sufficient caustic safety re-
                        serves are always available in 41V-26004 to ensure safe shutdown of
                        the plant.
                      In all above operating cases the waste gas leaving the final absorber has
                      a maximum chlorine content of 5 mg/m3.

                      Waste Gas Dechlorination

                      Each of the two electrolyser trains is connected to its own waste gas
                      dechlorination system.

                      Train 1: P&I Diagram 26101, 26102, 26103

                      Train 2: P&I Diagram 26201, 26202, 26203

                      Diagram 26001.

                      Note:       Two trains are installed. Equipment numbers are for train one.

                      41J-26102 (26202) operated in series followed by a final absorber 41T-

10.2.3     PROCESS CHEMISTRY

10.2.3.1   Absorption of Chlorine in Caustic Soda
                      The chlorine contained in the waste gas stream reacts with caustic soda
                      to form sodium hypochlorite (bleaching lye), sodium chloride and water:

                             Cl2 + 2NaOH → NaOCl + NaCl + H2O

                      The heat of reaction (at 25 °C) is -1465 KJ/Kg of absorbed chlorine. This
                      reaction is highly exothermic.

                      With the absorption of chlorine, the caustic soda excess is reduced (ex-
                      cess in 18% NaOH is approx. 220 g/l). Over-chlorination of NaOH causes
                      formation of sodium chlorate, which decomposes the hypochlorite rapid-
                      ly.

10.2.3.2   Decomposition of Hypochlorite
                      Above 38 °C decomposition of NaOCI to NaCIO3 (chlorate) will be fa-
                      voured, so low temperatures are to be maintained during chlorination.
                      The stability of the hypochlorite solution dependant on following five fac-
                      tors:

                      • Hypochlorite concentration
                      • Concentration of certain catalysts
                      • Alkalinity, or pH-value of the solution
                      • Temperature of the solution
                      • Exposure to light.
                      The effect of variations in each of these factors, together and separately,
                      have been studied quantitatively. The most stable solutions are those of
                      low hypo-chlorite concentration, with a pH of 11 or higher, low copper and
                      nickel content, and storage in the dark at low temperatures.

                      A large excess of alkalinity does not stabilize 15% NaOCl solutions any
                      more than a slight excess (0.5% NaOH), but if the alkalinity drops below
                      0.04% NaOH, or a pH of about 11, decomposition becomes more rapid.

                      Stability of hypochlorite solutions is expressed by the term "half-life". This
                      is the number of days required for the NaOCl or available chlorine content
                      of a bleach solution to be reduced to half its initial value.

                      Effect of concentration and temperature

                      The influence of concentration and temperature on the stability (half-life)
                      of sodium hypochlorite solutions stored in the dark is shown in following
                      table:

                      Half-life days at

                             Available             100 °C         60 °C           25 °C           15 °C
                            chlorine g/l

                                  200               0.016           0.6             44              175
                                  100               0.079           3.5            220              800
                                  50                0.250          13.0            790             5000
                                  25                0.630          28.0           1800
                                   5                2.500         100.0           6000

                      From these data, it will be seen that both the concentration of available
                      chlorine and the temperature of storage have an extremely important in-
                      fluence on the rate of loss of available chlorine. For example, the half-life
                      of the 25 g/l solution is decreased over 98% when the storage tempera-
                      ture is 60 °C as compared with 25 °C; also the half-life at 25 °C, is de-
                      creased about 56% when the concentration is changed from 25 to 50 g/l.

                      Effect of catalysts

                      The most powerful catalysts in promoting decomposition of NaOCl, in or-
                      der of relative effectiveness, are 1. Cobalt, 2. Nickel, 3. Copper.

                      Of course, copper is the one generally present to some extent and should
                      be kept as low as possible, not over 0.0001% (one part per million) in the
                      finished (max. 15%) bleaching lye solution.
                      All of these are very much more effective than iron or manganese. Quan-
                      titative data on the effect of copper, iron and alumina on strong (200 g/l)
                      bleach liquer show the following limiting conditions:

                      Cu          0.00001%

                      Fe2O3       0.01%

                      Al2O3       0.01%



                      Effect of alkalinity

                      By controlling the alkalinity of the hypo solution with excess caustic the
                      rate of decomposition of the hypo can be retarded. At low pH values the
                      decomposition is very fast. For this reason it is convenient to handle hypo
                      solutions with a free caustic content of at least 10 g NaOH/l.

                      Once the above prerequisites are fulfilled, following activities are to be

                               (26205).

                               bleaching lye pumps.

                      • Start 18% caustic pump 41P-26002 A/B and pump 18% NaOH to the
                        final absorber 41T-26101 (26201).

                          The 18% NaOH overflows from the final absorber to suction tank II
                          41V-26102 (41V-26202) and finally to suction tank I 41V-26101
                          (41V-26201).

                          lye tank) 18% caustic feed to the final absorber can be stopped.
                      • Start-up of the ejectors:
                             • The gas passage through the 2 ejectors and final absorber is
                               checked. Put gas pressure controller 41PYIC2610108 (2620108)
                               on MANUAL and open the control valve PV2610106 (2620106) ful-
                               ly.
                             • The bleaching lye circulation pump 41P-26101 A/B (26201 A/B) is
                               started and the discharge valve is opened slowly. The ejector
                               41J-26101 (26201) starts to draw in air.
                             • Now bleaching lye circuit II and final absorber is put into operation
                               by starting bleaching lye circulation pump 41P-26101 C/D
                               (26201 C/D).
                               Adjust the circulation rate to the final absorber to 35 m3/h by
                               41FIC2610201 (2620201) acting on 41FV2610201 (2620201).

10.8       PART 8: NORMAL SHUTDOWN

10.8.1     NORMAL SHUTDOWN
                      The waste gas dechlorination system shall be in operation at all times
                      when the chlorine plant is in operation.

                      Note:       No shutdown for short periods should be initiated or sched-
                                  uled.



10.8.2     SHUTDOWN FOR LONGER PERIOD
                      The waste gas dechlorination system shall not be shutdown even during
                      shutdown of chlorine plant. Only when a shutdown of waste gas dechlo-
                      rination system is extremely necessary, it should be stopped.

                      The waste gas dechlorination system can be shutdown 120 minutes after
                      shutdown of the electrolysis respective train.

                      • At zero-load of the electrolysers, the caustic flow to the final absorber
                        can be stopped.
                      • The bleaching lye circulation pumps 41P-26101 A/B/C/D
                        (41P-26201 A/B/C/D) can be stopped, when all cells and all chlorine
                        containing equipment and piping are free of chlorine.
                      • For prolonged shutdown it is recommended to drain the tanks and to
                        flush the system with water.

10.9       PART 9: EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN

10.9.1     EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN OF UNIT
                      The waste gas dechlorination system cannot be shutdown during opera-
                      tion of the chlorine plant. This unit shall remain in operation even during
                      shutdown of the chlorine plant. Only when a shutdown of the waste gas
                      dechlorination system is extremely necessary, it should be stopped. In
                      this case, the electrolysers of the respective train have to be stopped. The
                      waste gas dechlorination unit will operate till minimum 120 minutes after
                      the electolysers are shut down. At zero load of the electrolysers, the caus-
                      tic flow to the final absorber can be stopped. The circulation pumps can
                      be stopped, when all the electrolysers and all chlorine containing equip-
                      ment and piping are free of chlorine.

                      In case of power failure the circulation pumps as well as the 18% caustic
                      pumps will start automatically on emergency diesel.

11.2       PART 2: DESCRIPTION OF PROCESS

11.2.1     TECHNOLOGICAL PRINCIPLES
                      The bleach solution preparation system is designed for the production of
                      40m3/d of a hypo solution with an average concentration of 13,7% w/w of
                      active chlorine.

                      Solution strength:        165 gpl. average Cl2

                      with excess caustic of:   3 - 10 gpl.



11.2.2     UNIT DESCRIPTION
                      The chlorinated caustic soda solution (18%) delivered from the bleaching
                      lye production tank 41V-27001 via bleaching lye circulation pump
                      41P-27002 A/B, is fed to the bleaching lye ejector 41J-27001, and is the
                      motive force for pulling dry chlorine gas from the chlorine compression
                      area into the ejector.

                      The combined fluids caustic and chlorine react to form a sodium hy-
                      pochlorite solution.

                      The sodium hypochlorite solution is collected in the bleach lye production
                      tank 41V-27001. This solution is then pumped and circulated with the
                      bleaching lye cooler 41E-27001 back to the production tank. The product
                      lye is forwarded in the storage tank 41TK-27002 on level control
                      41LIC270101. The bleaching lye storage tank has a volume of 500 m3.

                      In order to control the quality of the bleach solution fresh caustic soda /
                      bleaching lye from the waste gas unit is added. The addition is controlled
                      by redox measurement, 41AC2700101, at about 570 mV. The caustic
                      soda / bleaching lye is pumped into the bleaching lye production cycle by
                      bleaching lye pump 41P-26102 A/B (41P-26202 A/B) from the bleaching
                      lye tank 41V-26104 (41V-26204), located in the waste gas dechlorination
                      area (over flow from suction tank I). Feeding of caustic soda / bleaching
                      lye from the waste gas units should be done from one trains only.
                      A manual addition of NaOH 32% is also possible if required.




                                                         Doc. ID-Code                           Rev.
Copyright 2005 Uhde GmbH
                                                   8408205-CB-PR-MNL-0102                        02
                                          PVC Arvand
                                        Operating Manual
                                                                        National Petrochemical comany
                 SAZE H
                 C O NSU LTANTS               C/A Plant                 Arvand Petrochemical

Job Code:        PVC Arvand         Job Code:                        Owner Job Code: PVC Arvand
                                                                                       Page 751 of 967


                      The density of the bleach solution is controlled by addition of demineral-
                      ised water to the suction side of the bleaching lye circulation pump, and
                      is kept at 1,231 kg/m3 (15 °C).

                      The bleaching lye in the storage tank can be recycled by the loading
                      pump 41P-27003 A/B back into the production tank 41V-27001, if re-
                      quired.

                      A truck filling station for tank trailers is also provided. The trucks will be
                      filled with bleaching lye from the storage tank via loading pump
                      41P-27003A/B.

11.2.3     PROCESS CHEMISTRY
                      Chlorine will reacts with a caustic soda solution to produce sodium hy-
                      pochlorite according to the following equation:

                             Cl2 + 2NaOH = NaOCl + NaCl + H2O + 24,7 kcal. (1465 kJ/kgCl2)

                      At temperature above 38 °C the formation of sodium chlorate is favoured
                      by decomposition of sodium hypochlorite. For this reason low tempera-
                      tures should be applied for the preparation of soda bleach solutions.

                      The stability of sodium hypochlorite solutions is dependent upon five ma-
                      jor factors:

                      • Concentration of the sodium hypochlorite solution
                      • Concentration of certain impurities which catalyse decomposition
                      • Alkalinity or pH of the solution
                      • Temperature of the solution, both in preparation and in storage
                      • Exposure to light.


                      Stable solutions are favoured at pH values above pH 11, containing low
                      concentrations of copper and nickel, low temperatures, and dark contain-
                      ment vessels.

                      Copper, nickel and cobalt are catalysts which contribute to the decompo-
                      sition of sodium hypochlorite solutions.



                                                           Doc. ID-Code                          Rev.
Copyright 2005 Uhde GmbH
                                                     8408205-CB-PR-MNL-0102                       02
                                         PVC Arvand
                                       Operating Manual
                                                                       National Petrochemical comany
                 SAZE H
                 C O NSU LTANTS              C/A Plant                  Arvand Petrochemical
                                                                             Company
Uhde Project No: 03-3039           Sazeh Project No: 8047           Owner Project No: 8408205
Job Code:        PVC Arvand        Job Code:                        Owner Job Code: PVC Arvand
                                                                                      Page 752 of 967


                      The alkalinity or pH value has a pronounced effect on the stability of so-
                      dium hypochlorite solutions. There is no evidence that excess alkalinity
                      greater than 0,5% by weight of solution as NaOH has a beneficial effect
                      on the stability of the sodium hypochlorite solution. Should the alkalinity
                      drop below 0,04% by w/w NaOH (below pH 11) decomposition will accel-
                      erate.

                      Decomposition of Hypochlorite

                      Above 38 °C decomposition of NaOCI to NaCIO3 (chlorate) will be fa-
                      voured, so low temperatures are to be maintained during chlorination.
                      The stability of the hypochlorite solution dependant on following five fac-
                      tors:

                      • Hypochlorite concentration
                      • Concentration of certain catalysts
                      • Alkalinity, or pH-value of the solution
                      • Temperature of the solution
                      • Exposure to light.


                      The effect of variations in each of these factors, together and separately,
                      have been studied quantitatively. The most stable solutions are those of
                      low hypo-chlorite concentration, with a pH of 11 or higher, low copper and
                      nickel content, and storage in the dark at low temperatures.

                      A large excess of alkalinity does not stabilize 15% NaOCl solutions any
                      more than a slight excess (0.5% NaOH), but if the alkalinity drops below
                      0.04% NaOH, or a pH of about 11, decomposition becomes more rapid.

                      Stability of hypochlorite solutions is expressed by the term "half-life". This
                      is the number of days required for the NaOCl or available chlorine content
                      of a bleach solution to be reduced to half its initial value.




                                                          Doc. ID-Code                          Rev.
Copyright 2005 Uhde GmbH
                                                    8408205-CB-PR-MNL-0102                       02
                                              PVC Arvand
                                            Operating Manual
                                                                             National Petrochemical comany
                 SAZE H
                 C O NSU LTANTS                   C/A Plant                  Arvand Petrochemical
                                                                                  Company
Uhde Project No: 03-3039                Sazeh Project No: 8047            Owner Project No: 8408205
Job Code:        PVC Arvand             Job Code:                         Owner Job Code: PVC Arvand
                                                                                            Page 753 of 967


                      Effect of concentration and temperature

                      The influence of concentration and temperature on the stability (half-life)
                      of sodium hypochlorite solutions stored in the dark is shown in following
                      table:

                      Half-life days at

                             Available             100 °C         60 °C           25 °C           15 °C
                            chlorine g/l

                                  200               0.016           0.6             44              175
                                  100               0.079           3.5            220              800
                                  50                0.250          13.0            790             5000
                                  25                0.630          28.0           1800
                                   5                2.500         100.0           6000

                      From these data, it will be seen that both the concentration of available
                      chlorine and the temperature of storage have an extremely important in-
                      fluence on the rate of loss of available chlorine. For example, the half-life
                      of the 25 g/l solution is decreased over 98 % when the storage tempera-
                      ture is 60 °C as compared with 25 °C; also the half-life at 25 °C, is de-
                      creased about 56 % when the concentration is changed from 25 to 50 g/l.

                      Effect of catalysts

                      The most powerful catalysts in promoting decomposition of NaOCl, in or-
                      der of relative effectiveness, are 1. Cobalt, 2. Nickel, 3. Copper.

                      Of course, copper is the one generally present to some extent and should
                      be kept as low as possible, not over 0.0001% (one part per million) in the
                      finished (max. 15 %) bleaching lye solution.
                      All of these are very much more effective than iron or manganese. Quan-
                      titative data on the effect of copper, iron and alumina on strong (200 g/l)
                      bleach liquer show the following limiting conditions:

                      Cu          0.00001 %

                      Fe2O3       0.01 %

                      Al2O3       0.01 %



                      Effect of alkalinity

                      By controlling the alkalinity of the hypo solution with excess caustic the
                      rate of decomposition of the hypo can be retarded. At low pH values the
                      decomposition is very fast. For this reason it is convenient to handle hypo
                      solutions with a free caustic content of at least 10 g NaOH/l.

11.6       PART 6: NORMAL START-UP

11.6.1     GENERAL PRECONDITION
                      Following prerequisites are to be ensured before start-up:

                      • Chilled water must be available and running through bleaching lye
                        cooler 41E-27001.
                      • Demineralised water must be available.
                      • Instrument air must be available.
                      • Waste gas dechlorination plant must be in operation.
                      Note:       The bleaching lye production tank 41V-27001 should be con-
                                  nected to the Waste Gas Unit, which supplies 18% caustic /
                                  bleaching lye for production. The supply should only come
                                  from one waste gas unit.

                      • Chlorine plant and compressor are in operation.
                      • All controllers in AUTO mode.
                      • All interlocks are active.



11.6.2     FINAL PREPARATION
                      Once the above preparations are complete carry out the following activi-
                      ties.

                      • Fill 41V-27001 with 18% caustic soda by using bleaching lye pump
                        41P-26102 A/B (26202 A/B).
                      • When tank 41V-27001 is full (80% level) start pump 41P-27002 A or B
                        and circulate via bleaching lye cooler 41E-27001 and bleaching lye
                        product tank 41V-27001.
                      • Feed 18% NaOH on level control LIC2700101 to bleaching lye storage
                        tank 41TK27002.
                      • Start bleaching lye loading pump 41P-27003 A/B and recycle circulate
                        back to production tank 41V-27001.

11.6.3     INITIAL START-UP
                      The 18% caustic soda system of the bleach lye production plant is in op-
                      eration. Start up of the ejectors’s gas passage, only after 18% NaOH is
                      filled into the system.

                      • The gas passage through the ejector was checked with air.
                      • Open slowly the control valve 41FIC2200108 and feed chlorine to the
                        bleaching lye ejector 41J-27001.
                      • Check quality of the bleaching lye with Redox measurement
                        41AIC2700101 (about 570 mV). Fresh caustic will be added on redox
                        control from bleaching lye tank 41V-26104 (26204).
                      Note:       Only caustic of one of the bleaching lye tanks 41V-26104
                                  (26204) should be fed to the bleaching lye production unit. The
                                  bleaching lye tank 41V-26104 (26204) can be filled with caus-
                                  tic / bleaching lye by adding 18% caustic to final absorber
                                  41T-26101 (26201).

                      • Check density of the bleaching lye with 41DIC2700101. The density is
                        controlled by the addition of demineralised water.
                      • Circulate bleach lye until it is forwarded to the storage tanks on level
                        control 41LIC2700101.
                      • Put all controllers in AUTO mode.



11.6.4     START-UP AFTER SHORT SHUTDOWN
                      • Check levels in bleach lye production tank 41V-27001 and bleach lye
                        storage tank 41TK27001.
                      • Start pumps 41P-27002 A or B.
                      • Start pump 41P-27003 A or B, if required to recycle bleaching lye back
                        to production tank.
                      • Open chlorine valve from compressor to beach lye ejector 41J-27001,
                        and add chlorine slowly.

11.7       PART 7: NORMAL OPERATION

11.7.1     NORMAL ROUTINE OF OPERATION
                      The system is operating automatically and the parameters must be ob-
                      served in the FCS:

                      • Level of bleach lye product tank 41V-27001.
                      • Level of bleach lye storage tank 41TK27002.

                      Note:        Before levels in the storage tank reach high:

                             • Arrange for truck loading
                             • Open hand valve on discharge of 41P-27002 A/B and feed bleach
                               lye to the bleach lye tanks 41V-26104 and/or 26204 for destruction
                               in anolyte system.
                      • Check density measurement
                      • Check Redox measurement
                      • Check temperature 41TI2700102, 41TI2700101, 41TI2700105,
                        41TI2700104, 41TI2700103.
                      • Check pressure gauges on pumps.
                      • Check ampere meters on pumps.
                      • Check level of bleaching lye / 18% caustic in bleaching lye tank
                        41V-26104 (26204). The bleaching lye tank 41V-26104 (26204) has to
                        be filled by adding 18% caustic to final absorber 41T-26101 (26201) in
                        the waste gas unit.
                      • For truck loading please refer to vendor information of Requisition No.:
                        8408205-CB-ME-REQ-0064.

11.7.4     REDUCED CAPACITY OPERATION
                      If the storage tank is full, shut off chlorine gas flow to bleach lye ejector
                      41J-27001.

                      Plant can be operated „SLOWLY“, by reducing the chlorine flow to the
                      ejector 41J-27001.



11.8       PART 8: NORMAL SHUTDOWN

11.8.1     NORMAL SHUTDOWN
                      The waste gas dechlorination system (Unit 260, 261, 262) shall not be
                      shutdown even during shutdown of the chlorine plant.

                      The bleach lye production can be shutdown any time:

                      • Stop chlorine gas flow to ejector 41J-27001.
                      • Stop Bleaching Lye Circulation Pump 41P-27002 A/B.
                      • Stop Bleach Lye Filling Pump 41P-27003 A/B.
                      • Stop chilled water flow to Bleaching Lye Cooler 41E-2701, if required.
                      • Stop demineralised flow to circulation pump suction.



11.8.2     SHUTDOWN FOR LONGER PERIOD
                      Follow procedures under 11.8.1, Normal Shutdown.

                      Note:       Rubberlined tanks shall be kept humid and/or wet. Fill with wa-
                                  ter, if necessary.

11.9       PART 9: EMERGENCY OPERATIONS AND SHUTDOWN

11.9.1     EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN OF UNIT
                      In case of an emergency shutdown situation the waste gas chlorination
                      system will remain in operation, and all chlorine gas streams are diverted
                      to the waste gas dechlorination system.

                      In case of power failure, pumps of bleach lye production plant will stop.

                      A hand switch at the truck loading station is provided to interrupt the filling
                      operation immediately.

11.9.1.1   Interlock Description
                      Please refer to ANNEX A8, INTERLOCK DESCRIPTION.

11.9.1.2   Alarm And Interlock Trip Settings
                      Please refer to ANNEX A19, LIST OF THRESHOLD VALUES.



11.9.2     EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN DUE TO GENERAL REASONS
                      If it is necessary to shutdown the bleach lye production line:

                      • Stop chlorine flow to ejector 41J-27001.
                      • Stop pump 41P-27002 A and/or B.



11.9.3     START-UP AFTER AN EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN
                      • Check Bleach Lye Production Tank level and fill in 18% NaOH or
                        bleaching lye from storage tank, if necessary.
                      • Check Bleach Lye Storage Tank level.
                      • Start pump 41P-27002 A or B.
                      • Establish circulation and chilled water / demineralised water flows.
                      • Start chlorine flow to ejector 41J-27001.

11.10.5.1.1Danger caused by chlorine
                      The hazardous chemical handled in this system of the plant is chlorine.

                      Toxic! Danger caused by chlorine!
                      Toxic by inhalation, ingestion and through skin contact. Inhalation can
                      cause serious lung damage and may be fatal. 1000ppm (0.1%) is likely to
                      be fatal after a few deep breaths, and half that concentration fatal after a
                      few minutes. May irritate or burn skin.
                      Irritating to eyes, respiratory system and skin.

                      Observe following safety phrases:

                      • In case of accident or if you feel unwell, seek medical advice immedi-
                        ately!
                      • Wear protective gloves. Wear protective glasses!


                      Avoid release to the environment!

                      Very toxic to aquatic organisms!

12.2       PART 2: DESCRIPTION OF PROCESS

12.2.1     TECHNICAL PRINCIPLES
                      The catholyte systems of the electrolyser trains are designed to handle
                      the 32% caustic produced in the electrolysers, and to separate the caus-
                      tic product from the hydrogen.

                      Each system serves to cool / heat and dilute the 32% caustic to approx.
                      30% which is then returned to the electrolysers.

                      The two electrolyser trains of the C/A Plant are connected to one
                      catholyte system each.

                      The catholyte system of one train consists of one catholyte circulation
                      system feeding one train of electrolysers. The catholyte system supplies
                      the catholyte feed to the cell room or to single electrolysers at tempera-
                      tures between 40 and 85 °C to enable start-up, shutdown and operation
                      at different cell loads.

                      The product caustic soda is continuously withdrawn from the catholyte
                      circulation loops as a 32% solution and is fed to the caustic evaporation
                      unit at a total rate of max. 196 m3/h (both trains).

                      The catholyte head tanks provide a reservoir of catholyte to automatically
                      fill the electrolysers in the case of power failure.

12.2.2     UNIT DESCRIPTION
                      Catholyte circulation - Train 1 / Train 2

                      PFDs:       08101- Train 1

                                  08201- Train 2

                      P&IDs: 31101, 31102 - Train 1

                                  31201, 31202 - Train 2

                      There are two electrolyser trains each connected to its own catholyte cir-
                      cuit. Each catholyte circuit consists of:

                      1.      one hydrogen separator
                      2.      two catholyte tanks, hydraulically connected, both in operation
                      3.      two catholyte pumps (one spare)
                      4.      one catholyte heater
                      5.      one catholyte cooler
                      6.      one catholyte head tank

                      Note:         The equipment number in the following description refer to
                                    catholyte train 1. Equipment numbers for catholyte train 2 are
                                    in brackets.

                      32% caustic soda leaves the electrolyser through an overflow pipe into
                      the catholyte header along with hydrogen. In the catholyte header (below
                      the cells) separation of H2 and catholyte takes place.

                      The catholyte (32% NaOH) flows under gravity via the hydrogen separa-
                      tors 41V-31103 (41V-31203) at approx. 88°C to the catholyte tanks
                      41V-31102 A/B (41V-31202 A/B). As the hydrogen system is operating at
                      an overpressure of about 240 mbar, a seal is necessary to separate H2
                      pressure from the ambient pressure in the catholyte tank. The hydrogen
                      separators 41V-31103 (41V-31203) act as such a seal.

                      A small stream of N2 (3 - 4 Nm3/h) is fed to the catholyte header going to
                      the catholyte tank. This N2 is vented to the catholyte head tank
                      41V-31101 (41V-31201) via vent line of catholyte tanks 41V-31101 A/B


                                                            Doc. ID-Code                          Rev.
Copyright 2005 Uhde GmbH
                                                      8408205-CB-PR-MNL-0102                       02
                                        PVC Arvand
                                      Operating Manual
                                                                      National Petrochemical comany
                 SAZE H
                 C O NSU LTANTS             C/A Plant                 Arvand Petrochemical

Job Code:        PVC Arvand       Job Code:                        Owner Job Code: PVC Arvand
                                                                                     Page 773 of 967


                      (41V-31201 A/B) and from catholyte head tank to atmosphere, and
                      thereby prevents caustic from coming into contact with air (CO2) and
                      hence formation of Na2CO3. Any hydrogen accumulation in the system is
                      also prevented.

                      From the catholyte tanks 41V-31101 A/B (41V-31201 A/B), the catholyte
                      pumps 41P-31101 A/B (41P-31201 A/B) transfer the major portion of
                      caustic soda pressure controlled to the electrolysers. The catholyte head
                      tank 41V-31101 (41V-31201) is in by-pass of the main stream. The bal-
                      ance of caustic is branched off as product to 32% NaOH to the caustic
                      evaporation unit 41U-32050.

                      The catholyte pump 41P-31101 A/B (41P-31201 A/B) serves the follow-
                      ing purposes:

                      • Circulate catholyte through coolers or heater to electrolysers.
                      • Fill catholyte head tanks.
                      • Feed product caustic to caustic evaporation and / or to the intermedi-
                        ate caustic tanks.


                      The catholyte head tank is always kept full by overflowing a small part
                      stream of catholyte back to the catholyte tank.
                      The head tank offers a reserve of caustic which automatically drains into
                      and fills the electrolysers, displacing hydrogen gas in the case of power
                      failure / stop of catholyte pumps.

                      The 32% caustic is diluted with polished/demin water (WDS) before it en-
                      ters the catholyte header. The amount of polished water addition to
                      catholyte to the electrolysers is controlled by FIC3110104 (FIC3120104),
                      acting on FV3110104 (FV3120104). The rate of addition of polished wa-
                      ter is adjusted according to the load of the rectifiers.

                      Heat exchangers are used for heating 41E-31101 (41E-31202) or cooling
                      41E-31102 (41E-31202) the catholyte. During heating the caustic flow
                      through the cooler should be blocked and vice versa while cooling. The
                      main feed temperature to the electrolyser is temperature controlled.

                      The catholyte heat exchangers are also used for heating / cooling of
                      catholyte during start-up and shutdown of the electrolysers.

                      Catholyte cooler 41E-31102 (41E-31202) is used for cooling the catholyte
                      during normal operation. Catholyte heater 41E-31101 (41E-31201) will
                      be used for heating if required.

                      Low pressure steam is used as heating medium and cooling water is used
                      as cooling medium.

                      Demineralised water is added to the 32% catholyte solution re circulated
                      to the electrolyser for dilution to control the concentration at approx.
                      30% NaOH.

                      For start-up or shutdown of an individual electrolyser, caustic is supplied
                      to the individual electrolyser through the filling line. This line branches of
                      the main line after the heater / cooler to adjust the required temperatures
                      for heating / cooling of a single electrolyser.

                      The product stream (32% NaOH) is tapped upstream of the catholyte
                      heat exchangers. This 32% caustic stream is fed to the caustic evapora-
                      tion system 41U-32050, through flow measurement loop 41FI3110201
                      (41FI3120201). In case that the caustic evaporation system is not in op-
                      eration, the 32% caustic is collected in the 32% NaOH intermediate stor-
                      age tanks 41TK32001 A/B. The intermediate storage tanks are
                      hydraulically connected and have a total volume of 3,200 m3, correspond-
                      ing to about 16 hours of retention time (hold-up capacity). 32% caustic
                      collected in the intermediate storage tanks can be recovered for concen-
                      tration in the caustic evaporation system using 32% caustic transfer
                      pump 41P-32001.

                      A part stream of hot 32% caustic product is used for meeting internal con-
                      sumption of NaOH in the chlorine plant.

12.2.3     PROCESS CHEMISTRY
                      The 32% NaOH (Catholyte) from the catholyte tanks is diluted with
                      polished/demineralised water (WDS) to approx. 30% NaOH concentra-
                      tion which goes to electrolysers. In the electrolysers the catholyte con-
                      centration is increased back to 32 %.

                      Chemistry of electrolysis is covered in more detail in electrolysis chapter
                      (see chapter 6.2.2).

12.6       PART 6: NORMAL START-UP

12.6.1     GENERAL PRECONDITION
                      Following prerequisites are to be ensured before start-up of catholyte
                      system.

                      • Following systems should be in operation:
                        Cooling water, instrument air, nitrogen, demineralised water and low
                        pressure steam.
                      • Following systems should be ready for operation:
                        Rectifiers and electrolysers, brine system.
                      • All controllers are in AUTO mode.
                      • All interlocks are ACTIVE.
                      • Confirm the purity of demineralised water and caustic 32% before
                        start-up.



12.6.2     FINAL PREPARATION
                      Establish and confirm manpower requirement and that communication
                      systems between Central Control Room and field personnel is function-
                      ing.

12.6.3     INITIAL START-UP
                      • Start nitrogen supply to catholyte tank 41V-31101 A/B. Also fill seal
                        flushing system of catholyte pump 41P-31101 A/B with demin. water
                        and pressurize with plant air.
                      • Fill the catholyte tanks 41V-31101 A/B (41V-31202 A/B) with
                        32% NaOH and maintain level in this tank at minimum 60% level.
                      • Start the catholyte pump 41P-31101 A/B (41P-31201 A/B) fill the ca-
                        tholyte head tank 41V-31101 (41V-31202), till the catholyte head tank
                        overflows back to the catholyte tanks.
                        If the catholyte head tank is empty, sufficient 32% NaOH (Caustic)
                        must be available in the catholyte tank. Caustic can be transferred
                        from 32% NaOH intermediate storage tank to the catholyte tank to
                        meet the additional requirement of 32% NaOH or can be imported from
                        external source.
                      • Establish circulation in the catholyte system
                        Catholyte tank 41V-31101 A/B (41V-31201 A/B) → Catholyte Pump
                        41P-31101 A/B (41P-31102 A/B) → Catholyte heat exchangers
                        41E-31101(41E-31201) → (Catholyte head tank 41V-31101
                        (41V-31201) overflows to the catholyte tanks) → Catholyte header to
                        electrolysers → Catholyte cellroom bypass (Electrolyser in bypass) →
                        Catholyte header from electrolysers → Hydrogen separator
                        41V-31103 (41V-31203) → Catholyte tank. The level in the catholyte
                        tank should always be lower than 50%.
                      • Once the circulation is established through the cellroom bypass valve,
                        electrolysers can be taken for filling (see chapter 6, Start-up of First
                        Electrolyser, Filling of Electrolyser). Accordingly, cooling or heating of
                        the catholyte system by cooling water or steam respectively is to be
                        carried out in the catholyte heat exchanger 41E-31101 (41E-31201 or
                        41E-31102 (41E-31202).
                      • Once electrolysers are filled, establish catholyte circulation through
                        electrolyser and close the cellroom bypass valve. Check caustic con-
                        centration by opening of 2“ recycle line from product line to catholyte
                        tanks.
                      • Heat up the electrolysers (see chapter 6, Start-up of First Electrolyser,
                        Heating of Electrolysers) by heating up catholyte in catholyte heat ex-
                        changers 41E-31101 (41E-31201) (max. up to 85 °C) for the start-up
                        of electrolyser. The outlet temperature of the electrolysers should be >
                        75 °C (see also chapter 6). During heating of the catholyte system the

12.7.2        TROUBLE SHOOTING
                          The following trouble shooting discusses upset conditions of the catholyte
                          circulation which are considered to be serious.

                          In case of a rectifier shutdown or power failure, the catholyte dilution is
                          prevented through interlock closing the demineralised water (WDS) addi-
                          tion to the caustic circulation in order to protect the membranes by too low
                          NaOH concentration (see also chapter 6).
                          However, in case of upsets there is usually enough time for the operators
                          to eliminate the trouble. The necessary actions are summarised in the fol-
                          lowing table.

12.7.3     PERFORMANCE CHECK
                      Samples are to be taken from sample points, as per sample schedule (re-
                      fer to Analytical Manual).

                      The various parameters observed in FCS during normal operation must
                      continuously be monitored.

                      In the field following parameters should be monitored:

                      • Demin Water Level of seal pot.
                      • Catholyte pump 41P-31101 A/B (41P-31201 A/B) discharge pressure
                        PI3110101, PI3110102 (PI3120101, PI3120102).
                      • Temperature of cooling water return for catholyte heat exchangers
                        TI3110204 (TI3120204).
                      • Temperature of catholyte to the electrolysers TI3110101 (TI3120101).



12.7.4     REDUCED CAPACITY OPERATION
                      The catholyte of each train is designed to operate from 100% train capac-
                      ity to 40% train capacity.

                      The catholyte flow to each electrolyser has to be adjusted according to
                      load (see electrolyser operation).

                      The caustic pressure to the electrolyser is kept constant by speed control
                      of the pump independent of flow to the electrolysers.

                      The catholyte outlet temperature of the electrolysers has to be constant
                      (see chapter 5). Therefore switch over from cooling to heating of
                      catholyte system might be required.

                      No other special operational procedures are to be followed for reduced
                      capacity operation, since all process parameters are automatically con-
                      trolled, based on the operating plant load.

12.7.5     EFFLUENT AND RISK TO THE ENVIRONMENT
                      Steam condensate generated during catholyte heating in the catholyte
                      heat exchanger 41E-31101 (41E-31202) during plant start-up is cooled
                      by dilution with raw water to < 70 °C. The cooled condensate is collected
                      via pipeline in a pit and pumped to the the main waste water collection pit.

                      Any caustic spillage in the process building is collected in a pit. From this
                      pit, the alkaline waste water is pumped to the waste water system for neu-
                      tralisation of NaOH in the stream.


12.8       PART 8: NORMAL SHUTDOWN
                      The catholyte circulation should not be shutdown unless it is necessary.

                      Caution For a shutdown of the catholyte system, the electrolysers have
                              to be shutdown before the catholyte system is shutdown.


                      The shutdown can be categorised as brief or long shutdown.



12.8.1     BRIEF SHUTDOWN OR SHUTDOWN FOR LONGER PERIOD
                      • For electrolysers shutdown refer to chapter 6.
                      • Stop all utilities (i.e. cooling water, steam and demineralised water), to
                        the catholyte system, if required.
                      • Shutdown the catholyte system (i.e. stop the catholyte pump
                        41P-31101 A/B (41P-31201 A/B), if required.
                      • Ensure sufficient space for catholyte head tank volume in catholyte
                        tank.


                      Note:       Do not shutdown seal water to pumps.

12.8.1.1   Filling of Catholyte System from Intermediate Storage Tanks
                      After long term shut down of catholyte system or if caustic concentration
                      in catholyte system is too low for start-up of electrolysers (see chapter 5)
                      it is possible to pump caustic from intermediate storage tank back into
                      catholyte tanks:

                      • Close block valves in caustic line to caustic evaporation unit (also
                        upstream of flow meter 41FT3110201 (41FT3120201)).
                      • Open 2“ recycle line to catholyte tanks downstream of flow meter.

                        41P-32007.

                      Note:       Tank sample before refilling catholyte system. Use caustic
                                  from intermediate storage tanks only if concentration and im-
                                  purities are within the quality limits!

12.9       PART 9: EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN

12.9.1     EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN OF UNIT
                      • In case of power failure, catholyte pump 41P-31101 A/B
                        (41P-31201 A/B) connected to emergency power system will restart.
                        Catholyte from the head tank will flow by gravity to the cells, if pumps
                        are not running.
                      • The level in the catholyte tank should be kept at 40% at all times to
                        ensure sufficient volume for volume of head tank in the case of power
                        failure.
                      • Check whether demineralised water addition to catholyte is stopped.
                      • Ensure that the concentration of catholyte in the circulation loop is
                        greater than 28%. Please also refer to chapter 6, Electrolysis.

12.9.3     START-UP FROM EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN
                      Once power supply is established, the catholyte pump connected to the
                      emergency power, will switch over to normal power supply.

                      • Ensure that the concentration of catholyte in the circulation loop is
                        greater than 28%.
                      • In case concentration is less than 28%, fill the catholyte tank with fresh
                        32% NaOH from intermediate caustic storage tank 41TK32001 A/B,
                        using 32% NaOH transfer pump 41P-3207 (see chapter 7.8.1.1).
                      • Before start-up adjust the temperature of catholyte in the loop at 75 °C
                        outlet temperature of electrolysers by heating with steam in the catho-
                        lyte heater 41E-31101 (41E-31201).

12.10.5    SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS, SPECIFIC INSTRUCTIONS PER UNIT
                      The hazardous chemicals handled in the catholyte system is caustic soda
                      (30% to 32%).

                      Should an accident occur, immediate first aid is imperative.

                      For details of precautionary measures and safety instructions in case of
                      an accident involved with handling caustic soda, please refer to
                      chapter 1.8.

                      The catholyte drain header and catholyte tank are purged with nitrogen in
                      order to avoid hydrogen accumulation in the catholyte system.



12.10.5.1 Handling hazardous materials

12.10.5.1.1Danger caused by caustic soda/catholyte
                      Caustic soda/catholyte is handled in this system.

                      Danger caused by caustic soda/catholyte!
                      Harmfull! Very corrosive. Causes severe burns. May cause serious
                      permanent eye damage. Very harmful by ingestion. Harmful by skin
                      contact or by inhalation of dust.

                      Observe following safety phrases:

                      • In case of contact with eyes, rinse immediately with plenty of water and
                        seek medical advice!
                      • Wear rubber or PVC gloves. Wear eye/face protection!
                      • In case of accident or if you feel unwell, seek medical advice immedi-
                        ately!
