13.2       PART 2: DESCRIPTION OF PROCESS

13.2.1     TECHNICAL PRINCIPLES
                      The caustic evaporation unit is designed for the production of max. 2020
                      tpd. NaOH 50%. The unit is common for both trains and is fed by 32%
                      caustic out of the catholyte system of the trains (see chapter 7).

                      The minimum capacity of the evaporation lies at 20% of 2020 tpd, i. e. 404
                      tons/day NaOH 100%.

                      To evaporate the 32% cell liquor high pressure steam from outside B. L.
                      is used. The steam condensate is pumped back to B. L. while the process
                      condensate is used in the brine system for water balance.

                      The unit consists of the following components:

                      • First effect falling film evaporator with vapour separator
                      • Condensation system for vacuum vapours and vapour condensate
                        collector/recycling system
                      • Second effect falling film evaporator with vapour separator
                      • Third effect falling film evaporator with vapour separator
                      • Heat recuperation system to pre-heat the caustic solution
                      • Instrumentation and control system designed to operate the process
                        plant.



13.2.2     UNIT DESCRIPTION

13.2.2.1   Process Description
                      The plant is designed for continuous concentration of 2020 tons per day
                      (as NaOH 100%) of NaOH 32% out of both trains of the membrane cell
                      electrolysis of both trains up to NaOH 50% at 45°C.

                      The concentration is done in a triple effect plant with indirect process va-
                      pour condensation. The plant mainly consists of three falling film evapo-
                      rators.



                                                          Doc. ID-Code                          Rev.
Copyright 2005 Uhde GmbH
                                                    8408205-CB-PR-MNL-0102                       02
                                         PVC Arvand
                                       Operating Manual
                                                                       National Petrochemical comany
                 SAZE H
                 C O NSU LTANTS              C/A Plant                 Arvand Petrochemical
                                                                            Company
Uhde Project No: 03-3039           Sazeh Project No: 8047           Owner Project No: 8408205
Job Code:        PVC Arvand        Job Code:                        Owner Job Code: PVC Arvand
                                                                                      Page 794 of 967


                      The 32% caustic liquid is fed into the falling film evaporator first effect
                      41E-32051. On product side (tube side) this effect operates under a vac-
                      uum of 0.14 bar(a). During one single pass through the first effect, the
                      caustic is concentrated up to approx. NaOH 36,5%. It is heated on the
                      shell side by process vapours from the second effect, falling film evapo-
                      rator second effect 41E-32052. The process vapours generated in the
                      first effect are condensed in surface condenser 41E-32054. Inert gases
                      are sucked off by the steam ejector group.

                      After the first effect, the NaOH 36,5% solution is pumped by pump 41P-
                      32051 A/B, in parallel through the plate heat exchangers 41E-32055 and
                      41E-32056, to the falling film evaporator second effect 41E-32052.

                      In the plate heat exchanger 41E-32055 the caustic is pre-heated from ap-
                      prox. 72.8°C to approx. 120.9°C by cooling the NaOH 50%, and in the
                      plate heat exchanger 41E-32056 by cooling the steam condensate.

                      The falling film evaporator second effect 41E-32052 is heated by the
                      process vapours from the third effect. The process condensate is led via
                      the vapour condensate flash tank 41V-32053 to the vapour condensate
                      tank 41V-32051.

                      The flashed process vapours from vapour condensate flash tank 41V-
                      32053 are led together with the process vapours from the second effect
                      falling film evaporator to the heating side (shell side) of the falling film
                      evaporator first effect 41E-32051.

                      From the tube side of the second effect falling film evaporator 41E-32052
                      the caustic soda solution is fed by pump 41P-32052 A/B, in parallel
                      through the tube bundle heat exchangers 41E-32057 and 41E-32058 to
                      the falling film evaporator third effect 41E-32053.

                      In the heat exchangers 41E-32057 and 41E-32058, the caustic is pre-
                      heated from approx. 123.9°C to approx. 181.3°C by cooling the NaOH
                      50% and the steam condensate.

                      In the falling film evaporator third effect 41E-32053, the caustic achieves
                      the final concentration of 50%. The operating pressure on product side
                      (tube side) in the falling film evaporator third effect 41E-32053 is 3.8 bar
                      (a). This effect is heated by steam at a pressure of 17.5 bar (a). The
                      steam condensate flows via steam condensate tank 41V-32052 working



                                                          Doc. ID-Code                          Rev.
Copyright 2005 Uhde GmbH
                                                    8408205-CB-PR-MNL-0102                       02
                                         PVC Arvand
                                       Operating Manual
                                                                        National Petrochemical comany
                 SAZE H
                 C O NSU LTANTS              C/A Plant                  Arvand Petrochemical

                                                                                       Page 795 of 967


                      as a steam trap - through the two heat exchangers 41E-32058 and 41E-
                      32056 where it is cooled down to approx. 90°C.

                      Before feeding the steam to falling film evaporator third effect it will be de-
                      superheated in steam condensate tank 41V-32052 by flowing through a
                      cooled packed tower. When leaving the steam condensate tank the
                      steam is saturated at 17.5 bar abs (205.7°C).

                      The 50% caustic soda solution is pumped by pump 41P-32053 A/B
                      through the three heat exchangers 41E-32057; 41E-32055 and 41E-
                      32059 with a temperature of approx. 189.3°C, and leaves the plant at a
                      temperature of 45°C. The heat exchanger 41E-32057 is cooled by NaOH
                      41.7%, whereas the heat exchangers 41E-32055 is cooled by NaOH
                      36,5%. In the last heat exchanger 41E-32059, the caustic is cooled by
                      cooling water.

                      The process condensate from falling film evaporator first effect 41E-
                      32051 and falling film evaporator second effect 41E-32052 as well as
                      from the surface condenser 41E-32054 is collected in the vapour conden-
                      sate tank 41V-32051 and then pumped by pump 41P-32051 A/B to the
                      battery limit.

                      Operating Flexibility

                      The minimum capacity of the evaporation unit lies at 20% of 2020 tpd,
                      i. e. 404 tons/day NaOH 100%.

                      The required minimum flow of pumps 41P-32051 A/B, 41P-32052 A/B
                      and 41P-32053 A/B is higher. In order to nevertheless operate the de-
                      sired partial load, caustic must be recirculated via bypass. The minimum
                      required flow is controlled automatically by flow control loop
                      41FIC3200201, 41FIC3200401 and 41FIC3200501.

13.2.2.2   Basic Description of Evaporation
                      Evaporation

                      The falling film evaporators are designed as tube bundle falling film evap-
                      orator. In the falling film evaporator head, the caustic soda is evenly dis-
                      tributed via slotted sleeves to the tubes.




                                                          Doc. ID-Code                           Rev.
Copyright 2005 Uhde GmbH
                                                    8408205-CB-PR-MNL-0102                        02

                                         Operating Manual

                                                                                        Page 796 of 967


                      The caustic soda leaves the tube bundle and reaches the vapour separa-
                      tor installed under the falling film evaporator.

                      The vapours produced in the evaporators leave the separators via a de-
                      mister consisting of extremely fine wire meshing which permits the sepa-
                      ration of even smallest caustic droplets carried along by the vapours.

                      The liquid caustic is collected in the lower part of the separator. A con-
                      stant liquid level will be maintained by a level control system.

                      Water Recuperation System

                      • Process Condensate System:
                        In the vapour condensate tank 41V-32051, the process condensate
                        from the shell side of falling film evaporator 41E-32051, the shell side
                        of falling film evaporator 41E-32052, and from the surface condenser
                        41E-32054 is collected. From there, the process condensate is fed by
                        the process condensate pump 41P-32054 A/B to the condensate tank
                        41V-34001 to be used in the brine system for water balance.
                      • Cooling Water System:
                        Cooling water is supplied to following users:
                             • Surface condenser 41E-32054/320E054 (Type I)
                             • Heat exchanger 41E-32059/320E059 (Type II)
                             • Inter Surface Condenser 41E-32060/320E060 and Final Surface
                               Condenser 41E-32061/320E061 from steam ejector group
                               (Type I)
                      • Waste Water System:
                        The following wastes leave the plant via a waste water trench:
                             • all wash water from washing floors and equipment, drainages, etc.
                             • waste water from body and eye showers
                             • waste water from steam ejector group
                             • relief valves in NaOH lines
                             • flushing water of pump seals.
                      • Steam and Steam Condensate System:
                        Steam is used for heating of falling film evaporator 41E-32053. The
                        steam condensate is led back to battery limit via steam condensate
                        tank 41V-32052 heat exchangers 41E-32058 and 41E-32056. The

13.3       PART 3: DESCRIPTION OF PLANT CONTROL

                      Product Side (NaOH)

                      • NaOH Flow Control:
                        The plant capacity is controlled by external flow controller in the NaOH
                        32% line. The actual flow is continuously registered by flow totaliser
                        FIQ3110201/FIQ3120201. Minimum plant capacity lies at 20% of de-
                        sign load, i.e. at 404 tons/day NaOH 100%, or at 40.54 m³/h of NaOH
                        32%.

                          Capacity range of falling film evaporators and NaOH pumps is sub-
                          stantially lower. In order to be able nevertheless to operate the desired
                          partial load, caustic soda must be recirculated automatically via by-
                          pass.

                          WARNING:
                          Operation of evaporator and pumps below above mentioned fig-
                          ures can harm the equipment seriously.

                          In front of each falling film evaporator the NaOH feed is indicated/re-
                          corded and low flow will activate an alarm and will trip the NaOH 32%
                          flow (external feed valve closed) and steam supply to evaporator 41E-
                          32053 (41TV3200501 closed), low flow will trip the relevant pump.


                             Note:   The flow to the unit has to be reduced slowly to avoid too
                                     high concentration at third effect and possible blockage of
                                     heat exchangers caused by crystalisation of caustic.


                      • Level Control 41E-32051 (Loop 41LIC3200201):
                        Inside the vapour separator of the falling film evaporator 41E-32051
                        the caustic soda liquid level is kept constant by level controller
                        41LIC3200201, in order to avoid dry running and cavitation of the sub-
                        sequent caustic soda pump and overfilling of the evaporator.

                          Too high and too low levels of the caustic soda are first signalled by an
                          alarm.

                      Steam Heating System

                      • NaOH 50% Concentration Control of Caustic Soda Solution (Loop
                        41TIC3200501):
                        The 50% caustic soda solution leaves the falling film evaporator 41E-
                        32053 at boiling temperature. This temperature is kept constant by
                        changing the steam pressure on heating side of the falling film evapo-
                        rator, which is done by temperature controller 41TIC3200501. The ac-
                        tual temperature is continually recorded.

                          The concentration of NaOH in the third effect evaporator is calculated
                          automatically (41AI3200501) from the temperature (41TI3200501) and
                          pressure inside (41PI3200501) and reported on the screen.
                          The concentration can also be taken from the boiling curve.

                          The nominal value (set-point) for temperature controller
                          41TIC3200501 is to be determined (= boiling temperature) and de-
                          pending on the boiling pressure inside.

                          Too high temperature is alarmed by 41TIC3200501 SAHH and close
                          the steam valve (41TV3200501) and NaOH 32% feed valve.

                      • Level Control Steam Condensate Tank (Loop 41LIC3200503):
                        The level control, by a level controller 41LIC3200503 in the steam con-
                        densate tank 41V-32052 primarily functions as a steam trap and as a
                        secondary task it keeps the steam condensate system under pressure,
                        thus to use the steam condensate to pre heat the caustic soda solution
                        in the heat exchangers 41E-32058 and 41E-32057. To avoid an over-
                        flow of the tank, a high level will be signalled by level alarm. The actual
                        operating pressure can be read at the pressure instrument
                        41PI3200505.

13.6       PART 6: NORMAL START-UP



13.6.1     GENERAL PRECONDITION
                      Prior to start-up of the caustic concentration unit, the following prerequi-
                      sites must be fulfilled:

                      • Following systems are in operation:
                        Cooling water circulation, plant air, instrument air, demineralised wa-
                        ter, nitrogen system, steam unit, catholyte system, caustic intermedi-
                        ate storage and caustic soda storage unit.
                      • Caustic soda 32% will be available either direct from catholyte system
                        or from caustic intermediate storage at normal operating conditions.
                      • All interlocks of above items are active


                      Also the following conditions must be fulfilled in order to ensure trouble-
                      free start-up and operation of the plant:

                      • The operating staff must be familiar with the operation and layout of the
                        plant (know-how of flow sheets and P+I diagrams).
                      • The operating staff must know the mode of operation and the mainte-
                        nance instructions for every single apparatus and for all parts of the
                        plant (know-how of the operating and maintenance manuals, mechan-
                        ical catalogues).
                      • The pre-commissioning of the various parts of equipment and plant
                        parts must have been performed completely and should be completed
                        by then.
                      • It is very important that the temporary strainers are removed from the
                        pipes before the final start-up with caustic soda.
                      • Safety showers and first aid equipment must be ready for use.

13.6.3     INITIAL START-UP
                      Start-up sequences are as follows:

                      • Fill process condensate collection tank 41V-32051 with demineralised
                        water, in order to guarantee sealing of the barometrically immersed
                        pipes, until 41LIC3200601 show approx. 50%.
                      • Fill the steam condensate tank 41V-32052 with demineralised water or
                        steam condensate such that all equipment and piping between the
                        tank and the level control valve 41LV3200503 are filled with liquid, lev-
                        el controller 41LIC3200503 shows approx. 10%, such as control valve
                        41LV3200503 is closed.
                      • There are four ventilating valves to atmosphere and two valves to the
                        vacuum system (via surface condenser) on the shell side of falling film
                        evaporator 41E-32051. Open the ventilation to the atmosphere and
                        make sure that ventilation to the vacuum system (via surface
                        condenser) are closed.

                          Also open the ventilation to the atmosphere on the shell side of falling
                          film evaporator 41E-32052.

                          Ventilation to the atmosphere on the shell side of falling film evaporator
                          41E-32053 remains closed.
                      • Open the shut-off valve of the steam trap at the inlet of the process
                        condensate flash tank 41V-32053
                      • Start the cooling water flow through the surface condenser 41E-32054,
                        the caustic cooler 41E-32059 and the steam ejector group.
                      • To fill the evaporation plant with caustic soda:
                             • Adjust external flow controller and level controllers 41LIC320201,
                               41LIC320401, 41LIC320501 to manual operation. Open the
                               valves by changing the manual value of the controller to ca. 10%.
                             • Start external caustic feed pump: The caustic is fed to evaporator
                               41E-32051.

13.7       PART 7: NORMAL OPERATION

13.7.1     NORMAL ROUTINE OF OPERATION

13.7.1.1   Operation Tips and Instructions
                      The plant has been designed for the production ranges indicated in chap-
                      ter 12.2.1. Best efficiency is achieved when operating the plant at nominal
                      capacity. The values indicated in the project documentation are applica-
                      ble to nominal capacity operation and may vary considerably when oper-
                      ating at a fraction of the nominal capacity.

                      Lifetime of the various plant components depends very much on the
                      mode of operation. Therefore, continuous operation should be aimed at,
                      at least with respect to the evaporation unit, since:

                      • repeated start-ups and shutdowns of the evaporation unit increase cor-
                        rosion of the equipment made of nickel. At every new start-up, the nick-
                        el oxide film that protects the inside walls of the tubes from corrosion
                        is washed off.



13.7.1.2   Nickel Absorption in the Plant
                      Certain operating conditions produce an unacceptably high nickel ab-
                      sorption of the caustic soda in the evaporation unit and, in consequence,
                      damages to the plant and to the wear and tear parts are increased. The
                      following operating conditions in particular lead to an increased nickel ab-
                      sorption:

                      • Atmospheric oxygen intrusion into nickel-made apparatus
                      • Increased NaClO3 content in the 32% NaOH feed (max. allowable: 19
                        ppm).
                      In order to eliminate immediately any increase of corrosion, check at least
                      once a day the nickel contents of the evaporated caustic by means of a
                      chemical analysis. For additional safety proceed with a double analysis.

                      After shutdowns with a duration of more than 1/2 year and prior to the new
                      start-up, all nickel-made elements must be carefully cleaned.

13.7.1.3   Keeping Graphs and Charts
                      Warranty claims are only accepted if the present instructions have been
                      followed closely. Therefore, all recording charts and graphs must be kept
                      until the end of the warranty period. In case of warranty claims, all charts
                      and graphs must be submitted to Bertrams to prove that the plant was op-
                      erated correctly.



13.7.1.4   Plant Supervision
                      The plant has been designed with priority on automatic operation. How-
                      ever, supervision shall be done with the utmost care since the caustic
                      soda constitutes potential dangers.

                      At start-up

                      Whenever starting-up the plant, it is indispensable to walk continuously
                      through the plant and check that the programmed operating conditions
                      are achieved and that all systems operate according to specifications.

                      Two hours after having achieved operating conditions, take samples and
                      analyse the following products:

                      • Caustic soda feed 32%
                      • Caustic soda solution 50%.
                      Eight hours after having reached operating conditions, take samples and
                      analyse the caustic soda feed and caustic soda solution.

                      Controls to be performed every shift

                      • Check and re-adjust the manual controls, if necessary (distribution of
                        NaOH to heat exchanger, cooling water, etc.).

                      • Check functions of machines (abnormal noises and temperature in-
                        creases etc., leakage at seals etc.).
                      • Inspection walk through the plant. Pay attention to:
                                  •     Leakages
                                  •     Pressure indicators, temperature indicators and level indi-
                                        cators
                                  •     Noise of pumps
                                  •     Temperature of motors and pumps
                                  •     Vibration of motors, pumps, piping etc.
                                  •     Damages at the equipment and instruments.


                      Read instruments and write operating report

                      • Check the instruments especially those which aren't monitored in the
                        control room. Read the values and write them down once per shift.
                      • Check all local instruments at least once per shift.
                      • Check all inspection glasses at least once per shift.


                      Controls to be performed once a year

                      (for the first time 4 months after initial start-up)

                      After one year, the entire plant shall be subject to a complete overhaul,
                      permitting to detect possible abnormal wear and to eliminate its causes
                      in time.

                      out.

13.7.1.5   Calculation of the Concentration of NaOH
                      In each falling film evaporator the calculation of NaOH concentration is
                      done automatically by using following formula.

                      w = A*p2*T2 + B*p2*T + C*T2 + D*p*T2 + E*p*T + F*p + G*p2 + H*T + I

                      with:

                      • p         pressure in bar abs
                      • T         Temperature in °C
                      • w weight


                      The formula gives as result the concentration of NaOH as weight. The re-
                      sult has to be multiply by 100 to get Concentration as weight%.

13.7.2     TROUBLE SHOOTING
                      In the following it is only referred to such operating problems of the falling
                      film evaporators and the surface condenser, which are not indicated by
                      an alarm signal or otherwise.


13.7.2.1   Final Concentration of Caustic Soda Solution below 50% NaOH
                      Steam pressure does not correspond to the working pressure of falling
                      film evaporator third effect 41E-32053:

                      • Check set-point of 41TIC3200501 by means of Boiling Curve (see
                        chapter 12.6.3) for NaOH 50% and the pressure on product side of fall-
                        ing film evaporator third effect (41PI3200501).

                      Plant capacity higher than 2020 tons/day:

                      • Check flow measurement 41FI3200302.

                      Feed concentration lower than 32%:

                      • Decrease feed flow.

                      Condensate back draft:

                      • Due to an obstruction, the condensate flows back through the chan-
                        nels and dissolves the already evaporated caustic. This is the case
                        when the temperature of the vapour separators does no longer corre-
                        spond with the pressure and concentration according to the boiling
                        curve. Check the vapour condensate lines if obstructions occur.


13.7.2.2   Capacities of falling film evaporator 41E-32051 decrease
                      This can be recognised by the following indications:

                      • The concentration step in falling film evaporator 41E-32051 decreas-
                        es, pressure on shell side increases.
                      • Pressure on surface condenser 41E-32054 is higher than 0,14 bar (a),
                        to be indicated on pressure indicator 41PI3200605.

                      • Check the cooling water flow and its outlet temperature (41TI3200606)
                        from surface condenser 41E-32054. Increase the cooling water flow.
                      • Inert gases on shell side of evaporator 41E-32051:
                             • Make sure that ventilation to the atmosphere is tight.
                             • Open carefully both ventilation valves to the surface condenser
                               41E-32054/320E054, only some turns for some minutes. At the
                               same time, the pressure on shell side and on product side must be
                               observed.
                             • On shell side, the pressure may not drop more than 0,1 bar while
                               on product side the pressure may not rise more than 0,05 bar. This
                               is very important in order to prevent a collapse of the vacuum on
                               product side.

                      This can be recognised by the following indications:

                      • The concentration step in falling film evaporators 41E-32052 and 41E-
                        32053 decreases, plant capacity decreases, pressure on shell side in-
                        creases.
                      • Inert gases on shell side of evaporators 41E-32052; 41E-32053
                      • Open slightly the ventilation valve to the atmosphere on shell side until
                        vapour or steam streams out.

13.7.3     PERFORMANCE CHECK
                      There are many parameters in the system that will indicate the perform-
                      ance of the system and help operators make adjustments. These param-
                      eters can easily be trended to aid in long-term performance analysis and
                      trouble shooting.

                      • Samples of the feed and the product from each evaporator should be
                        taken to measure the caustic concentration.
                      • The temperatures and operating pressure of the system should also be
                        monitored on an hourly basis using log sheets.
                        These parameters can act as a signal to the operators of potential
                        problems. It will also help familiarize personnel with the system and its
                        normal operating conditions.
                      • The conductivity of the process condensate should also be monitored.
                        A high conductivity is evidence of carryover from the evaporators.
                      • During normal operation the process parameters mentioned under
                        Section 12.7.1 and 12.7.2 must be recorded/documented.
                      Note:       The importance of keeping a written data log cannot be over-
                                  emphasized as it forces the operator to observe the operation
                                  of the entire system, it reveals long term trends, and it is an in-
                                  valuable aid when trouble shooting.

13.7.4     REDUCED CAPACITY OPERATION
                      The caustic evaporation unit has been designed for a minimum turn down
                      ratio of 20% of nominal load (2020 tpd) i.e. 404 tpd NaOH 100%.

                      Operation below 20% increases the risk of drying and blockage of the fall-
                      ing film system and difficulties in the heat balance.

13.7.4.1   Normal operation with reduced capacity
                      The capacity of the electrolysers are 2,000 tpd, produced in two trains.

                      The turn down ratio of the electrolysers is 40%.

                      When only one train at min. load (40%) is in operation the production is
                      400 tpd NaOH 100% which equals the min. load (20%) of the evaporation
                      unit.

                      Therefore, in case the caustic evaporation unit is running at minimum
                      load, the electrolysers are itself running at reduced capacity and the flow
                      of 32% NaOH to the caustic evaporation unit is controlled to maintain a
                      constant level in the catholyte tank.

                      In such a case the steam flow to the evaporators and other process pa-
                      rameters in this unit get automatically adjusted.

                      Note:       The flow to the unit has to be reduced slowly to avoid too high
                                  concentration at third effect and possible blockage of heat ex-
                                  changers caused by crystalisation of caustic.



13.7.4.2   Intermediate storage tanks (41TK32001 A/B)
                      For more flexibility two intermediate storage tanks with 1,600 m3 volume
                      each are foreseen.

                      Normally these storage tanks are empty.



13.7.4.3   Reduced capacity operation with flexibility
                      It is possible to run the caustic operation unit at reduced capacity with the
                      electrolysers running at full capacity.

                      In such a case, the excess 32% NaOH production is stored in the inter-
                      mediate storage tanks.

                      However, this is possible only for about 12 hours, since the intermediate
                      storage tanks will get completely filled.

                      Also it is possible to run the electrolysers with minimum capacity, when
                      the caustic evaporation unit is stopped. In such a case, the storage ca-
                      pacity of the intermediate storage tanks reaches for about 36 hours.

13.8       PART 8: NORMAL SHUTDOWN

13.8.1     Short-term shutdown
                      Provided that the plant shutdown is only to last up to max. 7 days, and
                      that the ambient temperature does not fall below 25°C, a short-term shut-
                      down may be performed. If this is not the case, proceed according to
                      chapter 'Long-term Shutdown'.

                      • Turn off the steam flow to falling film evaporator 41E-32053.
                      • Feed NaOH 32% to the plant until the concentration in the equipment
                        is 32%. The Pumps 41P-32051A/B; 41P-32052A/B; 41P-32053A/B
                        are still running. The freezing Point of 32% caustic is lower then 50%
                        which helps to avoid freezing (s. Freezing Points).
                      • Close the bypass valve at the three falling film evaporators.
                      • Stop the caustic soda flow by stopping the caustic soda pumps, i.e. ex-
                        ternal feed pump / external flow control valve and pumps 41P-32051A/
                        B; 41P-32052 A/B; 41P-32053 A/B.
                      • Stop the steam ejector group, vapour condensate pump 41P-32054A/
                        B.
                      • Turn off cooling water supply.
                      Under the above-mentioned conditions it is not necessary to drain the
                      plant.

                      Then proceed as follows:

                      Draining of the Plant
                      Open the ventilation valves to the atmosphere and drain the whole evap-
                      oration system, i.e. caustic soda lines and all utility lines. Make sure that
                      the temperature in the draining system is not higher then 50°C.

                      Washing of the Plant
                      After draining, the whole caustic soda lines consisting of the three falling
                      film evaporators shall be let cool down and flushed with soft water, and
                      then be emptied again.

                      Regarding procedures for long-term shut-down of apparatus and machin-
                      ery, see the corresponding Operating and Maintenance Manuals of the
                      various items (mechanical catalogues).

13.10.5    SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS, SPECIFIC INSTRUCTIONS PER UNIT
                      The hazardous chemicals handled in the caustic evaporation unit is caus-
                      tic soda (32% to 50%).

                      Should an accident occur, immediate first aid is imperative.

                      For details of precautionary measures and safety instructions in case of
                      an accident involved with handling caustic soda, please refer to chapter
                      1.8.



13.10.5.1 Handling Hazardous Materials



13.10.5.1.1Danger caused by caustic soda/catholyte
                      Caustic soda/catholyte is handled in this system.

                      Danger caused by caustic soda/catholyte!
                      Harmfull! Very corrosive. Causes severe burns. May cause serious
                      permanent eye damage. Very harmful by ingestion. Harmful by skin
                      contact or by inhalation of dust.

                      Observe following safety phrases:

                      • In case of contact with eyes, rinse immediately with plenty of water and
                        seek medical advice!
                      • Wear rubber or PVC gloves. Wear eye/face protection!
                      • In case of accident or if you feel unwell, seek medical advice immedi-
                        ately!



13.10.5.2 Directions for Safe Operation and Inspection
                      Please refer to chapter 1.8, Safety Instructions.

14.2       PART 2: DESCRIPTION OF PROCESS


14.2.1     TECHNOLOGICAL PRINCIPLES
                      The 50% caustic storage system is designed for the storage of the 50%
                      caustic soda solution, which is produced in the caustic evaporation plant.

                      The 50% caustic storage system consists of two storage tanks, each with
                      a capacity of 30,000 m3, of pumps and piping systems with various inter-
                      locks and controls.

                      The pumps are used for the following purposes:

                      • Caustic soda circulation back to the 50% storage tanks.
                      • Caustic soda loading of trucks.
                      • Caustic soda loading of ships.

                      At a filling rate of about 100 m3/h the total retention time of 50% caustic
                      soda in the storage tanks is about 20 - 25 days of production.

                      The operating strategy proposed for the 50% NaOH storage system is, to
                      use either one for filling, while the other tank is on stand-by (full) or being
                      drained to ships and/or trucks.

                      The storage tanks can be unloaded to the ship loading system via the
                      ship loading station 41U-33050 at a rate of 800 m3/h.

                      Note:       The pipe routing to the jetty and the final location of the ship
                                  loading arm is not yet established (about 7 km away), Change
                                  Order 018.

                      The filling station for trucks is designed for a capacity of 40 m3/h, and is
                      located next to the 50% caustic storage tanks.

                      A set of pumps with mixing jets will provide circulation of the caustic soda
                      from the storage tanks back to the storage tanks.

                      The circulation system will not be operated while loading a ship.

14.2.2     UNIT DESCRIPTION
                      Caustic Soda at 50% by wt. of concentration is received from the plant
                      and stored within the Caustic Soda Storage Tanks (41TK33001 A/B) with
                      a volume of 30.000 m3 each. The storage tanks is fixed roof type, made
                      of carbon steel rubber lined material.
                      Each of the two tanks will be equipped with tank gauging system for ac-
                      curate level measurement and compensation, high and low level indica-
                      tors and temperature measurement. The tanks are located within a dike,
                      designed to hold the content of one tank.
                      Safety interlocks are provided to stop the feed into tank upon high liquid
                      level and to stop pumps on low level signal.

                      Tank filling, caustic soda circulation, ship loading and truck loading can
                      be selected with the respective selector switch in the FCS.



                      Filling

                      Tank A and/or B can be selected for filling. Filling of either tank, or both
                      of them can be activated if they have no high-high level.

                      When the storage tanks are ready for filling the caustic soda evaporation
                      plant can be started up.



                      50% NaOH Circulation

                      To avoid caustic layers with different concentration in the tank and in or-
                      der to slow down the 50% caustic soda solution from cooling down in pip-
                      ing and storage tanks a circulation loop is provided which circulates the
                      solution from a selected storage tank A or B with pumps 41P-33002 A or
                      B via mixing jets 41F-3300 A/B or C/D back to the respective storage
                      tank. No tank heating system is required. Each storage tank is equipped
                      with a pair of mixing jets.




                                                          Doc. ID-Code                          Rev.
Copyright 2005 Uhde GmbH
                                                    8408205-CB-PR-MNL-0102                       02
                                         PVC Arvand
                                       Operating Manual
                                                                        National Petrochemical comany
                 SAZE H
                 C O NSU LTANTS              C/A Plant                  Arvand Petrochemical

Job Code:        PVC Arvand        Job Code:                        Owner Job Code: PVC Arvand
                                                                                       Page 837 of 967


                      The mixing jets provide intensive mixing of circulating NaOH with the
                      NaOH inside the tank. The driving force is NaOH from the circulation
                      pumps. The mixing jets suck in a large volume of NaOH and force the
                      combined NaOH solution back into the liquid inside the tank.

                      Note:       The circulation shall not be operated when the same tank is
                                  being unloaded to a ship.



                      Ship Loading

                      Note:       Ship loading and use of NaOH 50% transfer pipeline is on
                                  HOLD due to Change Order 018.

                      The ship loading system consists of the 50% NaOH storage tanks
                      41TK33001 A or B, transfer pumps 41P-33001 A or B, the 16“pipeline, the
                      loading facility at the jetty and the pigging system. The loading facilities at
                      the dock has a marine arm, having its own electro-hydraulic control and
                      operating system. The system is designed to load 800 m3/h of 50% caus-
                      tic soda onto ocean going tankers with 5,000 - 45,000 DWT. The product
                      line is attached to the support structure by means of special mountings
                      which also compensate for thermal expansion or contraction due to tem-
                      perature variations to avoid over stressing, where applicable.

                      The ship loading operation will be completely monitored, controlled and
                      safety interlocked at the jetty on the loading arm control panel. In case of
                      any emergency, the loading operation may be stopped by pushing the
                      emergency push bottom.

                      The sequence of the shut-down will stop the ship loading pumps
                      41P-33001 A/B. The same sequence will activate the closure of the jetty
                      valve 41XV3300301.

                      A surge relief valve and drain vessel at jetty is provided to avoid liquid
                      hammer in the pipeline during shut-down of system.

                      Note:       While unloading one tank the produced caustic for evaporation
                                  unit shall be filled in the other tank.

                      Truck loading

                      A filling station is located near the 50% caustic storage tanks for filling of
                      trucks. The capacity for loading is designed for 40 m3/h. The 50% caustic
                      soda solution will be pumped to the trucks from the 50% caustic soda
                      storage tanks with truck loading pumps 41P-33003 A or B.

                      Truck loading is initiated from the FCS with selector switch 41HS3300104
                      „TRUCK LOADING“.



                      Pigging System / Draining of Pipelines

                      Note:       Pigging System is on HOLD due to Change Order 018.

                      An air driven pigging unit 41U-33070 for draining the pipeline during cold
                      weather periods (<12 °C) is provided. The pig launcher will be located
                      near the jetty and the pig receiver or trap will be located near the
                      50% NaOH storage tanks.

                      The pig has to be transported by truck from the receiver back to the
                      launcher.



14.2.3     PROCESS CHEMISTRY
                      The system handles 50% caustic soda (NaOH) only. Chemical reactions
                      do not take place, however temperature related sodification may take
                      place and has to be carefully avoided, e.g. by draining of pipes and circu-
                      lation.

14.6       PART 6: NORMAL START-UP

14.6.1     GENERAL PRE-CONDITION
                      Following pre-requisites are to be ensured before start-up of the 50%
                      caustic soda storage system, including ship and truck loading.

                      • Following systems should be in operation:
                        Instrument air, demineralised water and electrical power.
                      • Following systems should be ready for operation:
                        Rectifiers and electrolysers / 32% caustic soda intermediate storage
                        and caustic evaporation plant.
                      • All controllers are in AUTO mode.
                      • All interlocks are active.



14.6.2     FINAL PREPARATION
                             • Check valve positions in FCS.
                             • Check communication facilities between central control room and
                               50% caustic storage area.

                      Note:        When ship loading is activated, check communication with
                                   loading jetty.

14.6.3     INITIAL START-UP

14.6.3.1   50% Storage Tank Filling
                      The start-up of the 50% caustic soda storage tank system consists of:

                      • the filling of the tank (s)
                      • the circulation system.


                      For filling of the 50% caustic storage tank (s) 41TK33001 A/B the follow-
                      ing procedure applies:

                      A.)         Fill 50% caustic storage tank 41TK33001 A

                                  • Select tank A for filling by selecting tank A with selector switch
                                    41HS3300101 „TANK FILLING“
                                  • Filling valve 41XV3300107 will open
                                  • Filling valve 41XV3300108 will close
                                  • Start-up caustic evaporation plant and feed 50% caustic soda
                                    to storage tank A.

                             Note:    When tank A is full 41LS3300105 SAHH will close
                                      41XV3300107 and 41XV3300108 will open, filling of tank B
                                      will commence.



                      B.)         Fill 50% caustic storage tank 41TK33001 B

                                  • Select tank B for filling by selecting tank B with selector switch
                                    41HS3300101 „TANK FILLING“
                                  • Filling valve 41XV3300107 will close
                                  • Filling valve 41XV3300108 will open
                                  • Start-up caustic evaporation plant and feed 50% caustic soda
                                    to storage tank B.

                             Note:    When tank B is full 41LS3300106 SAHH will close
                                      41XV3300107 and will open 41XV3300108, thus filling of
                                      tank A will commence.

14.6.3.5   Pigging System
                      A pigging system will be provided to drain the caustic soda pipe back into
                      the storage tanks in case of disturbances at the ship loading station and
                      during cold weather periods (Temperature < 12°C).

                      The pig will be driven by air, the launcher will be located near the loading
                      jetty, the receiver trap near the 50% caustic soda storage tanks, that
                      means the pipe will be drained to the storage tank(s). For detail operating
                      procedure please refer to vendor documentation (HOLD due to Change
                      Order 018).

                      Note:       Throttle discharge valve of ship loading pump while filling the
                                  line after pigging.
                                  Vent air pockets at high point vents of pipeline during filling of
                                  line.

14.7.3     PERFORMANCE CHECK
                      Samples are to be taken from sample points as per sample schedule.
                      (Refer to Analytical Manual).

                      The various parameters observed in FCS during normal operation must
                      continuously be monitored.

                      In the field following parameters should be monitored:

                      • Truck loading pump discharge pressure
                      • Ship loading pump discharge pressure

                      • Check seal water in overflow pots.



14.7.4     REDUCED CAPACITY OPERATION
                      This plant section can be operated under reduced load without problems.

                      Check that minimum flows for pumps is available, otherwise shut-down
                      pumps.

                      The filling operations of the 50% NaOH storage tanks will depend on the
                      load of the caustic evaporation plant.

                      The loading operations of ships and trucks will normally run at full load
                      (100% capacity) to minimise loading times.

14.8       PART 8: NORMAL SHUTDOWN

14.8.1     NORMAL SHUTDOWN
                      The 50% NaOH storage tank system is normally operated as follows:

                      • Tank A or B is being filled with 50% NaOH from the caustic evaporation
                        plant.
                      • Tank A or B is being drained, unloaded to a ship or truck.


                      Therefore, the normal shutdown procedure during filling does not require
                      any action.

                      During unloading the normal shutdown requires to stop the pumps.



                      For Brief Shutdown

                      No actions required, except stopping of pumps.

                      Depending on ambient temperatures (< 12°C) draing of pipeline by use
                      of pigging system is required to avoid freezing of NaOH 50%.



14.8.2     SHUTDOWN FOR LONGER PERIOD
                      If the complete emptying of tanks is required, schedule the unloading with
                      trucks and ships. Connect temporary pipe / hose from low point of tank to
                      pump suction line to empty the last volume of caustic by truck loading
                      pump into trucks. So only minimum amounts of caustic have to be drained
                      into the waste water pit.

                      If a shutdown is scheduled during cold weather periods drain suction and
                      discharge lines at pumps to avoid plugging due to solidified caustic soda.
                      Empty ship loading pipeline by using the pigging system. The storage
                      tank filling line from caustic evaporation unit should be flushed with 32%
                      caustic via evaporation unit.

14.10.5    SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS, SPECIFIC INSTRUCTIONS PER UNIT

14.10.5.1 Handling Hazardous Materials
                      Please refer to chapter 1.8, SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS.

                      The hazardous chemical handled in this area is 50% NaOH. Should an
                      accident occur, immediate first aid is imperative.

                      For details of precautionary measures and safety instruction in case of an
                      accident with caustic soda, please refer to chapter 1, Safety and Health.




14.10.5.1.1Danger caused by caustic soda/catholyte
                      Caustic soda/catholyte is handled in this system.

                      Danger caused by caustic soda/catholyte!
                      Harmful! Very corrosive. Causes severe burns. May cause serious
                      permanent eye damage. Very harmful by ingestion. Harmful by skin
                      contact or by inhalation of dust.

                      Observe following safety phrases:

                      • In case of contact with eyes, rinse immediately with plenty of water and
                        seek medical advice!
                      • Wear rubber or PVC gloves. Wear eye/face protection!
                      In case of accident or if you feel unwell, seek medical advice immediately!



14.10.5.2 Directions for Safe Operation and Inspection
                      Follow all government regulations, labour laws and plant management
                      procedures when opening tanks, piping, instrumentation and valves.

15.2       PART 2: DESCRIPTION OF PROCESS

15.2.1     TECHNOLOGICAL PRINCIPLES
                      The hydrogen treatment systems of the electrolyser trains are designed
                      to handle the hydrogen produced in the electrolysers, equivalent to a total
                      chlorine production rate of 585,000 t/a and 330 days of operation per year
                      in both trains.

                      The hydrogen treatment system of each train, is designed for a produc-
                      tion of about 1,000 kg/h of hydrogen gas (100%).

                      Each hydrogen system treatment unit receives a normal wet hydrogen
                      flow rate of about 2,500 kg/h or 14,000 m3/h from the electrolysers (which
                      is saturated with water at 88 °C).

                      Each train of electrolysers is connected to one hydrogen system.

                      The systems consist of the treatment section, where cooling and filtering
                      of the gas is done, a condensate collection system and the hydrogen
                      stack.



15.2.2     UNIT DESCRIPTION
                      The hydrogen treatment is shown in the following P&I Diagrams:

                      Train 1: P&I Diagram 34101

                      Train 2: P&I Diagram 34201


                      Each train of the hydrogen system consists of:

                      • hydrogen cooler
                      • hydrogen filter
                      • hydrogen stack




                                                         Doc. ID-Code                          Rev.
Copyright 2005 Uhde GmbH
                                                   8408205-CB-PR-MNL-0102                       02
                                          PVC Arvand
                                        Operating Manual
                                                                        National Petrochemical comany
                 SAZE H
                 C O NSU LTANTS               C/A Plant                 Arvand Petrochemical
                                                                             Company
Uhde Project No: 03-3039            Sazeh Project No: 8047           Owner Project No: 8408205
Job Code:        PVC Arvand         Job Code:                        Owner Job Code: PVC Arvand
                                                                                       Page 860 of 967


                      The hydrogen condensate system which is common for both trains is
                      shown in:

                      P&I Diagram 34101

                      It consists of:

                      • Condensate tank
                      • Condensate pumps


                      Note:       Equipment numbers are for train 1, equipment numbers for
                                  train 2 are in brackets.

                      The hydrogen gas leaving the electrolysers has an overpressure of
                      240 mbar and a temperature of approx. 88 °C. It is saturated with water
                      over 32% NaOH solution at operating conditions.

                      The gas is cooled to approx. 55 °C by cooling water Type II (WS 02) in
                      hydrogen cooler 41E-34101 (41E-34201), where most of the water va-
                      pour condenses.

                      The gas from the hydrogen cooler is sent to the hydrogen filter
                      41FT34102 (41FT34202), which serves the purpose of removing droplets
                      of caustic in the hydrogen gas. Demineralised water (WDS) is sprayed
                      into the gas stream at the inlet of the filter to prevent the accumulation of
                      caustic on the filter surface.

                      Hydrogen gas from the filter is sent to the HCl synthesis unit (see chapter
                      17), to the EDC/PVC plant and to the stack(s).

                      The condensate from the hydrogen cooler, hydrogen filter, main piping
                      and piping to the HCl synthesis unit (see chapter 17) are collected in two
                      headers which overflow to the condensate tank 41V-34001, which is
                      common for both trains.

                      In the condensate tank also process condensate (vapour) from the caus-
                      tic evaporation unit and the alkaline waste water from the ion exchanger
                      regeneration is added.




                                                           Doc. ID-Code                          Rev.
Copyright 2005 Uhde GmbH
                                                     8408205-CB-PR-MNL-0102                       02
                                         PVC Arvand
                                       Operating Manual
                                                                       National Petrochemical comany
                 SAZE H
                 C O NSU LTANTS              C/A Plant                 Arvand Petrochemical
                                                                            Company
Uhde Project No: 03-3039           Sazeh Project No: 8047           Owner Project No: 8408205
Job Code:        PVC Arvand        Job Code:                        Owner Job Code: PVC Arvand
                                                                                      Page 861 of 967


                      The contents of the condensate tank 41V-34001 are then added to the
                      lean brine stream on level control 41LIC3410101 using condensate
                      pumps 41P-34001 A,B,C and represent one source of the make-up water
                      for the electrolysis process.

                      There are three condensate pumps, 2 operations and one spare.

                      The cell differential pressure in the electrolysers is controlled by the pres-
                      sure in the hydrogen system. Accordingly, the pressure in the hydrogen
                      system is maintained by 41PDIC0810311 (41PDIC0820311). A further in-
                      crease of pressure in the system is controlled by 41PDIC0810312
                      (41PDIC0820312), venting hydrogen into the atmosphere through stack
                      41X-34101 (41X-34201). At high loads of the electrolysers the differential
                      pressure is only controlled by 41PDIC0810312 (41PDIC0820312) via
                      stack due to a surplus of produced hydrogen.

                      The stack is also equipped with a silencer 41X-34101-I01
                      (41X-34201-I01) to reduce the noise by venting H2 through the stack.

                      A continuous nitrogen purge through the stack avoids air (O2) diffusion
                      into the stack.

                      Also continuous nitrogen purging is carried out in the vapour space above
                      the seal. By this the condensate tank 41V-34001 is purged with nitrogen
                      to avoid explosive atmosphere in the tank possibly caused by hydrogen.

                      In case of H2 igniters at the stack, steam can be added to extinguish the
                      fire at low electrolyser loads.

15.6       PART 6: NORMAL START-UP



15.6.1     GENERAL PRECONDITION
                      Prior to start-up of the hydrogen section, following prerequisites must be
                      fulfilled:

                      • Following systems are in operation:
                        Cooling water circulation, demineralised water, instrument air and ni-
                        trogen system.
                      • All controllers in AUTO mode.
                      • All interlocks are in ACTIVE.
                      • All liquid seals are filled with water.
                      • Following systems are ready for operation:
                        Rectifiers and electrolysers, HCl synthesis unit and H2 consumers at
                        EDC/VCM/PVC Plant.



15.6.2     FINAL PREPARATION
                      Establish / confirm communication lines between field and control room.

15.6.3     INITIAL START-UP
                      • Start cooling water circulation through hydrogen coolers 41E-34101
                        (41E-34201.
                      • Start the flow of demineralised water to the upstream of hydrogen filter.
                      • Fill the condensate header completely with demineralised water, till
                        overflow to the condensate tank 41V-34001 is observed in the sight
                        glass.
                      • Fill condensate tank 41V-34001 with demin water. Start two of the
                        condensate pumps 41P-34001 A/B/C. Put 41LIC3410101 in AUTO.
                      • Fill liquid seal at hydrogen stack with raw water.
                      • Start the flow of nitrogen to the following:
                             • Hydrogen stack 41X-34101 (41X-34201).
                             • Hydrogen piping downstream of hydrogen filter 41FT34201 (202).

                                                           Doc. ID-Code                          Rev.
Copyright 2005 Uhde GmbH

                                            PVC Arvand

Job Code:        PVC Arvand          Job Code:                        Owner Job Code: PVC Arvand
                                                                                        Page 866 of 967


                             • Condensate header overflow line to the condensate tank.
                             • Chlorine/hydrogen differential pressure is controlled by hydrogen
                               B-valve 41PDV0810323 (41PDV0820312) to stack. Nitrogen is
                               purged into hydrogen system by 41XV0810101 (41XV0820101) to
                               maintain overpressure.
                             • Controller of hydrogen A-valve 41PDV0810311 (41PDV0820311)
                               to EDC-Plant is in manual mode closed.
                      • Energise the electrolysers according to chapter 5, Start-up of first elec-
                        trolyser, energising the electrolyser.
                      Note:        Before starting the electrolysis the H2 System to be flushed
                                   with nitrogen until residual oxygen concentration is <0,5% v/v.

                      • Immediately after energising the cells the hydrogen will be discharged
                        via B-valve 41PDV0810312 (41PDV0820312) on auto to the hydrogen

                        Check differential pressure. Control valve to stack will close automati-
                        cally to keep differential pressure.

15.8       PART 8: NORMAL SHUTDOWN
                      It is possible to shutdown the hydrogen system of one train without shut-
                      ting down the entire chlorine plant. The procedure for shutdown of hydro-
                      gen system of one train is mentioned in chapter 15.8.1.



15.8.1     NORMAL SHUTDOWN
                      The procedure for shutdown of the hydrogen system of one train is as fol-
                      lows:

                      • Ensure chlorine system of the corresponding train is ready for shut-
                        down.
                      • Shutdown the HCl Synthesis unit only if connected to corresponding
                        train, see chapter 17.8.
                      • Slowly reduce load of electrolysers.
                      • Route hydrogen to stack by closing PDV081311 (PDV082311) and
                        opening PDV0810312 (PDV0820312).
                      • This will stop the flow of hydrogen gas to EDC Plant.
                      • Shutdown electrolysers (see chapter 6.8).
                      • PDIC0810311 (PDIC0820311) is put in MANUAL and closed.
                        PDIC0810312 (PDIC0820312) is put on AUTO with a set point of
                        40 mbar.
                        This will maintain differential pressure across the cells and nitrogen
                        valve XV0810101 (XV0820101) opens when necessary to maintain
                        hydrogen header pressure with nitrogen.
                      If the hydrogen system can not be maintained under positive pressure
                      due to the nature of maintenance work, then hydrogen system must be
                      purged with nitrogen for a sufficient duration. Local measurement should
                      be made to confirm safe atmosphere.

                      After the maintenance jobs are over, the hydrogen section must again be
                      purged free of any air with nitrogen, and residual oxygen must be brought
                      down to < 0.5% v/v before plant start up.

15.9       PART 9: EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN

15.9.1     EMERGENCY SHUTDOWN OF UNIT
                      • In this case, the hydrogen is discharged into the atmosphere via the
                        hydrogen stack.
                      • Nitrogen purge at the electrolysers will start to flush the hydrogen sys-
                        tem via stack.
                      • Cell differential pressure will be maintained by action of PDV0810312
                        (PDV0820312) and PDV0810311 (PDV0820311) can be kept closed.
                      Caution: Care should be taken to maintain the section under positive
                               pressure during shutdown.

                      • In case of high pressure in the hydrogen system, an emergency sys-
                        tem depressurisation valve XV3410101 (XV3420101) has been pro-
                        vided, which will open when activated by interlock, venting hydrogen
                        gas into atmosphere through the hydrogen stack.

15.10.5.1.1Danger caused by hydrogen
                      Hydrogen is generated in the electrolysers.

                      Extremely flammable!



                      Observe following safety phrases:

                      Keep away from sources of ignition! Do not smoke!

                      Take precautionary measures against static discharges!

                      Keep container in a well-ventilated place!



15.10.5.2 Directions for Safe Operation and Inspection
                      Safety of Plant

                      The features of the electrolysis cell requires that the hydrogen pressure
                      is at all times maintained above the chlorine pressure. Furthermore for
                      safety reasons, the hydrogen pressure should be positive on each part of
                      the system. The following considerations have been taken regarding the
                      same.

                      • The differential pressure across the electolysers are controlled by
                        PDIC0810311/312 (PDIC0820311/312).
                      • In case of very high pressure in the hydrogen system, an emergency
                        depressurisation valve has been provided, which when activated
                        opens by interlock, venting hydrogen into atmosphere through the
                        stack.
                      • Very low pressures in hydrogen system is prevented by the hydrogen
                        under pressure protection interlock which opens nitrogen into the hy-
                        drogen system.
                      Also safety considerations have been taken to prevent the possibility of
                      hydrogen forming an explosive mixture.




                                                         Doc. ID-Code                          Rev.
Copyright 2005 Uhde GmbH

                      • There are no pockets in the hydrogen system.
                      • The hydrogen gas is vented to atmosphere via stack.
                      • Continuous nitrogen purging is done in the hydrogen stack.
                      • Automatic nitrogen purging of the hydrogen system during shutdown
                        via electrolyser headers.


                      In addition extensive instrumentation and interlocks have been provided
                      for continuous monitoring and safe operation of the system.

                      In the case of a fire at the hydrogen stack, a high temperature switch will
                      activate the steam flow by opening 41XV3410101 (41XV3420101). The
                      load of the train has to be reduced until the fire is extinguished.

                      Safety of Personnel and Safety Instructions

                      Prior to any maintenance work in the hydrogen system, the entire system
                      must be purged with nitrogen for sufficient time.

                      Should an accident occur in spite of careful operation of the plant, imme-
                      diate first aid is imperative.

16.2       PART 2: DESCRIPTION OF PROCESS

16.2.1     TECHNOLOGICAL PRINCIPLES
                      The system provides holding pits in process units / buildings, for water
                      collection of process areas, and lifting pumps to transfer the waste water
                      to the final treatment.

                      The pits are specifically located near product storage and pumping sta-
                      tions and near loading facilities.

                      The water streams are segregated depending on the nature for pollution;
                      two main subsystems are installed, the first one for collection of water po-
                      tentially polluted by caustic soda while the second one for water poten-
                      tially polluted by hydrochloric acid. This waters are pumped to the main
                      waste water pits.

                      The wash water is finally treated in the sludge tanks where sludge / under
                      flow of the clarifiers is solved with HCl, neutralised and send to battery
                      limits.

                      The surface waters from paved areas are those generated by rain, field
                      activity (wash-down operation, fire fighting equipment test) or during
                      emergency conditions. This water is mainly collected in a trench ring
                      around C/A Plant. In case of overflowing pits in the process areas the wa-
                      ter is also flowing into this trench.



16.2.2     UNIT DESCRIPTION
                      The waste water unit (common for both the trains) is designed to treat
                      process effluents from the plant and to send them after pH adjustment
                      and free chlorine removal to battery limits for disposal.

                      The waste water system consists of three Sludge Tanks 41V-36001A/B/C.
                      Normally one tank is on receiving mode, one is used for neutralisation
                      and pump out, and one as stand by. Bulk of waste water coming to the
                      tank are acidic waste water from the EDC/VCM plant. This HCl is used to
                      dissolve the sludge of the clarifier which is also joining into the sludge
                      tanks. The acidic waste water is neutralised by 18% NaOH in the tanks.



                                                          Doc. ID-Code                          Rev.

                      To facilitate homogenisation, the sludge tanks are equipped with agita-
                      tors.

                      Treated water is pumped to battery limit.

                      Facilities are provided to dose HCl, NaOH and 10% bisulphite solution, if
                      necessary. The flow of these chemicals (NaOH and Bisulphite) can be
                      adjusted depending on pH and redox values.

                      In addition to the tanks there are 2 Waste Water Pits 41X-36001 A/B. One
                      pit is used mainly for collecting the acidic waste water from the ion ex-
                      changer regeneration and the waste water from the trenches in the chlo-
                      rine plant. This waste water is continuously pumped into the sludge tank
                      on-line. For mixing the liquid in the pits the min. flow line of the water
                      waste pump 41P-36001A/B are equipped with a jet.

                      Waste water and surface waters from process buildings are collected in
                      pits / sumps from trenches in various process areas or send via trench di-
                      rectly to the waste water treatment. In case of pit overflow the water will
                      be collected in trench ring around the C/A Plant.

                      The sumps are equipped with air operated pit / sump pumps and deliver
                      the waste waters, if required, to the Waste Water Collecting Pits
                      41X-36001 A or B, each with a capacity of 220 m3. The pits can over flow
                      from one into the other.

Job Code:        PVC Arvand          Job Code:                        Owner Job Code: PVC Arvand
                                                                                        Page 885 of 967


                      The sludge tanks also receive the collected waste from the Waste Water
                      Collecting Pits 41X-36001 A or B, as well as the chemicals HCl, caustic
                      soda and sodium bisulphite for pH adjustment and dechlorination purpos-
                      es. The pH-adjustment is done automatically at the tank which is in neu-
                      tralisation mode. The filling of the sludge tanks is sequence controlled.

                      The treated waste water is leaving the sludge tanks via Waste Water
                      Pumps 41P-36002 A, B and/or C. Final pH adjustment is activated with
                      the addition of hydrochloric acid and/or caustic soda at the Jet Mixers
                      41J-26002 and 41J-36003.

                      Vent gases from the sludge tanks are routed through Vent Scrubber
                      41T-36001 to the atmosphere. 41T-36001 is a packed tower irrigated with
                      service/raw water to absorb Cl2 containing fumes, if required.



16.2.3     PROCESS CHEMISTRY
                      Waste waters and sludges from various units and with various pH values
                      are collected in the waste water treatment plant, and treated with caustic
                      soda and/or hydrochloric acid so that the pH value of the waste water
                      leaving for battery limits is between 5 and 9.

                      Sludge Treatment in Sludge Tank 41V-36001A-C

                      The clarifier underflow sludge is treated with 16% HCl. Thus, magnesium
                      hydroxide (Mg(OH)2) and calcium carbonate (CaCO3) reacts with HCl to
                      form magnesium chloride (MgCl2) and calcium chloride (CaCl2).

                             Mg(OH)2 + 2HCl → MgCl2 + 2H2O
                             Heat of reaction ∆ Hr (at 25 °C) = -23.83 kcal/mol

                             CaCO3 + 2HCl → CaCl2 + H2O + CO2+
                             Heat of reaction ∆ Hr (at 25 °C) = -19.34 kcal/mol

                      Any excess HCl in the effluent is neutralised with 18% NaOH and alkaline
                      the waste water from collecting pits in the sludge tanks. The carbon diox-
                      ide gas evolved is vented to atmosphere via vent scrubber 41T-36001 at
                      a safe location.
