16.3       PART 3: DESCRIPTION OF PLANT CONTROL

16.3.1     METHOD OF CONTROL
                      • The pH and Redox of the waste water leaving the Waste Water Col-
                        lecting Pits 41X-36001 A or B is measured. Chemical addition is done
                        manually.
                      • The sludge going to the Sludge Tanks 41V-36001 A, B or C is batch-
                        wise neutralised and pumped away. The Redox of the waste water is
                        measured in the re circulated by-pass stream. Bisulfite addition if re-
                        quired is done manually while caustic soda is added automatically.
                      • Final pH of the stream to battery limits is measured and caustic or hy-
                        drochloric acid is added automatically by means of Jet Mixers
                        41J-36002 and 41J-36003, if required.

                      Please also refer to ANNEX A5, METHOD OF CONTROL.



16.3.2     OPERATING CONDITIONS
                      The flow to and from the waste water treatment plant will vary considera-
                      bly. The flow depends on weather conditions, usage of water for wash-
                      downs, emergency situations (firewater), rainfall etc.

                      Please also refer to chapter 16.7, Normal Operation and chapter 16.2.2,
                      Unit Description.



16.3.3     PROCESS VARIABLES
                      • Flow of waste water to/from the waste water treatment plant
                      • pH of the various streams
                      • Addition of HCl
                      • Addition of NaOH 18%
                      • Addition of Sodium Bisulphite.
                      • Addition of caustic / bleaching lye.

16.6       PART 6: NORMAL START-UP

16.6.1     GENERAL PRECONDITION
                      The general preconditions require that vessels, piping, instrument and
                      electrical cabling was completed, vessels are clean, utilities are available
                      (water, electricity). Analysers have been tested and calibrated. FCS-se-
                      quence have been tested.

                      FCS monitors in control room are available and the chemical feed lines
                      are connected. Battery limit is ready to accept treated waste water. Com-
                      munication with control room is functioning from the field.



16.6.2     FINAL PREPARATION
                      Fill all sumps with water and check if air driven pumps can operate and
                      deliver to the waste water collecting pits.

                      Double check that valves are properly installed and jog pumps for direc-
                      tion of rotation.

                      Fill sludge tanks and waste water collecting pits with water to 30% level.



16.6.3     INITIAL START-UP
                      • Start pump 41P-36001 A or B according to vendor instruction.
                      • Slowly open discharge valve, observe flow through 41FIS3600104 and
                        analysers 3600101 and 3600102.
                      • Continue circulation back to sludge pit.
                      • Start pump 41P-36002 A, B or C.
                      • Circulate back to tank(s) 41V-36001 A/B/C.
                      • Start agitators 41MX36001 A/B/C.
                      Note:       Do not start agitators unless tank is filled.

                      • Leave discharge valve closed to battery limits.
                      • Start service water flow to vent scrubber 41T-36001.

                      • Open valve to waste water collecting pit, so that water can be circulat-
                        ed back to 41X-36001 A/B.
                      • Repeat procedure for all sludge tanks and all sludge tank pumps.
                      • Accept hydrochloric waste waters from B.L. (EDC/VCM).
                      • Accept 18% NaOH solution from caustic safety tank.
                      • Check pH control of 41AIC3600212/22/23 to achieve pH of 5-9.
                      • Accept sludge from the brine clarifiers 41R-04101 and/or 41R-04201.
                      • Follow up FCS-sequence for HCl / NaOH addition and switch over to
                        next sludge tank.
                      • Add constant flow of waste water from collecting pits to sludge tank.
                      • Add sodium bishulphite if high redox valve is measured at
                        41AIC3600211/21/31.
                      • Monitoring pH.
                      • When pH is within acceptable range send waste water to B.L.
                      • Start-up mixing jets 41J-36002 and 41J-36003.
                      • Check pH control of 41AIC3600301 and 41AIC3600302 to achieve pH
                        of 5-9.
                      • Final pH-check of waste water to B.L.

16.8       PART 8: NORMAL SHUTDOWN

16.8.1     NORMAL SHUTDOWN
                      The waste water treatment plant can stay in operation at all times.

                      One of the waste water collecting pits can be cleaned and/or maintained,
                      while the other is in operation.

                      One of the sludge tanks can be cleaned and/or maintained, while the oth-
                      ers are in operation.

                      For a complete shutdown follow the following procedure:

                      • Stop all agitators.
                      • Stop all pumps at sludge tanks and waste water collecting pits.



16.8.2     SHUTDOWN FOR LONGER PERIOD
                      A long term shutdown has to be scheduled well in advance. Removal of
                      sludge from the clarifiers is not possible during shutdown.

                      Therefore a stop of the brine system (salt addition) might be required, de-
                      pending on shutdown period (>12 hours).

                      Ensure low level of sludge in the clarifiers before shutdown.

                      Also the HCl from EDC / VCM Plant can not be neutralised. Co-ordination
                      with EDC / VCM Plant is required.

                      Follow procedures as outlined under chapter 16.8.1, Normal shutdown.

16.10.5.1.1Danger caused by caustic soda/catholyte
                      Caustic soda/catholyte is handled in this system.

                      Danger caused by caustic soda/catholyte!
                      Harmfull! Very corrosive. Causes severe burns. May cause serious
                      permanent eye damage. Very harmful by ingestion. Harmful by skin
                      contact or by inhalation of dust.

                      Observe following safety phrases:

                      • In case of contact with eyes, rinse immediately with plenty of water and
                        seek medical advice!
                      • Wear rubber or PVC gloves. Wear eye/face protection!
                      • In case of accident or if you feel unwell, seek medical advice immedi-
                        ately!

                      Hydrochloric acid causes burns and is irritating to eyes, respiratory

                      • In case of accident or if you feel unwell, seek medical advice immedi-
                        ately!

                      Avoid release to the environment!

                      Very toxic to aquatic organisms due to pH shift!

17.2       PART 2: DESCRIPTION OF PROCESS

17.2.1     TECHNOLOGICAL PRINCIPLES
                      The hydrochloric acid (HCl) synthesis system is designed for the produc-
                      tion of 124 t/d of HCl 100% as 32 +/- 1% w/w solution. The unit is designed
                      to operate up to turndown ratio of 20%, i.e. 24.8 t/d of HCl 100%.

                      This unit is common for both trains.

                      The HCl synthesis system consists of HCl Synthesis unit with scrubber
                      column and two HCl storage tanks with transfer pumps.

                      The HCl is used:
                      • in oxygen control in the chlorine gas by brine acidification
                      • during ion exchange regeneration
                      • in waste water treatment.
                      The unit will be run batchwise or at low load during the initial operation of
                      the plant - as the membranes age and current efficiency declines, more
                      acid is required to ensure low oxygen content in chlorine.

                      The hydrochloric acid solution is stored in two storage tanks
                      41TK-38001 A and B, with a combined volume of 250 m3.

17.2.2     UNIT DESCRIPTION
                      Hydrochloric acid (HCl) synthesis

                      PFD: 37001

                      P&ID: 37001 / 38001

                      The synthesis of hydrochloric acid (HCl) and absorption in demineralised
                      water to produce 32% HCl acid is accomplished in a HCl furnace (with an
                      integrated isothermal absorber) 41U-37050. The synthesis of HCl is per-
                      formed by the combustion of H2 gas and Cl2 gas. The heat generated dur-
                      ing combustion and during absorption of HCl in water, is removed by
                      cooling water.The HCl synthesis unit is operated at slight overpressure.

                      The furnace 41U-37050 consists of a combustion chamber, a long life
                      quartz / graphite burner 41B-37052 and an isothermal falling film absorb-
                      er 41B-37051, built as an integral part of the combustion chamber. The
                      combustion chamber and the absorber are incorporated in a steel shell
                      which acts as a cooling jacket.

                      This unit is protected with the bursting disc 41PS3700120 located at the
                      bottom of the unit. Rupture of the disc due to overpressure (set pressure
                      2 barg) initiates discharge of a small quantity of hydrogen chloride va-
                      pours at the bottom of the unit. These vapours are discharged to atmos-
                      phere at safe location. Liquid HCl must be drainded to trench.

                      An automatic monitoring and control cabinet is locally provided for the
                      safe operation of the unit. The monitoring unit is connected to the main
                      control room. Ignition of the burner is effected with the automatic ignition
                      system 41X-37055. An emergency shutdown system is provided to avoid
                      damage due to overheating or explosion.

                      The hydrogen gas is supplied to the HCl synthesis unit from the hydrogen
                      filter 41FT34102 or 41FT34202 at a temperature of approx. 55 °C. The
                      hydrogen supply should only be from one train. This is achieved by me-
                      chanical lock of the supply valves. Before entering the burner it passes
                      through the H2 flame arrester 41X-37052.

                      The dry chlorine gas is supplied from chlorine compressor 41U-22150
                      and/or 41U-22250 discharge. Based on chlorine gas input rate to the fur-
                      nace, monitored by FICR3700102, the hydrogen gas flow is adjusted by
                      the ratio controller 41FY3700114.

                      The ratio between hydrogen and chlorine depends of the chlorine capac-
                      ity.
                      For 124 tpd the stoechiometric hydrogen excess is 10%.
                      For 24,8 tpd the stoechiometric hydrogen excess is 30%.

                      If the ratio, controlled by 41FFY3700115, reaches HH or LL, the HCl Syn-
                      thesis Unit will be shut down. See also 14.2.3.2 regarding Hydrogen ex-
                      cess.

                      To obtain optimal system operation, the pressure of both gases should be
                      stable at the inlet of the burner.

                      The demineralised water used for the absorption of the HCl gas is fed to
                      the top of the scrubber column 41C-37051, from where it flows by gravity
                      via the packings to the falling film isothermal absorber 41B-37051 of the
                      synthesis unit. The quantity of demineralised water addition is controlled
                      through 41DIC3700101 according to the concentration of the hydrochlo-
                      ric acid produced. A constant recycle of 32% HCl from the storage tank
                      41TK38001 A/B via HCl pump 41P-38001 A/B to the scrubber column is
                      also required to achieve a shutdown ratio of 20%.

                      Based on chlorine gas input rate to the furnace, hydrogen gas flow and
                      demineralised water flow is adjusted proportionately by a ratio controller
                      41FY3700111.

                      The HCl gas produced in the furnace is absorbed in weak HCl from scrub-
                      ber column in a falling film isothermal absorber to produce hydrochloric
                      acid of max. 33% w/w concentration. The tail gas from the synthesis unit
                      is sent to the scrubber column 41C-37051, where the remaining HCl gas
                      is absorbed in the demineralised water.

                      The hydrochloric acid solution then flows to the storage tanks 41TK38001
                      A and B. The evolving heat is removed from the synthesis unit by cooling
                      water which fills the gap between the carbon block and the outside steel
                      shell of the synthesis unit.

                      The ignition of the burner is automatic. Plant air is used as oxygen source
                      for start-up.

                      Before start-up and after shutdown the control sequence of the unit initi-
                      ates the purge of chlorine and hydrogen lines to the burner and through
                      the synthesis unit with nitrogen, to avoid any potentially explosive gas
                      mixtures (see graph depicting safe and explosive zones for air-chlorine-
                      hydrogen mixtures).

                      Flame eyes monitor the flame, and upon loss of flame initiate the shut-
                      down sequence where the chlorine gas and hydrogen gas valves are au-
                      tomatically close and N2 purge of the unit starts.

                      The safety system also includes flame arrestors at H2 lines to main burner
                      and pilot burner (41X-37051, 41X-37052) to prevent the flame from en-
                      tering hydrogen and/or other process or utility lines.

                      The hydrochloric acid storage consists of two horizontal tanks
                      41TK38001 A and B which are connected in parallel, and two pumps,
                      41P-38001 A/B which are connected directly to storage tank 41TK38001
                      B.

                      Pumps 41P-38001 A or B distribute the hydrochloric acid solution to HCl
                      tanks 41V-06103 and 41V-06203 located at the brine ion exchangers
                      41FT06101A-D and 41FT06201 A-D, as well as to the HCl Dilution Ejec-
                      tor 41J-07003.

                      Necessity of the scrubber column

                      The synthesis unit implements co-current isothermal absorption, which
                      does not allow complete absorption of the HCl gas. Consequently, and
                      whatever the concentration and temperature of the hydrochloric acid pro-
                      duced, there is always a certain partial pressure Pg of HCl gas (greater
                      than the vapour pressure Ts of the solution), which cannot be discounted.

                      The aim of the scrubber column is to finish the absorption of the residual
                      HCl gas not absorbed in the synthesis unit. This quantity is small com-
                      pared to other known system on account of the higher thermal exchange
                      efficiency in the synthesis unit section.

                      The process employed is counter current adiabatic absorption, which al-
                      lows a very low HCl content to be obtained in the tail gases leaving the
                      scrubber column. If necessary, the last remaining traces of Cl2 and HCl
                      gas can be scrubbed in the bubble cap trays located above the packing.

                      The gases to be scrubbed coming from the synthesis unit enter the col-
                      umn via the bottom and the absorption water enters via the top. It is this
                      solution that goes on to finish the HCl gas absorption and produce acid at
                      the required concentration at the outlet of the HCl-Synthesis Unit.

17.2.3     PROCESS CHEMISTRY
                      The reaction of hydrogen and chlorine is highly exothermic. The equilib-
                      rium flame temperature for the adiabatic reaction of stoechiometric pro-
                      portions of H2 and Cl2 is 2490 °C. At this temperature, the equilibrium
                      mixture contains 4.2% free chlorine by volume. As the gases are cooled,
                      the free H2 and Cl2 combine rapidly, and at 200 °C, the concentration of
                      free chlorine is negligible.
                      With proper control of the feed gas mixture, a burner gas containing over
                      99% HCl can be obtained.

                      The absorption of hydrogen chloride in water is also highly exothermic.
                      The heat of solution at infinite dilution is -74.85 J/mol (17.89 kcal/mol).
                      The absorption of HCl in water is carried out isothermally, using a falling
                      film water-cooled absorber, and adiabatically, in a packed tower. The
                      weak acid from the scrubber column gets concentrated to max. 33% HCl
                      in the isothermal absorber.

                      The reaction is as follows:

                             ½ H2 + ½ Cl2 → HCl (aq.) + 166.7 KJ/mol.

                      For optimum combustion and to obtain low free chlorine content in acid,
                      the gases are burnt with about 10% excess flow of hydrogen gas. The
                      content of free chlorine in HCl is approx. 1 ppm w/w.

17.2.3.1   Temperature of the Flame
                      The temperature of the HCl flame is about 2490 °C when the chlorine and
                      hydrogen gases are almost pure, in other words at a Cl2 or H2 concentra-
                      tion close to 95% in volume (v/v):

                             Cl2(g) + H2(g) → 2 HCl(g) + 600 kcal/kg

                      If the chlorine gas contains inert gases, which is frequent, the tempera-
                      ture of the flame is lower.

                      However, if these inert gases are composed of oxygen, the oxygen com-
                      bines with the hydrogen and the very exothermal reaction results in a suf-
                      ficiently hot flame to maintain the H2 + Cl2 → HCl reaction, even for
                      mixtures with a low Cl2 content.

                             H2(g) + ½ O2(g) → H2O(g) + 3250 kcal/kg

                      In the case where the burner receives oxygen, the quantity of O2 must be
                      taken into account when calculating the hydrogen excess necessary. Ac-
                      cording to the reactions described above, oxygen consumes twice as
                      much hydrogen than chlorine does.

17.2.3.2   Hydrogen Excess
                      Necessity of the hydrogen excess

                      Chlorine and hydrogen combine in equal according to the reaction:

                             Cl2(g) + H2(g) → 2 HCl(g)

                      Tests have demonstrated that the burner of HCl Synthesis units ensures
                      complete combustion of Cl2 and H2 if the stoechiometric proportion is re-
                      spected. However, to deal with fluctuations in the flow rates of feed gas
                      and thus prevent explosions in installations due to the spontaneous reac-
                      tion of unburned Cl2 and H2, it is advised always to operate with an ex-
                      cess volume of one of the constituents. As it is not possible to discharge
                      chlorine into the atmosphere, and taking into account both that hydrogen
                      is not polluting and that wet chlorine tends to corrode graphite, the burner
                      is fed with a minimum stoechiometric hydrogen excess of 5%.

                      Uncorrected excess and stoechiometric excess

                      The minimum 5% hydrogen excess recommended is a stoechiometric ex-
                      cess based on the amount of pure combustible constituents (Cl2 and O2)
                      present in the chlorine and hydrogen gas. This excess is different from
                      the uncorrected excess (read by the ration controller) which is a simple
                      ration between the real global flow rates of chlorine and hydrogen.

                      The stoechiometric excess calculation takes into account two combustion
                      reactions:

                      Cl2(g) + H2(g) → 2 HCl(g)

                      H2(g) + ½ O2(g) → H2O(g)

                      Let Q0H2 be the flow rate of pure H2 in the hydrogen gas (Nm3/h or 0°C - 1atm)
                      Let Q0H2 be the flow rate of pure Cl2 in the hydrogen gas (Nm3/h or 0°C - 1atm)
                      Let Q0H2 be the flow rate of pure O2 in the hydrogen gas (Nm3/h or 0°C - 1atm)

                      The stoechiometric flow rate of pure H2 necessary to burn all the Cl2 and
                      O2 is Q0Cl2 + 2 x Q0O2.
                      If an excess of 5% above stoechiometric conditions is added, the flow rate
                      of pure H2 necessary becomes:

                      Q0H2 = 1.05 x (Q0Cl2 + 2 x Q0O2)

                      The total flow rate of hydrogen gas is therefore:

                      QT0H2 = Q0H2 / yH2 in Nm3/h (where y is the volumetric content of pure H2
                      in the hydrogen gas).

                      Therefore, the real hydrogen flow rate at temperature T (°K) and at pres-
                      sure P (Pa) is:

                      QTH2 = QT0H2 x T x P0 / (T0 x P) in m3/h

                      With T0 = 273.15°K and P0 = 101325 Pa (normal temperature and pres-
                      sure conditions).

                      Influence of the hydrogen excess

                      The hydrogen excess ensures the complete combustion of chlorine and
                      therefore the production of a very high quality acid. However, care should
                      be taken of minimise the excess necessary, primarily for safety and proc-
                      ess efficiency reasons:

                      • The excess, and therefore unburned, hydrogen represents a potential
                        danger of explosion in the system. The compact system greatly reduc-
                        es this risk.
                      • The presence of an inert gas (with regard to the absorption process)
                        such as hydrogen above the acid solution can reduce the efficiency of
                        HCl absorption. Indeed, the partial pressure or the HCl content in the
                        gas is reduced on account of the presence of H2; the absorption force
                        (partial HCl pressure in the gas / HCL solution vapour pressure) there-
                        fore drops. The presence of a too high hydrogen excess can lead to
                        the system overheating and reductions in capacity.

                                                                                     Page 915 of 967


                      It is therefore important to find a good compromise between the minimum
                      stoechiometric excess of 5% and the upper excess in order to produce a
                      quality acid while maintaining safety and efficient operation.

                      It is recommended to operate with a stoechiometric excess of

                      • 10% at 100% load (124 tpd HCl 100%) and
                      • 30% at 20% load (24,8 tpd HCl 100%).

17.2.3.3   Quality of the Acid Produced
                      Purity

                      If the feed gases and the absorption water do not contain impurities and
                      if the minimum stoechiometric hydrogen excess is respected, the quality
                      of the concentrated acid obtained is that of a hydrochloric acid marketed
                      as a strictly pure product, namely:

                      • Colour: clear
                      • Free chlorine content: < 1 ppm

                      Concentration

                      The HCl concentration normally sought is 32% but can vary between 30%
                      and 37%.

                      The production of more concentrated acid is subject to three essential
                      conditions:

                      • The temperature of the cooling water must be sufficiently low (<30°C).
                      • The temperature of the absorption water must be sufficiently low
                        (<30°C).
                      • The chlorine must not contain too many inert gases (hydrogen always
                        being practically pure so as not to reduce the absorption efficiency (ab-
                        sorption force).

17.2.3.4   Quality of the Tail Gases
                      The clean tail gases of the system are discharged into the atmosphere
                      and are composed of:

                      • The excess hydrogen gas not burned in the synthesis.
                      • Possible inert gases present in the feed gas (N2, CO2, CO, etc.).
                      • Steam (vaporised in the absorption process).
                      Minute quantities of chlorine and hydrogen chloride are also present. The
                      following maximum contents in stabilised operation are guaranteed:

                      • Cl2 < 1 ppm v/v
                      • HCl < 18 ppm v/v
                      These values corresponded to the anti-pollution standards generally in
                      force.

17.6       PART 6: NORMAL START-UP



17.6.1     GENERAL PRECONDITION
                      Prior to start-up of the HCl synthesis unit, the following prerequisites must
                      be fulfilled:

                      • Following systems are in operation:
                        Cooling water circulation, plant air, instrument air, demineralised wa-
                        ter, nitrogen system, waste gas dechlorination, H2 / process conden-
                        sate, hydrogen and chlorine system.
                      • Chlorine gas at compressor discharge and hydrogen gas at the outlet
                        of hydrogen filter are available to the HCl synthesis at normal operating
                        pressure. H2 feed only from one train possible.
                      • All condensate seals are filled with water.
                      • Ensure hydrogen lines are flushed with nitrogen until residual oxygen
                        concentration is < 0,5% v/v.
                      • All interlocks of above systems are ACTIVE.



17.6.2     FINAL PREPARATION
                      Establish and confirm manpower requirement and that communication
                      system between Central Control Room and field personnel is functioning.

17.6.3     INITIAL START-UP
                      • Start flow of cooling water to the isothermal absorber and scrubber
                        cooler.
                      • Start flow of nitrogen to HCl tank 41TK38001 A/B.
                      • Open main isolation valves on Cl2, H2 Air, N2 and demineralised water
                        lines to HCl unit.
                      • Ensure hydrogen lines are flushed with nitrogen unit oxygen concen-
                        tration is <0,5% v/v.
                      The following rules must be respected in order for start-up to take place
                      in optimal safety conditions:

                      • The hydrogen flow rate is sufficient to burn all the air at start-up (ex-
                        cess of hydrogen).
                      • The total hydrogen flow rate at the end of the start-up sequence must
                        be such that the H2 / Cl2 excess is ensured.
                      • The total H2 + Cl2 flow rate at the end of the start-up sequence must be
                        such that it corresponds to the minimum capacity of the burner.
                      • The quantity of HCl gas at the end of the start-up sequence must be
                        compatible with the flow rate of the absorption water (concentration of
                        the acid produced less than 30%).


17.6.3.1   Start-up Procedure
                      The start-up is carried out from the control room (remote).

                      During the remote start-up from the control room, it is recommended to
                      send an operator to the installation to „see with his own eyes“ that the pro-
                      cedure is taking place normally.

                      During the first start-up, the sequence is performed in manual (any auto-
                      matic control valves operating in manual). Once the sequence has been
                      understood and mastered by the operators, the complete sequence can
                      be carried out in automatic mode.

                      Start-up a synthesis unit always takes place in five major steps:

                      1. Nitrogen purge
                      2. Introduction of absorption water and recycled acid into the system
                      3. Introduction of air at the burner
                      4. Creation of the air / hydrogen flame at the burner
                      5. Air / chlorine substitution


                      The start-up sequence is considered finished when the air / chlorine sub-
                      stitution is completed (air valve closed) and the HCl flame is stable. Dur-
                      ing start-up, a diluted acid is produced.

                      1. Nitrogen purge
                         A purge must definitely be carried out before each start-up of the
                         installation (in manual or in automatic) and after each shut-down
                         (programmed or emergency).
                      2. Introduction of absorption water and recycled acid into the sys-
                         tem
                         During the start-up sequence and recycled acid into the system, the
                         quantity of water and recycled introduced into the system corre-
                         sponds to the minimum liquid flow rate in order to ensure wetting of
                         the blocks and the packing of the scrubber column.
                         The recycled acid flow rate is kept constant.
                      3. Introduction of air at the burner
                         The necessary air at start-up must be ensured that the four rules of
                         safety conditions are fulfilled (see chapter 17.6.3).
                         In practice, the minimum capacity of the burner minus 20% is used
                         at the starting point and has to correspond with the hydrogen flow
                         rate.
                      4. Creation of the air / hydrogen flame at the burner
                         Start-up the pilot burner by pressing the „Burner Start“ button will
                         constitute a air / hydrogen pilot flame into the interiors of the furn-
                         ance.
                         Once the flame is ignited the phase of substituting air by chlorine
                         begins.
                         During the first start-up, the air / hydrogen flame can be left to stabi-
                         lise for two minutes before introducing the chlorine.
                         The air / hydrogen flame has an orange colour.
                      5. Air / chlorine substitution
                         This phase consists in gradually replacing the air with chlorine at a
                         constant hydrogen flow rate. At the end of the sequence (air valve
                         closed) only the Cl2 / H2 flame remains. This flame is transparent
                         white.

                             The procedure remains the same whether the air or chlorine valves
                             are manual or automatic:
                             1.   Close the air valve partially
                             2.   Open the chlorine valve gently.

                             Repeat steps 1 and 2 several times until complete closure of the air
                             valve.

                                                            Doc. ID-Code                          Rev.
Copyright 2005 Uhde GmbH
                                                      8408205-CB-PR-MNL-0102                       02

                                                                                        Page 923 of 967


                             During this operation, the chlorine valve must be manipulated with
                             caution to prevent large arrivals of chlorine at the burner due for ex-
                             ample to the sudden and untimely opening of the valve (case of a
                             membrane stuck to the seat of the valve). The speed of closing the
                             air must always be faster than the speed of opening the chlorine. In-
                             deed, the chlorine and oxygen both consume hydrogen. Care should
                             therefore be taken to ensure that the quantity of chlorine is not too
                             high in order to avoid emanations.

                             The colour of the flame gradually changes from orange to transpar-
                             ent white. If the chlorine is injected too suddenly, a „cloud“ of white
                             mist appears around the flame and also stagnates in the inspection
                             portholes. If this mist does not dissipate after a few seconds, the air
                             flow rate must be reduced by closing the valve accordingly.

                             At the end of the sequence (air valve closed), the chlorine flow rate
                             must be compatible with the hydrogen excess set. If the flame
                             wavers („flickers“) in the burner, the capacity must be increased
                             quickly.

                             During the first start-up, the readings of the gas flow meters can be
                             erroneous on account of low flow rates or incorrect calibration. These
                             values must therefore be read with a critical eye and, more particu-
                             larly, these instruments must not be employed alone at this stage.
                             The changes in the colour of the flame should therefore also be ob-
                             served carefully to monitor the correct execution of the sequence.

                             During the air / chlorine substitution, the hydrogen excess must be
                             always ensured.

17.6.3.2   Increasing the capacity
                      During the first start-up
                      As for the first start-up sequence, increasing the capacity is carried out in
                      manual mode (any automatic control valves operating in manual).
                      Before increasing the capacity, the concentration of the acid must be ad-
                      justed to the required value. To do this, increase the hydrogen then the
                      chlorine flow rate at a constant absorption water flow rate until obtaining
                      the required concentration.

                      The phase of increasing the capacity can then begin.


                                                            Doc. ID-Code                          Rev.
Copyright 2005 Uhde GmbH
                                                      8408205-CB-PR-MNL-0102                       02
                                         PVC Arvand
                                       Operating Manual
                                                                       National Petrochemical comany

Job Code:        PVC Arvand        Job Code:                        Owner Job Code: PVC Arvand
                                                                                      Page 924 of 967


                      The procedure consists in increasing the flow rates always in the follow-
                      ing order:

                      a.) Absorption water     (FIC 3700111)
                      b.) Hydrogen             (FIC 3700104)
                      c.) Chlorine             (FIC 3700102)

                      Increasing the hydrogen flow before the chlorine flow is vital to ensure the
                      excess necessary for the complete combustion of chlorine.

                      To increase the load, proceed in increments of 5% of the nominal capac-
                      ity of the installation. After each increase, an interval of 10 minutes must
                      be respected to ensure stabilisation of the fluids at the required flow rates
                      (flame stable and white - no chlorine or HCl emissions at the chimney).
                      In the case of stabilisation problems, increase the waiting period between
                      each increment and reduce the load rise speed.

                      Increasing the capacity in a well-controlled system
                      Once the controllers are adjusted and also the operators mastered the re-
                      actions perfectly, increases in capacity can be carried out in automatic
                      mode and at a faster rate.

                      Before increasing the capacity, the concentration of the acid must
                      checked for the required value. If necessary increase the hydrogen then
                      the chlorine flow rate manually at a constant absorption water flow rate
                      until obtaining the required concentration. Change over back to automatic
                      mode is then possible.

                      In automatic operation, increasing the capacity is achieved by increasing
                      the chlorine flow rate (41FICR3700102). The increase in the hydrogen
                      41FIC3700104 and then the absorption water 41FIC3700111 flow rates
                      is done automatically in cascade. The control programme ensures a hy-
                      drogen excess even when increasing the chlorine flow. The master /
                      slave system between Cl2 and H2 is therefore respected for a higher level
                      of operating safety.

17.7       PART 7: NORMAL OPERATION

17.7.1     NORMAL ROUTINE OF OPERATION
                      • Monitor FCS and local instrumentation.
                      • Record abnormal observations.
                      • Regular sampling according to sample schedule (refer to Analytical
                        Manual).
                      • Routine operating checks.

                      When a units is operating in stabilised operation, the operators must
                      monitor the following variables at regular intervals:

                      • Hydrogen flow rate
                      • Chlorine flow rate
                      • Absorption water flow rate
                      • Recycled acid flow rate
                      • Temperature of the tail tower
                      • Cooling water flow rates
                      • Stability of the flame
                      • Concentration and temperature of the acid produced
                      • Quality of the acid (free chlorine measurement about every 2 hours)
                      • Vents at the chimney (no HCl mist or smell of chlorine)
                      • Other safety aspects (safety disk / overflow of the tank / pressure of the
                        purging nitrogen, etc.).
                      • Some of these checks are carried out from the control room, others on
                        site while doing the rounds.

17.7.3     PERFORMANCE CHECK
                      During normal operation all the process parameters must be monitored
                      and/or recorded/documented.

                      In addition to the above FCS observations, following field activities should
                      be carried out:

                      • Check discharge pressure of HCl transfer pumps through PI3800101 /
                        3800102.
                      • In case of high level in waste collection pit for HCl synthesis are, start
                        the waste water pump 41P-38002 to transfer waste to the main waste
                        water collecting pit for treatment.
                      • Check the flame in the HCl furnace through the sight glass. Inspection
                        during start-up is not advised due to the increased risk during ignition.
                        Shortly after ignition the flame has to be checked.
                      • Samples are to be taken for analysis from the various sample points
                        (see Analytical Manual) and the results should be checked and
                        documented.

17.7.4     REDUCED CAPACITY OPERATION
                      The HCl synthesis unit has been designed to operate at a maximum
                      100% load to a minimum turn down ratio of 20%. This can be achieved
                      by changing set point of Cl2 flow to the desired production. H2 will change
                      in ratio accordingly. The surplus of hydrogen at turn down ratio < 30% is
                      up to 30%. Demineralised water flow will change according to product
                      density.

                      No special operational procedure are to be followed for reduced capacity
                      operations, since the process parameters are automatically controlled for
                      the load conditions.

17.8       PART 8: NORMAL SHUTDOWN

17.8.1     NORMAL SHUTDOWN
                      A shutdown of the HCl synthesis unit may be taken for the following rea-
                      sons:

                      • Maintenance work in HCl synthesis unit independent of electrolyser
                        shutdown.
                      • Load reduction of chlorine plant (if required)
                      • Shutdown of the entire chlorine plant.
                      • Switch over of H2 supply from one train to the other train.
                      • High level in HCl Tanks 41TK38001A/B.


                      Prerequisites for normal shutdown

                      • Ensure availability of nitrogen.
                      • Availability of sufficient quantity of HCl in HCl tank 41TK38001 A/B for
                        internal consumption.


                      Normal shutdown procedure

                      • Gradually reduce the load on HCl Synthesis unit to 30% of full load, by
                        reducing the flow rate of chlorine gas to the unit.
                      • Now press one of the hand switches 41HS3700102 to 05, which will
                        trip the HCl synthesis unit by the action of the interlock.
                      • All actions will take as described under emergency shutdown of HCl
                        synthesis unit, chapter 17.9.
                      • Isolate chlorine and hydrogen line to the synthesis through manual iso-
                        lation valves.

                      In case maintenance work is to be carried out in the HCl synthesis unit:

                      • Isolate all lines connected to the HCl synthesis unit through manual
                        isolation valves.
                      • Then flush the entire chlorine line with nitrogen or dry air, free of chlo-
                        rine.
                      • Similarly flush the hydrogen line with nitrogen.
                      • The cooling water supply to the HCl furnace may be stopped.

17.10.5    SAFETY INSTRUCTIONS, SPECIFIC INSTRUCTIONS PER UNIT
                      Safety of Plant and Personnel

                      The following safety measures have been incorporated in the HCl synthe-
                      sis unit

                      • Extensive control and interlocks have been provided in the HCl synthe-
                        sis section to ensure a safe start up and operation of the unit.
                      • The unit is operated at slight overpressure. This eliminates the possi-
                        bility of air intake into the system from the atmosphere, which may oth-
                        erwise increase the risk of explosion.
                      • The unit is protected with a bursting disc located at the bottom of the
                        unit. Rupture of the disc due to overpressure initiates discharge of a
                        small quantity to hydrogen chloride vapour to a safe location.
                      • For emergency shutdown of the HCl synthesis unit hand switches
                        41HS3700102 to 05, has been provided.
                      • The system has been provided with fire protection. In case the temper-
                        ature at outlet of the scrubber column is very high, the nitrogen purge
                        to the scrubber column is activated to extinguish the flame. Manual
                        shut-down of unit might be required.



17.10.5.1 Handling Hazardous Materials
                      The hazardous chemicals handled in the HCl synthesis and storage unit
                      are chlorine, hydrogen and hydrochloric acid. Should an accident occur
                      inspite of careful operation of the plant, immediate first aid is imperative.

                      For details of precautionary measures in case of accident involved with
                      handling these chemicals, please refer to chapter 1.8, Safety Instructions.

17.10.5.1.1Danger caused by chlorine
                      The hazardous chemical handled in this system of the plant is chlorine.

                      Toxic! Danger caused by chlorine!
                      Toxic by inhalation, ingestion and through skin contact. Inhalation can
                      cause serious lung damage and may be fatal. 1000ppm (0.1%) is likely to
                      be fatal after a few deep breaths, and half that concentration fatal after a
                      few minutes. May irritate or burn skin.
                      Irritating to eyes, respiratory system and skin.

                      Observe following safety phrases:

                      • In case of accident or if you feel unwell, seek medical advice immedi-
                        ately!
                      • Wear protective gloves. Wear protective glasses!


                      Avoid release to the environment!

                      Very toxic to aquatic organisms!



17.10.5.1.2Danger caused by hydrogen
                      Hydrogen is generated in the electrolysers.

                      Extremely flammable!



                      Observe following safety phrases:

                      Keep away from sources of ignition! Do not smoke!

                      Take precautionary measures against static discharges!

                      Keep container in a well-ventilated place!

17.10.5.1.3Danger caused by hydrochloric acid
                      Hydrochloric acid is handled in this system.

                      Danger caused by hydrochloric acid!
                      Toxic by inhalation and in contact with skin and if swallowed! Cor-
                      rosive!
                      Hydrochloric acid causes burns and is irritating to eyes, respiratory
                      system and skin.

                      Observe following safety phrases:

                      • In case of contact with eyes, rinse immediately with plenty of water and
                        seek medical advice!
                      • Wear gloves. Wear eye/face protection! Wear protective clothing! Pro-
                        vide for effective ventilation!
                      • In case of accident or if you feel unwell, seek medical advice immedi-
                        ately!

                      Avoid release to the environment!

                      Very toxic to aquatic organisms due to pH shift!
